infoSections.description: Product info section.  + Pass `infoSection.uniqueName`, `infoSection.title`, and `infoSection.description` to add a new info section while creating a product. + Pass an existing info section's `id` or `uniqueName` to assign that info section to the product.

uniqueName.description: Info section unique name. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

plainDescription.description: Info section description in HTML.  When provided on create/update, this string must be a valid HTML. It will then be converted to rich content. `plainDescription` is ignored when value is also passed to the `description` field. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION_PLAIN_DESCRIPTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

ribbon.description: Primary product ribbon displayed on the product. Use `additionalRibbons` to assign further ribbons beyond the primary one.  + Pass `ribbon.name` to add a new ribbon while creating a product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.

additionalRibbons.description: Additional [ribbons](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/ribbons-v3/introduction.md) displayed on the product, beyond the primary `ribbon`.  Use this field to highlight multiple product attributes at once, for example combining a "New" ribbon with a "Sale" ribbon. Both the primary and additional ribbons are rendered on product cards and on the product page. Ribbons appear in the same order as this list.  Each entry follows the same assignment rules as `ribbon`: + Pass `additionalRibbons.name` to add a new ribbon while creating or updating the product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.  A ribbon can be assigned to a product at most once: the same ribbon can't appear more than once in `additionalRibbons`, and a ribbon set as `ribbon` can't also appear in `additionalRibbons`.  Supports up to 4 additional ribbons per product.

mainCategoryId.description: The GUID of the product's primary direct category, which defines the product's breadcrumbs path. For example, if the product's main category is "T-Shirts" (which is a subcategory of "Clothing"), the breadcrumbs path will be "Clothing > T-Shirts".

When passing `productType: PHYSICAL`, you must also pass `physicalProperties`. When passing `productType: DIGITAL`, attach a file by uploading it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and passing the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id` in each variant. A digital product created without a file cannot be sold. When passing `productType: FIXED_BUNDLE`, you must also pass `fixedBundleProperties`.

A variant without `digitalFile` set cannot be sold.

Each variant can have a different digital file, allowing you to offer different content per variant.  `digitalFile.id` is a Media Manager file GUID — upload the file via [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and use the `file.id` from the upload response.

product.description: A product in a Wix Stores catalog.  Products can be physical goods that require shipping, or digital content that customers download. Each product has at least one variant, which represents a specific purchasable version with its own pricing, SKU, and inventory. Products with options (like size or color) have multiple variants. Default: `true`  > **Note:** For products without options, updating this field automatically > updates the default variant's visibility to match. > For products with options, the product and variant visibility values are independent.

visibleInPos.description: Whether the product is visible in POS (point of sale).  Default: `true` > **Note:** Always `false` for `productType: DIGITAL`.

media.description: Product media items. For a detailed explanation of product media, see [About Product Media](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/products-v3/about-product-media.md).

itemsInfo.description: All media items. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"MEDIA_ITEMS_INFO"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

items.description: All media items associated with this product.  The first item in the array is automatically set as the product's main media.

id.description: Set media by GUID of an existing file in Wix Media Manager.

url.description: Set media using an external media URL.

displayName.description: Media display name.  Overrides the default media name. Can be passed only when the media is set by a URL in this item's `url` field.

thumbnail.description: Media thumbnail. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"THUMBNAIL"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

taxGroupId.description: [Tax group GUID](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/e-commerce/extensions/tax/tax-groups/introduction.md). Used to apply specific tax rates to products.

options.description: Product options, such as "Size" or "Color". Options define the ways a product can vary.  When you provide options, you must also provide the corresponding variants. Each variant must have exactly one choice for each option. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Options are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Pass an existing customization's GUID to reuse it, or define options inline and new customization entities are created automatically.

choices.description: List of available choices for the option.

id.description: GUID of a customization with `customizationType: PRODUCT_OPTION`.

modifiers.description: Product modifiers. Collect additional information from customers without creating variants.  Unlike options, modifiers don't affect inventory or create additional variants. Use them for things like gift messages or engraving text. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Modifiers are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Pass an existing customization's GUID to reuse it, or define modifiers inline and new customization entities are created automatically.

defaultAddedPrice.description: Default amount to be added to the product's price.

title.description: Title of the text to be input by the customer.

id.description: GUID of a customization with `customizationType: MODIFIER`.

mandatory.description: Whether customer input is required for this modifier.  If not set, the modifier's `defaultMandatory` value applies.

brand.description: Product [brand](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/brands-v3/introduction.md).  + Pass `brand.name` to add a new brand while creating a product. + Pass an existing brand's `id` to assign that brand to the product.

infoSections.description: Product [info section](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/info-sections-v3/introduction.md).  + Pass `infoSection.uniqueName`, `infoSection.title`, and `infoSection.description` to add a new info section while creating a product. + Pass an existing info section's `id` or `uniqueName` to assign that info section to the product.

uniqueName.description: Info section unique name. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

plainDescription.description: Info section description in HTML.  When provided on create/update, this string must be a valid HTML. It will then be converted to rich content. `plainDescription` is ignored when value is also passed to the `description` field. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION_PLAIN_DESCRIPTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

ribbon.description: Primary [ribbon](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/ribbons-v3/introduction.md) displayed on the product. Use `additionalRibbons` to assign further ribbons beyond the primary one.  + Pass `ribbon.name` to add a new ribbon while creating a product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.

mainCategoryId.description: The GUID of the product's primary direct [category](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/categories/introduction.md), which defines the product's breadcrumbs path. For example, if the product's main category is "T-Shirts" (which is a subcategory of "Clothing"), the breadcrumbs path will be "Clothing > T-Shirts".

productType.description: Product type: `PHYSICAL` for tangible goods that require shipping, `DIGITAL` for downloadable content, or `FIXED_BUNDLE` for a bundle whose products the merchant selects.  When passing `productType: PHYSICAL`, you must also pass `physicalProperties`. When passing `productType: DIGITAL`, attach a file by uploading it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and passing the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id` in each variant. A digital product created without a file cannot be sold. When passing `productType: FIXED_BUNDLE`, you must also pass `fixedBundleProperties`.

variantsInfo.description: Product variants. Each variant represents a specific purchasable version of a product defined by option choices.  Each variant must reference all product options via its `choices` array, using `optionChoiceNames` in requests. You must explicitly provide each variant when creating products with options.  For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).

physicalProperties.description: Physical properties. Must be passed when `productType: PHYSICAL`

weight.description: Variant shipping weight. product.physicalProperties.shipping_weight_range values are taken from here.

pricePerUnit.description: Price per unit info, in order to show price per unit on the product page. For example if one sells cheese and defines 100g here then we know that buying this variant buyer receives 100g of cheese. But on product page price will be displayed for units defined on product level. See `pricePerUnit.value` to understand how it's calculated.

productDimensions.description: Product dimensions (length, width, height of the physical product).

packageDimensions.description: Package dimensions (length, width, height of the shipping package).

digitalProperties.description: Digital properties. Must be passed when `productType: DIGITAL`.  To attach a file, upload it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and pass the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id`. A variant without `digitalFile` set cannot be sold.

digitalFile.description: Digital file which will be downloaded by the buyer after successful purchase. Each variant can have a different digital file, allowing you to offer different content per variant.  `digitalFile.id` is a Media Manager file GUID — upload the file via [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and use the `file.id` from the upload response.

visible.description: Whether the variant is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`  > **Note:** For products without options, updating this field automatically > updates the product's visibility to match. > For products with options, the product and variant visibility values are independent.

choices.description: List of choices that define this variant. Each variant must have exactly one choice for each product option.  Use `optionChoiceNames` in all requests where this field is required. For products without options, this array is empty, representing a single "default variant".  For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).

actualPrice.description: Variant's current selling price. Must be greater than or equal to 0.

compareAtPrice.description: Original price before any discount, shown with a strikethrough in the UI of Wix sites. Only set this if a discount applies. When set, it should be higher than `actualPrice` to reflect savings.

revenueDetails.description: Variant revenue details.  > **Note:** Returned only when the following conditions are met: > + You pass `"MERCHANT_DATA"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests. > + Your app has the required `SCOPE.STORES.PRODUCT_READ_ADMIN` permission scope.

purchaseEligibility.description: Purchase eligibility settings for the product.

userCriteria.description: Criteria a buyer must meet to purchase the product.

additionalRibbons.description: Additional [ribbons](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/ribbons-v3/introduction.md) displayed on the product, beyond the primary `ribbon`.  Use this field to highlight multiple product attributes at once, for example combining a "New" ribbon with a "Sale" ribbon. Both the primary and additional ribbons are rendered on product cards and on the product page.  Each entry follows the same assignment rules as `ribbon`: + Pass `additionalRibbons.name` to add a new ribbon while creating or updating the product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.  A ribbon can be assigned to a product at most once: the same ribbon can't appear more than once in `additionalRibbons`, and a ribbon set as `ribbon` can't also appear in `additionalRibbons`.  Supports up to 4 additional ribbons per product.

extendedFields.description: Custom extended fields for the product object.  [Extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/schema-plugins/about-schema-plugin-extensions.md) must be configured in the app dashboard before they can be accessed with API calls.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions.  Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md).

tags.description: Tags assigned to the product, organized into public and private tags.

privateTags.description: Tags that require an additional permission in order to access them, normally not given to site members or visitors.

publicTags.description: Tags that are exposed to anyone who has access to the labeled entity itself, including site members and visitors.

subscriptionDetails.description: Product subscriptions.  Subscription discounts are defined at the product level but apply to each variant's `actualPrice`. This means the final subscription price varies per variant based on the variant's base price.

autoRenewal.description: Whether subscription is renewed automatically at the end of each period. Cannot be `false`, instead set `billingCycles`.

billingCycles.description: Number of billing cycles before subscription ends.

visible.description: Whether the subscription is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`

frequency.description: Frequency of recurring payment. For example, if `frequency: MONTH` and `billingCycles: 6`; payment will be made monthly for 6 months.

interval.description: Interval of recurring payment. Default: `1`. For example, if `frequency: MONTH`, `billingCycles: 3` and `interval: 2`; payment will be made every 2 months for a total of 6 months.

discount.description: Discount info (optional). For example, a $20 discount would be `amount: 20`, `type: AMOUNT`.

amountOff.description: Fixed amount subtracted from the variant price when calculating subscription prices.

percentOff.description: Percentage subtracted from the variant price when calculating subscription prices.

allowOneTimePurchases.description: Whether to allow one-time purchases in addition to subscription-based purchases.  Default: `false`

actions.name: query_products
actions.description: Query products. Retrieves a list of up to 100 products, given the provided filtering, sorting, and cursor paging. Pass supported values to the `fields` array in the request to include those fields in the response.  To learn about working with _Query_ endpoints, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md), and [Sorting and Paging](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-sorting-and-paging.md). limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

selectItemsBy.description: When `field_name` is a property of repeated field that is marked as `MATCH_ITEMS` and sort should be done by a specific element from a collection, filter can/should be provided to ensure correct sort value is picked.  If multiple filters are provided, they are combined with AND operator.  Example: Given we have document like {"id": "1", "nestedField": [{"price": 10, "region": "EU"}, {"price": 20, "region": "US"}]} and `nestedField` is marked as `MATCH_ITEMS`, to ensure that sorting is done by correct region, filter should be { fieldName: "nestedField.price", "select_items_by": [{"nestedField.region": "US"}] }

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

selectItemsBy.description: When `field_name` is a property of repeated field that is marked as `MATCH_ITEMS` and sort should be done by a specific element from a collection, filter can/should be provided to ensure correct sort value is picked.  If multiple filters are provided, they are combined with AND operator. aggregations.description: Logical groupings of data into facets, with summaries for each facet. For example, use aggregations to allow site visitors to narrow down their search results by selecting specific categories.

value.description: A value aggregation calculates metrics such as count for specific fields within a dataset, providing insights into the overall distribution and key statistics of those values. For example, use a value aggregation to get the number (count) of products for each price listed in the store.

includeOptions.description: Options for including missing values in results.

addToBucket.description: Specify a custom name for the bucket containing the missing values. Defaults are `"N/A"` for strings, `0` for integers, and `false` for booleans.

sortType.description: Sort type.

sortDirection.description: Sort direction.

limit.description: Number of aggregation results to return. Min: `1` Max: `250` Default: `10`

missingValues.description: Whether to include or exclude missing values in the aggregation results. Default: `EXCLUDE`.

range.description: A range aggregation calculates the count of the values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within the range of each bucket you define. For example, use a range aggregation to compare the number of reservations made for parties of 4 or less to the number of reservations made for parties with 5 or more.

buckets.description: List of range buckets. During aggregation each entity is placed in the first bucket its value falls into, based on the provided range bounds.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the range. Required if `to` is not provided.

to.description: Exclusive upper bound of the range. Required if `from` is not provided.

scalar.description: A scalar aggregation calculates a single numerical value from a dataset, summarizing the dataset into one key metric: `COUNT_DISTINCT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, or `MAX`.

type.description: Operator type for the scalar aggregation.

dateHistogram.description: A date histogram calculates the count of time values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within each time interval you define (hour, day, week, etc.) For example, use a date histogram to find how many reservations have been made at a restaurant each week.

interval.description: Interval for date histogram aggregation.

nested.description: A nested aggregation is applied within the results of another aggregation. Rather than aggregating directly on the primary dataset, first group data using one aggregation and then apply another aggregation within each group. It allows for more complex analyses where you can summarize data at different levels of detail or hierarchy. For example, to get the number of products that are in stock and out of stock for each price listed, first perform a value aggregation on `discountedPriceNumeric`, and a second value aggregation on `inStock`.

nestedAggregations.description: Flattened list of aggregations, where each next aggregation is nested within previous one.

value.description: A value aggregation calculates the distribution of a specific field's values within a dataset, providing insights into the overall distribution and key statistics of those values. For example, use a value aggregation to get the number (count) of orders for each order status.

range.description: A range aggregation calculates the count of the values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within the range of each bucket you define. For example, use a range aggregation to compare the number of reservations made for parties of 4 or less to the number of reservations made for parties with 5 or more. If ranges overlap, a record that fits more than one range will only be counted in the first range that matches the criteria.

scalar.description: A scalar aggregation calculates a single numerical value from a dataset, summarizing the dataset into one key metric: `COUNT_DISTINCT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, or `MAX`.

dateHistogram.description: A date histogram calculates the count of time values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within each time interval you define (hour, day, week, etc.). For example, use a date histogram to determine how many reservations have been made at a restaurant each week. If ranges overlap, a record that fits more than one range will only be counted in the first range that matches the criteria.

name.description: Unique, caller-defined aggregation name, returned in `aggregations.results`.

type.description: Type of aggregation to perform. The matching aggregation field must be passed.

fieldPath.description: Field to aggregate by. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

type.description: Type of aggregation to perform. Must align with the corresponding aggregation field.

fieldPath.description: Field to aggregate by. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

search.description: Free text to match in searchable fields.

mode.description: Defines how separate search terms in `expression` are combined

fields.description: Fields to search in. If the array is empty, all searchable fields are searched. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

fuzzy.description: Whether to enable the search function to use an algorithm to automatically find results that are close to the search expression, such as typos and declensions.

timeZone.description: Time zone to adjust date-time-based filters and aggregations, in ISO 8601 (including offsets) or IANA time zone database (including time zone GUIDs) format. Applies to all relevant filters and aggregations, unless overridden by providing timestamps including time zone. For example, "2023-12-20T10:52:34.795Z".

actions.name: count_products
actions.description: Count products. Counts the number of products that match the provided filtering.

filter.description: Filter object.

returnNonVisibleProducts.description: Whether to return non-visible products (`visible:false`). Your app must have the 'Product v3 read admin' (`SCOPE.STORES.PRODUCT_READ_ADMIN`) permission scope.  Default: `false`

mode.description: Defines how separate search terms in `expression` are combined

fields.description: Fields to search in. If the array is empty, all searchable fields are searched. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

fuzzy.description: Whether to enable the search function to use an algorithm to automatically find results that are close to the search expression, such as typos and declensions.

actions.name: bulk_create_products
actions.description: Bulk create products. Creates up to 100 products.  >**Note:** > The following limits apply to the total number of creatable entities in a single request. > > + `options`: 100 > + `modifiers`: 100 > + `infoSections`: 100 > + `variantsInfo.variants`: 1000 > > For example, you can create 10 products with up to 10 options for each product (10 x 10 = 100), or 1 product with 100 options. > Alternatively, you can create 100 products with up to 10 variants in each (100 x 10 = 1000), or 1 product with 1000 variants.

fields.description: Fields to include in the response.

physicalProperties.description: Physical properties.  Required when `productType: PHYSICAL`.

pricePerUnit.description: Price per unit settings. > **Note:** Use this field only when relevant. For example, for products that are sold by weight, volume, or length.

quantity.description: Quantity. For example, to define price per per 100 grams, set this field to `100`.

measurementUnit.description: Measurement unit. For example, to define price per 100 grams, set this field to "G".

slug.description: Product slug. A URL-friendly identifier used in the product page address.  If not provided, the slug is autogenerated based on the product name.

description.description: Product description using rich content. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"DESCRIPTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests. See.md Ricos document reference

nodes.description: Node objects representing a rich content document.

text.description: The text to display on the button.

codeBlockData.description: Data for a code block node.

textStyle.description: Styling for the code block's text.

styles.description: Visual styling for the divider lines.

src.description: The source for the file's data.

options.description: Options for defining the gallery's appearance.

disableExpand.description: Sets whether the gallery's expand button is disabled. Defaults to `false`.

disableDownload.description: Sets whether the gallery's download button is disabled. Defaults to `false`.

original.description: The source of the full size GIF.

downsized.description: The source of the downsized GIF.

gifType.description: Type of GIF (Sticker or NORMAL). Defaults to `NORMAL`.

renderedLevel.description: Rendered heading level for SEO/accessibility, overrides the HTML tag when set.

htmlData.description: Data for an embedded HTML node.

url.description: The URL for the HTML code for the node.

html.description: The HTML code for the node.

widgetId.description: The WixelWidget GUID for AI_WIDGET source nodes.

containerData.description: Styling for the HTML node's container. Height property is irrelevant for HTML embeds when autoHeight is set to `true`.

source.description: The type of HTML code.

autoHeight.description: If container height is aligned with its content height. Defaults to `true`.

link.description: Link details for images that are links.

disableExpand.description: Sets whether the image expands to full screen when clicked. Defaults to `false`.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

taxGroupId.description: [Tax group GUID](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/e-commerce/extensions/tax/tax-groups/introduction.md). Used to apply specific tax rates to products.

options.description: Product options, such as "Size" or "Color". Options define the ways a product can vary.  When you provide options, you must also provide the corresponding variants. Each variant must have exactly one choice for each option. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Options are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Pass an existing customization's GUID to reuse it, or define options inline and new customization entities are created automatically.

Use them for things like gift messages or engraving text. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Modifiers are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Use `additionalRibbons` to assign further ribbons beyond the primary one.  + Pass `ribbon.name` to add a new ribbon while creating a product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.

mainCategoryId.description: The GUID of the product's primary direct [category](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/categories/introduction.md), which defines the product's breadcrumbs path. For example, if the product's main category is "T-Shirts" (which is a subcategory of "Clothing"), the breadcrumbs path will be "Clothing > T-Shirts".

productType.description: Product type: `PHYSICAL` for tangible goods that require shipping, `DIGITAL` for downloadable content, or `FIXED_BUNDLE` for a bundle whose products the merchant selects. When passing `productType: DIGITAL`, attach a file by uploading it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and passing the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id` in each variant. A digital product created without a file cannot be sold. When passing `productType: FIXED_BUNDLE`, you must also pass `fixedBundleProperties`.

For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).

But on product page price will be displayed for units defined on product level. See `pricePerUnit.value` to understand how it's calculated.

A variant without `digitalFile` set cannot be sold.

Each variant can have a different digital file, allowing you to offer different content per variant.  `digitalFile.id` is a Media Manager file GUID — upload the file via [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and use the `file.id` from the upload response.

additionalRibbons.description: Additional [ribbons](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/ribbons-v3/introduction.md) displayed on the product, beyond the primary `ribbon`.  Use this field to highlight multiple product attributes at once, for example combining a "New" ribbon with a "Sale" ribbon. Both the primary and additional ribbons are rendered on product cards and on the product page.  Each entry follows the same assignment rules as `ribbon`: + Pass `additionalRibbons.name` to add a new ribbon while creating or updating the product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.  A ribbon can be assigned to a product at most once: the same ribbon can't appear more than once in `additionalRibbons`, and a ribbon set as `ribbon` can't also appear in `additionalRibbons`. Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

taxGroupId.description: [Tax group GUID](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/e-commerce/extensions/tax/tax-groups/introduction.md). Used to apply specific tax rates to products.

options.description: Product options, such as "Size" or "Color". Options define the ways a product can vary.  When you provide options, you must also provide the corresponding variants. Each variant must have exactly one choice for each option. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Options are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Pass an existing customization's GUID to reuse it, or define options inline and new customization entities are created automatically.

choices.description: List of available choices for the option.

id.description: GUID of a customization with `customizationType: PRODUCT_OPTION`.

modifiers.description: Product modifiers. Collect additional information from customers without creating variants.  Unlike options, modifiers don't affect inventory or create additional variants. Use them for things like gift messages or engraving text. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Modifiers are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Pass an existing customization's GUID to reuse it, or define modifiers inline and new customization entities are created automatically.

defaultAddedPrice.description: Default amount to be added to the product's price.

title.description: Title of the text to be input by the customer.

id.description: GUID of a customization with `customizationType: MODIFIER`.

mandatory.description: Whether customer input is required for this modifier.  If not set, the modifier's `defaultMandatory` value applies.

brand.description: Product [brand](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/brands-v3/introduction.md).  + Pass `brand.name` to add a new brand while creating a product. + Pass an existing brand's `id` to assign that brand to the product.

infoSections.description: Product [info section](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/info-sections-v3/introduction.md).  + Pass `infoSection.uniqueName`, `infoSection.title`, and `infoSection.description` to add a new info section while creating a product. + Pass an existing info section's `id` or `uniqueName` to assign that info section to the product.

uniqueName.description: Info section unique name. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

plainDescription.description: Info section description in HTML.  When provided on create/update, this string must be a valid HTML. It will then be converted to rich content. `plainDescription` is ignored when value is also passed to the `description` field. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION_PLAIN_DESCRIPTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

ribbon.description: Primary [ribbon](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/ribbons-v3/introduction.md) displayed on the product. Use `additionalRibbons` to assign further ribbons beyond the primary one.  + Pass `ribbon.name` to add a new ribbon while creating a product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.

mainCategoryId.description: The GUID of the product's primary direct [category](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/categories/introduction.md), which defines the product's breadcrumbs path. For example, if the product's main category is "T-Shirts" (which is a subcategory of "Clothing"), the breadcrumbs path will be "Clothing > T-Shirts".

productType.description: Product type: `PHYSICAL` for tangible goods that require shipping, `DIGITAL` for downloadable content, or `FIXED_BUNDLE` for a bundle whose products the merchant selects.  When passing `productType: PHYSICAL`, you must also pass `physicalProperties`. When passing `productType: DIGITAL`, attach a file by uploading it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and passing the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id` in each variant. A digital product created without a file cannot be sold. When passing `productType: FIXED_BUNDLE`, you must also pass `fixedBundleProperties`.

variantsInfo.description: Product variants. Each variant represents a specific purchasable version of a product defined by option choices.  Each variant must reference all product options via its `choices` array, using `optionChoiceNames` in requests. You must explicitly provide each variant when creating products with options.  For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).

physicalProperties.description: Physical properties. Must be passed when `productType: PHYSICAL`

digitalProperties.description: Digital properties. Must be passed when `productType: DIGITAL`.  To attach a file, upload it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and pass the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id`. A variant without `digitalFile` set cannot be sold.

visible.description: Whether the variant is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`  > **Note:** For products without options, updating this field automatically > updates the product's visibility to match. > For products with options, the product and variant visibility values are independent.

choices.description: List of choices that define this variant. Each variant must have exactly one choice for each product option.  Use `optionChoiceNames` in all requests where this field is required. For products without options, this array is empty, representing a single "default variant".  For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).

revenueDetails.description: Variant revenue details.  > **Note:** Returned only when the following conditions are met: > + You pass `"MERCHANT_DATA"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests. > + Your app has the required `SCOPE.STORES.PRODUCT_READ_ADMIN` permission scope.

purchaseEligibility.description: Purchase eligibility settings for the product.

userCriteria.description: Criteria a buyer must meet to purchase the product.

additionalRibbons.description: Additional [ribbons](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/ribbons-v3/introduction.md) displayed on the product, beyond the primary `ribbon`.  Use this field to highlight multiple product attributes at once, for example combining a "New" ribbon with a "Sale" ribbon. Both the primary and additional ribbons are rendered on product cards and on the product page.  Each entry follows the same assignment rules as `ribbon`: + Pass `additionalRibbons.name` to add a new ribbon while creating or updating the product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.  A ribbon can be assigned to a product at most once: the same ribbon can't appear more than once in `additionalRibbons`, and a ribbon set as `ribbon` can't also appear in `additionalRibbons`.  Supports up to 4 additional ribbons per product.

extendedFields.description: Custom extended fields for the product object.  [Extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/schema-plugins/about-schema-plugin-extensions.md) must be configured in the app dashboard before they can be accessed with API calls.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions.  Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md).

tags.description: Tags assigned to the product, organized into public and private tags.

privateTags.description: Tags that require an additional permission in order to access them, normally not given to site members or visitors.

publicTags.description: Tags that are exposed to anyone who has access to the labeled entity itself, including site members and visitors.

subscriptionDetails.description: Product subscriptions.  Subscription discounts are defined at the product level but apply to each variant's `actualPrice`. This means the final subscription price varies per variant based on the variant's base price.

autoRenewal.description: Whether subscription is renewed automatically at the end of each period. Cannot be `false`, instead set `billingCycles`.

billingCycles.description: Number of billing cycles before subscription ends.

visible.description: Whether the subscription is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`

frequency.description: Frequency of recurring payment. For example, if `frequency: MONTH` and `billingCycles: 6`; payment will be made monthly for 6 months.

interval.description: Interval of recurring payment. Default: `1`. For example, if `frequency: MONTH`, `billingCycles: 3` and `interval: 2`; payment will be made every 2 months for a total of 6 months.

discount.description: Discount info (optional). For example, a $20 discount would be `amount: 20`, `type: AMOUNT`.

allowOneTimePurchases.description: Whether to allow one-time purchases in addition to subscription-based purchases.  Default: `false`

returnEntity.description: Whether to return the full product entities in the response.  Default: `false`

actions.name: bulk_add_info_sections_to_products

fields.description: Fields to include in the response.

infoSectionIds.description: List of GUIDs of info sections to add.

products.description: List of product GUIDs and revisions.

revision.description: Revision number, which increments by 1 each time the product is updated. To prevent conflicting changes, the current revision must be passed when updating the product.

returnEntity.description: Whether to return the full updated product entities in the response.  Default: `false`

actions.name: bulk_add_info_sections_to_products_by_filter

filter.description: Filter object.

infoSectionIds.description: IDs of the info sections to add.

mode.description: Defines how separate search terms in `expression` are combined

fields.description: Fields to search in. If the array is empty, all searchable fields are searched. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

fuzzy.description: Whether to enable the search function to use an algorithm to automatically find results that are close to the search expression, such as typos and declensions.

actions.name: bulk_add_products_to_categories_by_filter
actions.description: Bulk add products to categories by filter. Adds multiple products to up to 5 categories, given the provided filter and search expression. categoryIds.description: IDs of the categories to which products will be added.

filter.description: Filter object.

mode.description: Defines how separate search terms in `expression` are combined

fields.description: Fields to search in. If the array is empty, all searchable fields are searched. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

fuzzy.description: Whether to enable the search function to use an algorithm to automatically find results that are close to the search expression, such as typos and declensions.

actions.name: bulk_adjust_product_variants_by_filter
actions.description: Bulk adjust product variants by filter. Adjusts the prices and costs of multiple variants by a specified amount or percentage, given the provided filter and search expression.  Use this method to apply bulk pricing changes, such as increasing all prices by 10%, without setting explicit values. Use [Bulk Update Product Variants By Filter](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/products-v3/bulk-update-product-variants-by-filter.md) to set explicit values instead. amount.description: A decimal value to increase or reduce from the original value, can be negative.

percentage.description: The percentage value to increase or reduce from the current value, can be negative.

amount.description: A decimal value to reduce from the original value.

percentage.description: The percentage value to reduce from the original value.

filter.description: Filter object.

mode.description: Defines how separate search terms in `expression` are combined

fields.description: Fields to search in. If the array is empty, all searchable fields are searched. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

fuzzy.description: Whether to enable the search function to use an algorithm to automatically find results that are close to the search expression, such as typos and declensions.

actions.name: create_products_with_inventory_bulk_create

products.description: List of products to create with inventory.

measurementUnit.description: Measurement unit. For example, to define price per 100 grams, set this field to "G".

slug.description: Product slug.  If not provided, the slug is autogenerated based on the product name.

plainDescription.description: Product description in HTML.  + When provided on create/update, this string must be valid HTML. visible.description: Whether the product is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`

visibleInPos.description: Whether the product is visible in POS (point of sale).  Default: `true` > **Note:** Always `false` for `productType: DIGITAL`.

media.description: Product media items.

itemsInfo.description: All media items. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"MEDIA_ITEMS_INFO"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

items.description: All media items associated with this product.  The first item in the array is automatically set as the product's main media.

id.description: Set media by GUID of an existing file in Wix Media Manager.

url.description: Set media using an external media URL.

thumbnail.description: Media thumbnail. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"THUMBNAIL"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

packageDimensions.description: Package dimensions (length, width, height of the shipping package).

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override.
