fields.description: Fields to include in the response.

physicalProperties.description: Physical properties.  Required when `productType: PHYSICAL`.

pricePerUnit.description: Price per unit settings. > **Note:** Use this field only when relevant. For example, for products that are sold by weight, volume, or length.

quantity.description: Quantity. For example, to define price per per 100 grams, set this field to `100`.

measurementUnit.description: Measurement unit. For example, to define price per 100 grams, set this field to "G".

revision.description: Revision number, which increments by 1 each time the product is updated. To prevent conflicting changes, the current revision must be passed when updating the product.  Ignored when creating a product with inventory.

slug.description: Product slug.  If not provided, the slug is autogenerated based on the product name.

plainDescription.description: Product description in HTML.  + When provided on create/update, this string must be valid HTML. It's then converted to rich content. + `plainDescription` is ignored when a value is also passed to the `description` field. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"PLAIN_DESCRIPTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

visible.description: Whether the product is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`

visibleInPos.description: Whether the product is visible in POS (point of sale).  Default: `true` > **Note:** Always `false` for `productType: DIGITAL`.

media.description: Product media items.

itemsInfo.description: All media items. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"MEDIA_ITEMS_INFO"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

items.description: All media items associated with this product.  The first item in the array is automatically set as the product's main media.

id.description: Set media by GUID of an existing file in Wix Media Manager.

url.description: Set media using an external media URL.

displayName.description: Media display name.  Overrides the default media name. Can be passed only when the media is set by a URL in this item's `url` field.

thumbnail.description: Media thumbnail. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"THUMBNAIL"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

taxGroupId.description: [Tax group GUID](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/e-commerce/extensions/tax/tax-groups/introduction.md). Used to apply specific tax rates to products.

options.description: Product options, such as "Size" or "Color". Options define the ways a product can vary.  When you provide options, you must also provide the corresponding variants. Each variant must have exactly one choice for each option. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Options are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Pass an existing customization's GUID to reuse it, or define options inline and new customization entities are created automatically.

choices.description: List of available choices for the option.

id.description: GUID of a customization with `customizationType: PRODUCT_OPTION`.

modifiers.description: Product modifiers. Collect additional information from customers without creating variants.  Unlike options, modifiers don't affect inventory or create additional variants. Use them for things like gift messages or engraving text. For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).  Modifiers are stored as reusable [customization](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/customizations-v3/introduction.md) entities. Pass an existing customization's GUID to reuse it, or define modifiers inline and new customization entities are created automatically.

defaultAddedPrice.description: Default amount to be added to the product's price.

title.description: Title of the text to be input by the customer.

id.description: GUID of a customization with `customizationType: MODIFIER`.

mandatory.description: Whether customer input is required for this modifier.  If not set, the modifier's `defaultMandatory` value applies.

brand.description: Product brand.  + Pass `brand.name` to add a new brand while creating a product. + Pass an existing brand's `id` to assign that brand to the product.

infoSections.description: Product info section.  + Pass `infoSection.uniqueName`, `infoSection.title`, and `infoSection.description` to add a new info section while creating a product. + Pass an existing info section's `id` or `uniqueName` to assign that info section to the product.

uniqueName.description: Info section unique name. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

plainDescription.description: Info section description in HTML.  When provided on create/update, this string must be a valid HTML. It will then be converted to rich content. `plainDescription` is ignored when value is also passed to the `description` field. > **Note:** Returned only when you pass `"INFO_SECTION_PLAIN_DESCRIPTION"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests.

ribbon.description: Primary product ribbon displayed on the product. Use `additionalRibbons` to assign further ribbons beyond the primary one.  + Pass `ribbon.name` to add a new ribbon while creating a product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.

additionalRibbons.description: Additional [ribbons](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/ribbons-v3/introduction.md) displayed on the product, beyond the primary `ribbon`.  Use this field to highlight multiple product attributes at once, for example combining a "New" ribbon with a "Sale" ribbon. Both the primary and additional ribbons are rendered on product cards and on the product page. Ribbons appear in the same order as this list.  Each entry follows the same assignment rules as `ribbon`: + Pass `additionalRibbons.name` to add a new ribbon while creating or updating the product. + Pass an existing ribbon's `id` or `name` to assign that ribbon to the product.  A ribbon can be assigned to a product at most once: the same ribbon can't appear more than once in `additionalRibbons`, and a ribbon set as `ribbon` can't also appear in `additionalRibbons`.  Supports up to 4 additional ribbons per product.

mainCategoryId.description: The GUID of the product's primary direct category, which defines the product's breadcrumbs path. For example, if the product's main category is "T-Shirts" (which is a subcategory of "Clothing"), the breadcrumbs path will be "Clothing > T-Shirts".

productType.description: Product type: `PHYSICAL` for tangible goods that require shipping, `DIGITAL` for downloadable content, or `FIXED_BUNDLE` for a bundle whose products the merchant selects.  When passing `productType: PHYSICAL`, you must also pass `physicalProperties`. When passing `productType: DIGITAL`, attach a file by uploading it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and passing the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id` in each variant. A digital product created without a file cannot be sold. When passing `productType: FIXED_BUNDLE`, you must also pass `fixedBundleProperties`.

variantsInfo.description: Product variants. Each variant represents a specific purchasable version of a product defined by option choices.  Each variant must reference all product options via its `choices` array, using `optionChoiceNames` in requests. Variants aren't auto-generated. You must explicitly provide each variant when creating products with options.  For more information, see [About Product Options and Variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/about-product-options-and-variants.md).

variants.description: List of related variants. Partial update of variants is not supported so on update you must pass all data for all of them. If you want to update existing variant you must provide `id`, otherwise new variant with different id will be created which might break some integrations that rely on variant ids.

physicalProperties.description: Physical properties. Must be passed when `productType: PHYSICAL`

weight.description: Variant shipping weight. product.physicalProperties.shipping_weight_range values are taken from here.

pricePerUnit.description: Price per unit info, in order to show price per unit on the product page. For example if one sells cheese and defines 100g here then we know that buying this variant buyer receives 100g of cheese. But on product page price will be displayed for units defined on product level. See `pricePerUnit.value` to understand how it's calculated.

productDimensions.description: Product dimensions (length, width, height of the physical product).

packageDimensions.description: Package dimensions (length, width, height of the shipping package).

digitalProperties.description: Digital properties. Must be passed when `productType: DIGITAL`.  To attach a file, upload it using [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and pass the resulting `file.id` from the upload response as `digitalProperties.digitalFile.id`. A variant without `digitalFile` set cannot be sold.

digitalFile.description: Digital file which will be downloaded by the buyer after successful purchase. Each variant can have a different digital file, allowing you to offer different content per variant.  `digitalFile.id` is a Media Manager file GUID — upload the file via [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url.md) and use the `file.id` from the upload response.

visible.description: Whether the variant is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`

actualPrice.description: Variant's current selling price. Must be greater than or equal to 0.

compareAtPrice.description: Original price before any discount, shown with a strikethrough in the UI of Wix sites. Only set this if a discount applies. When set, it should be higher than `actualPrice` to reflect savings.

revenueDetails.description: Variant revenue details.  > **Note:** Returned only when the following conditions are met: > + You pass `"MERCHANT_DATA"` to the `fields` array in Products API requests. > + Your app has the required `SCOPE.STORES.PRODUCT_READ_ADMIN` permission scope.

inventoryItem.description: Inventory item of the variant on the default location.

inStock.description: Tracking method - in stock.  When set to `true`, the item is available for sale without a quantity limit.

quantity.description: Tracking method - quantity left in inventory.  Quantity can be negative when decrementing inventory for an order that has already been paid.

subscriptionDetails.description: Product subscriptions.  Subscription discounts are defined at the product level but apply to each variant's `actualPrice`. This means the final subscription price varies per variant based on the variant's base price.

autoRenewal.description: Whether subscription is renewed automatically at the end of each period. Cannot be `false`, instead set `billingCycles`.

billingCycles.description: Number of billing cycles before subscription ends.

visible.description: Whether the subscription is visible to site visitors.  Default: `true`

frequency.description: Frequency of recurring payment. For example, if `frequency: MONTH` and `billingCycles: 6`; payment will be made monthly for 6 months.

interval.description: Interval of recurring payment. Default: `1`. For example, if `frequency: MONTH`, `billingCycles: 3` and `interval: 2`; payment will be made every 2 months for a total of 6 months.

discount.description: Discount info (optional). For example, a $20 discount would be `amount: 20`, `type: AMOUNT`.

amountOff.description: Fixed amount subtracted from the variant price when calculating subscription prices.

percentOff.description: Percentage subtracted from the variant price when calculating subscription prices.

allowOneTimePurchases.description: Whether to allow one-time purchases in addition to subscription-based purchases.  Default: `false`

purchaseEligibility.description: Purchase eligibility settings for the product.

userCriteria.description: Criteria a buyer must meet to purchase the product.

extendedFields.description: Custom extended fields for the product object.  [Extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/schema-plugins/about-schema-plugin-extensions.md) must be configured in the [app dashboard](https://dev.wix.com/dc3/my-apps/) before they can be accessed with API calls.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions.  Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md).

tags.description: Tags

privateTags.description: Tags that require an additional permission in order to access them, normally not given to site members or visitors.

publicTags.description: Tags that are exposed to anyone who has access to the labeled entity itself, including site members and visitors.

returnEntity.description: Whether to return the full inventory entities in the response.  Default: `false`

actions.name: create_inventory_item
actions.description: Create inventory item. Creates an inventory item.  The combination of `variantId` and `locationId` must be unique.

inventoryItem.description: Inventory Item.  Each inventory item represents a specific product variant at a specific location. The combination of `variantId` and `locationId` is unique. You can't have 2 inventory items for the same variant at the same location.

inStock.description: Indicates that inventory is tracked by status rather than quantity.  When set to `true`, the item is marked as available for sale without tracking exact quantities. When set to `false`, the item is marked as out of stock. This tracking method is useful for made-to-order products or items with unlimited inventory.  When using this tracking method, `trackQuantity` is `false` and preorder limits aren't supported.

quantity.description: Indicates that inventory is tracked by quantity.  Set this field to the number of items currently in stock. This tracking method is useful when you need to know exactly how many items are available.  When using this tracking method, `trackQuantity` is `true`. Quantity can be negative when inventory is decremented for an order that has already been paid.

locationId.description: Stores location GUID. If not specified when creating an inventory item, the store's default location is used.

preorderInfo.description: Item preorder info.  Preorder settings are configured per inventory item, so each variant-location combination can have its own preorder configuration.  > **Note:** The product entity's `inventory.preorderStatus` and `inventory.preorderAvailability` fields reflect only the default location's preorder state.

enabled.description: Whether preorder is enabled for this inventory item.  > **Note:** Preorder can't be enabled for digital products or products with subscriptions.  Default: `false`

message.description: Message displayed to customers when the item is out of stock and preorder is enabled.

limit.description: Maximum number of items that can be preordered after stock reaches zero.  Supported only for inventory items with `trackQuantity = true`.  Default: `100000`

extendedFields.description: Custom field data for the inventory item object.  [Extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/schema-plugins/about-schema-plugin-extensions.md) must be configured in the app dashboard before they can be accessed with API calls.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions.  Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md).

actions.name: get_inventory_item
actions.description: Get inventory item. Retrieves an inventory item.

actions.name: delete_inventory_item
actions.description: Delete inventory item. Deletes an inventory item.

actions.name: update_inventory_item
actions.description: Update inventory item. Updates an inventory item.   Each time the inventory item is updated, `revision` increments by 1. The current `revision` must be passed when updating the inventory item. This ensures you're working with the latest inventory item and prevents unintended overwrites.

inventoryItem.description: Inventory Item.  Each inventory item represents a specific product variant at a specific location. The combination of `variantId` and `locationId` is unique. You can't have 2 inventory items for the same variant at the same location.

inStock.description: Indicates that inventory is tracked by status rather than quantity.  When set to `true`, the item is marked as available for sale without tracking exact quantities. When set to `false`, the item is marked as out of stock. This tracking method is useful for made-to-order products or items with unlimited inventory.  When using this tracking method, `trackQuantity` is `false` and preorder limits aren't supported.

quantity.description: Indicates that inventory is tracked by quantity.  Set this field to the number of items currently in stock. This tracking method is useful when you need to know exactly how many items are available.  When using this tracking method, `trackQuantity` is `true`. Quantity can be negative when inventory is decremented for an order that has already been paid.

revision.description: Revision number, which increments by 1 each time the inventory item is updated. To prevent conflicting changes, the current revision must be passed when updating the inventory item.  Ignored when creating an inventory item.

locationId.description: Stores location GUID. If not specified when creating an inventory item, the store's default location is used.

preorderInfo.description: Item preorder info.  Preorder settings are configured per inventory item, so each variant-location combination can have its own preorder configuration.  > **Note:** The product entity's `inventory.preorderStatus` and `inventory.preorderAvailability` fields reflect only the default location's preorder state.

enabled.description: Whether preorder is enabled for this inventory item.  > **Note:** Preorder can't be enabled for digital products or products with subscriptions.  Default: `false`

message.description: Message displayed to customers when the item is out of stock and preorder is enabled.

limit.description: Maximum number of items that can be preordered after stock reaches zero.  Supported only for inventory items with `trackQuantity = true`.  Default: `100000`

extendedFields.description: Custom field data for the inventory item object.  [Extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/schema-plugins/about-schema-plugin-extensions.md) must be configured in the app dashboard before they can be accessed with API calls.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions.  Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md).

reason.description: The reason for the inventory change.

actions.name: query_inventory_items
actions.description: Query inventory items. Retrieves a list of up to 1,000 inventory items, given the provided filtering, sorting, and cursor paging.  To learn about working with _Query_ endpoints, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md), and [Sorting and Paging](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-sorting-and-paging.md). Learn more about the differences between [_Query_ and _Search_](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-search-query-and-list-methods.md) methods.

cursorPaging.description: Cursor token pointing to a page of results. Not used in the first request. Following requests use the cursor token and not `filter` or `sort`.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object.  Learn more about [filtering](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md#filters).

sort.description: Sort object.  Learn more about [sorting](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md#sorting).

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

actions.name: search_inventory_items
actions.description: Search inventory items. Retrieves a list of inventory items, given the provided filtering, sorting, and cursor paging.   Search Inventory Items runs with these defaults, which you can override:  - `createdDate` is sorted in `DESC` order - `cursorPaging.limit` is `100`  To learn about working with _Search_ endpoints, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md), and [Sorting and Paging](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-sorting-and-paging.md).  Learn more about the differences between [_Query_ and _Search_](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-ref...

cursorPaging.description: Cursor paging options.  Learn more about [cursor paging](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md#cursor-paging).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object.  Learn more about [filtering](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md#filters).

sort.description: List of sort objects.  Learn more about [sorting](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md#sorting).

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

aggregations.description: Logical groupings of data into facets, with summaries for each facet. For example, use aggregations to allow site visitors to narrow down their search results by selecting specific categories.

value.description: A value aggregation calculates metrics such as count for specific fields within a dataset, providing insights into the overall distribution and key statistics of those values. For example, use a value aggregation to get the number (count) of products for each price listed in the store.

includeOptions.description: Options for including missing values in results.

addToBucket.description: Specify a custom name for the bucket containing the missing values. Defaults are `"N/A"` for strings, `0` for integers, and `false` for booleans.

sortType.description: Sort type.

sortDirection.description: Sort direction.

limit.description: Number of aggregation results to return. Min: `1` Max: `250` Default: `10`

missingValues.description: Whether to include or exclude missing values in the aggregation results. Default: `EXCLUDE`.

range.description: A range aggregation calculates the count of the values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within the range of each bucket you define. For example, use a range aggregation to compare the number of reservations made for parties of 4 or less to the number of reservations made for parties with 5 or more.

buckets.description: List of range buckets, where during aggregation each entity will be placed in the first bucket its value falls into, based on the provided range bounds.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the range. Required if `to` is not provided.

to.description: Exclusive upper bound of the range. Required if `from` is not provided.

scalar.description: A scalar aggregation calculates a single numerical value from a dataset, summarizing the dataset into one key metric: `COUNT_DISTINCT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, or `MAX`.

type.description: Operator type for the scalar aggregation.

dateHistogram.description: A date histogram calculates the count of time values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within each time interval you define (hour, day, week, etc.) For example, use a date histogram to find how many reservations have been made at a restaurant each week.

interval.description: Interval for date histogram aggregation.

nested.description: A nested aggregation is applied within the results of another aggregation. Rather than aggregating directly on the primary dataset, first group data using one aggregation and then apply another aggregation within each group. It allows for more complex analyses where you can summarize data at different levels of detail or hierarchy. For example, to get the number of products that are in stock and out of stock for each price listed, first perform a value aggregation on `discountedPriceNumeric`, and a second value aggregation on `inStock`.

nestedAggregations.description: Flattened list of aggregations, where each next aggregation is nested within previous one.

value.description: A value aggregation calculates the distribution of a specific field's values within a dataset, providing insights into the overall distribution and key statistics of those values. For example, use a value aggregation to get the number (count) of orders for each order status.

range.description: A range aggregation calculates the count of the values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within the range of each bucket you define. For example, use a range aggregation to compare the number of reservations made for parties of 4 or less to the number of reservations made for parties with 5 or more. If ranges overlap, a record that fits more than one range will only be counted in the first range that matches the criteria.

scalar.description: A scalar aggregation calculates a single numerical value from a dataset, summarizing the dataset into one key metric: `COUNT_DISTINCT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, or `MAX`.

dateHistogram.description: A date histogram calculates the count of time values from the specified field in the dataset that fall within each time interval you define (hour, day, week, etc.). For example, use a date histogram to determine how many reservations have been made at a restaurant each week. If ranges overlap, a record that fits more than one range will only be counted in the first range that matches the criteria.

name.description: Unique, caller-defined aggregation name, returned in `aggregations.results`.

type.description: Type of aggregation to perform. The matching aggregation field must be passed.

fieldPath.description: Field to aggregate by. Use dot notation to specify a JSON path. For example, `order.address.streetName`.

type.description: Type of aggregation to perform. Must align with the corresponding aggregation field.

actions.description: Create category. Creates a category.

Each category belongs to a specific category tree, identified by its `treeReference`. Each Wix Stores site has one category tree.  > **Note:** Currently, only Wix Stores Catalog (V3) categories are supported. Pass `appNamespace: "@wix/stores"` in the `treeReference` for all API calls.

visible.description: Whether the category is visible to site visitors.  Visibility cascades to subcategories: if a parent category's visibility is set to `false`, all its subcategories become hidden as well. Setting a subcategory's visibility to `true` fails if any of its parent categories are hidden.  > **Notes:** > 1. Hidden categories and their items are still accessible via API calls. For example, List Items In Category returns items even for hidden categories. > 2. The `visible` field can only be changed using the [Update Category Visibility](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/categories/update-category-visibility.md) method. > 3. Default: `true`

parentCategory.description: Information about the category's parent. Top-level categories don't have a parent.

id.description: GUID of the parent category.  Leave empty or omit to create a top-level category.

slug.description: Category slug. A URL-friendly identifier used in the category page address.  If not provided, the slug is autogenerated based on the category name.

seoData.description: Custom SEO data for the category.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

For example, List Items In Category returns items even for hidden categories. > 2. The `visible` field can only be changed using the [Update Category Visibility](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/stores/catalog-v3/categories/update-category-visibility.md) method. > 3. props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

brand.description: Product brand. Including a brand name can help improve site and product [visibility on search engines](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-brand-names-to-boost-product-page-seo-in-wix-stores).

sku.description: Stock keeping unit. If [variant management](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-adding-and-customizing-product-options#setting-different-prices-for-variants) is enabled, SKUs will be set per variant, and this field will be empty.

weight.description: Product weight. If [variant management](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-adding-and-customizing-product-options#setting-different-prices-for-variants) is enabled, weight will be set per variant, and this field will be empty.

productDimensions.description: Product dimensions (length, width, height of the physical product). If [variant management](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-adding-and-customizing-product-options#setting-different-prices-for-variants) is enabled, dimensions will be set per variant, and this field will be empty.

length.description: Length. Measurement unit is handled at the system level (metric/imperial).

width.description: Width. Measurement unit is handled at the system level (metric/imperial).

height.description: Height. Measurement unit is handled at the system level (metric/imperial).

unit.description: Unit of measurement for dimensions (length, width, height).

packageDimensions.description: Package dimensions (length, width, height of the shipping package). If [variant management](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-adding-and-customizing-product-options#setting-different-prices-for-variants) is enabled, dimensions will be set per variant, and this field will be empty.

additionalInfoSections.description: Additional text that the store owner can assign to the product (e.g. shipping details, refund policy, etc.).

manageVariants.description: Whether variants are being managed for this product - enables unique SKU, price and weight per variant. Also affects inventory data.

value.description: Choice value.

discount.description: Discount deducted from the product's original price.

value.description: Discount value

seoData.description: Custom SEO data for the product.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

ribbon.description: Product ribbon. Used to highlight relevant information about a product. For example, "Sale", "New Arrival", "Sold Out".

brand.description: Product brand. Including a brand name can help improve site and product [visibility on search engines](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-brand-names-to-boost-product-page-seo-in-wix-stores).

actions.name: update_product_variants
actions.description: Update product variants. Updates variants of a specified product.

choices.description: The specific choices available or chosen from within a selection (e.g., choosing the red Selection triggers the red Choice). You may specify all the relevant choices for a specific variant, or only some of the options, which will return all corresponding variants (Not relevant when passing variant GUIDs)

variantIds.description: List of variant GUIDs (Not relevant when passing choices)

weight.description: Variant weight

visible.description: Whether the variant is visible to  customers

productDimensions.description: Product dimensions (length, width, height of the physical product)

length.description: Length. Measurement unit is handled at the system level (metric/imperial).

width.description: Width. Measurement unit is handled at the system level (metric/imperial).

height.description: Height. Measurement unit is handled at the system level (metric/imperial).

unit.description: Unit of measurement for dimensions (length, width, height).

packageDimensions.description: Package dimensions (length, width, height of the shipping package)

actions.name: convert_currency
actions.description: Convert currency. Returns a list of converted amounts, from the original (from) currency to the target (to) currency.

from.description: The from

to.description: The to

value.description: Value without decimals (e.g., for 10.95 value will be 1095).

decimalPlaces.description: Decimal places to apply (e.g., for 10.95 decimal_places will be 2).

actions.name: get_conversion_rate
actions.description: Get conversion rate. Returns the conversion rate between 2 currencies.

from.description: The from

to.description: The to

actions.name: list_currencies
actions.description: List currencies. Returns all currencies currently supported by Wix.

actions.name: get_currencies
actions.description: Get currencies. Retrieves the list of currencies that can be displayed on the site.  Returns all currencies that are currently enabled for the site. Visitors can view prices in any of these currencies.

actions.name: set_currencies
actions.description: Set currencies. Sets the list of currencies that can be displayed on the site.  When you set currencies for a site, visitors can view prices in any of these currencies. currencies.description: List of currencies to enable for the site. This list replaces any previously configured currencies. Pass an empty array to disable currency conversion.

actions.name: create_service
actions.description: Create service. Creates a service.   ### Required fields  When creating a service you must specify the following fields: - [`type`](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/services/services-v2/about-service-types.md): Whether it's an appointment-based service, class, or course. - `name`: Service name that's displayed to customers. - `onlineBooking`: Settings determining whether customers can book online, whether the business must manually confirm bookings, and whether customers can request to book an appointment time slot that already has a booking request awaiting business confirmation. - [`payment`](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/boo...

service.description: The `service` object represents an offering that a business provides to its customers.

appId.description: GUID of the app associated with the service. You can't update `appId`. Services are displayed in Wix Bookings only if they are associated with the Wix Bookings appId or have no associated app GUID. Default: `13d21c63-b5ec-5912-8397-c3a5ddb27a97` (Wix Bookings app GUID) For services from Wix apps, the following values apply: - Wix Bookings: `"13d21c63-b5ec-5912-8397-c3a5ddb27a97"` - Wix Services: `"cc552162-24a4-45e0-9695-230c4931ef40"` - Wix Meetings: `"6646a75c-2027-4f49-976c-58f3d713ed0f"`.<!-- [Scheduling Form Fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/about-scheduling-form-fields.md) services also use this app GUID. Use `createdByAppId` to distinguish between Wix Meetings and Scheduling Form Fields services.--> [Full list of apps created by Wix](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/platform/about-apps-created-by-wix.md). <!-- TODO: Uncomment when Platform docs are published - Learn more about [app identity in the Bookings Platform](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/bookings-platform/app-identity-in-the-bookings-platform.md). -->

sortOrder.description: Order of the service within a [category](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/services/categories-v1/category-object.md).

description.description: Service description. For example, `High-class hair styling, cuts, straightening and color`.

tagLine.description: Short service description, such as `Hair styling`.

defaultCapacity.description: Default maximum number of customers that can book the service. The service cannot be booked beyond this capacity.

media.description: Media associated with the service.

items.description: Media items associated with the service.

image.description: Details of the image associated with the service, such as URL and size.

url.description: Image URL. (similar to image.id e.g. "4b3901ffcb8d7ad81a613779d92c9702.jpg")

mainMedia.description: Primary media associated with the service.

coverMedia.description: Cover media associated with the service.

hidden.description: Whether the service is hidden from Wix Bookings pages and widgets.

category.description: [Category](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/services/categories-v2/introduction.md) the service is associated with. Services aren't automatically assigned to a category. Without an associated category, the service isn't visible on the live site.

form.description: Form the customer filled out when booking the service.

id.description: GUID of the form associated with the service. The form information that you submit when booking includes contact details, participants, and other form fields set up for the service. You can manage the service booking form fields using the Bookings Forms API.

payment.description: Payment options for booking the service. Learn more about [service payments](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/services/services-v2/about-service-payments.md).

fixed.description: The details for the fixed price of the service.  Required when: `rateType` is `FIXED`

price.description: The fixed price required to book the service.  Required when: `rateType` is `FIXED`

value.description: Monetary amount. Decimal string with a period as a decimal separator. For example `25.05`.

formattedValue.description: Monetary amount. Decimal string in local format. For example, `1 000,30`.

deposit.description: The deposit price required to book the service.  Required when: `rateType` is `FIXED` and `paymentOptions.deposit` is `true`

fullUpfrontPaymentAllowed.description: Whether customers can choose to pay the full service price upfront instead of only the deposit.  Used only when a `deposit` amount is set.  Default: `false`.

depositDetails.description: The deposit required to book the service, expressed as either a fixed amount or a percentage of the price.  Used only when `paymentOptions.deposit` is `true`.

amount.description: The deposit as a fixed monetary amount.

percentage.description: The deposit as a percentage of the full service price, for example `20` for 20% or `20.5` for 20.5%. Resolved to a concrete amount when the customer books.  Min: `0.01` percent Max: `99.99` percent

custom.description: The details for the custom price of the service.  Required when: `rateType` is `CUSTOM`

description.description: A custom description explaining to the customer how to pay for the service.

varied.description: The details for the varied pricing of the service. Read more about [varied price options](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-bookings-about-getting-paid-online#offering-varied-price-options).  Required when: `rateType` is `VARIED`

defaultPrice.description: The default price for the service without any variants. It will also be used as the default price for any new variant.

deposit.description: The deposit price required to book the service.  Required when: `rateType` is `VARIED` and `paymentOptions.deposit` is `true`

fullUpfrontPaymentAllowed.description: Whether customers can choose to pay the full service price upfront instead of only the deposit.  Used only when a `deposit` amount is set.  Default: `false`.

depositDetails.description: The deposit required to book the service, expressed as either a fixed amount or a percentage of the price.  Used only when `paymentOptions.deposit` is `true`.

subscription.description: Subscription pricing details for the service. Supported for course services only. The business charges recurring monthly payments instead of a one-time fee.  Required when: `rateType` is `SUBSCRIPTION`.

amountPerBillingCycle.description: Base price charged per billing cycle before tax and discounts. The actual amount charged may differ after checkout applies tax and discounts.

frequency.description: Billing frequency for recurring subscription charges. Reflected as `billingFrequency` in the booking's subscription info.  Currently supports `MONTHLY` only.

totalPayments.description: Total number of billing cycles in the subscription. For example, `12` for a 12-month subscription with monthly payments. Reflected as `totalCycles` in the booking's subscription info.  Required when: `rateType` is `SUBSCRIPTION`.

firstChargeDate.description: Determines when the first billing cycle payment is charged. Used together with `recurringStartDate` to define the subscription billing schedule.

recurringStartDate.description: Date and time when recurring billing starts.  When `firstChargeDate` is `CHECKOUT`, the first charge occurs at checkout and subsequent billing cycles start from this date.  When `firstChargeDate` is `SCHEDULED`, the first charge occurs on this date.  Customers who book after recurring billing starts are billed for the remaining billing cycles only.  Required when: `rateType` is `SUBSCRIPTION`.

rateType.description: The rate the customer is expected to pay for the service.

options.description: The payment options a customer can use to pay for the service.

online.description: Customers can pay for the service online. When `true`: + `rateType` must be `FIXED`, `VARIED`, or `SUBSCRIPTION`. + `fixed.price`, `varied.defaultPrice`, or `subscription.amountPerBillingCycle` must be specified respectively.  Required when: `rateType` is `SUBSCRIPTION`. Read more about [getting paid online](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-bookings-about-getting-paid-online).

inPerson.description: Customers can pay for the service in person.

deposit.description: This service requires a deposit to be made online in order to book it. When `true`: + `rateType` must be `VARIED` or `FIXED`. + A `deposit` must be specified. + `online` must be `true`. + `inPerson` must be `false`.

pricingPlan.description: Whether customers can pay for the service using a pricing plan. Read more about [service payment options](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/services/services-v2/about-service-payments.md).

addOnOption.description: How customers can pay for add-ons when paying for the related booking with a [pricing plan](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/pricing-plans/pricing-plans/introduction.md). If customers pay for the booking using any method other than a pricing plan, the value of this field is ignored.

enabled.description: Whether the service can be booked online. When set to `true`, customers can book the service online. Configure the payment options via the `service.payment` property. When set to `false`, customers cannot book the service online, and the service can only be paid for in person.

requireManualApproval.description: Booking the service requires approval by the Wix user.

allowMultipleRequests.description: Multiple customers can request to book the same time slot. This is relevant when `requireManualApproval` is `true`.

enabled.description: Whether a conference link is generated for the service's sessions.

locations.description: The locations this service is offered at. Read more about [service locations](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/services/services-v2/about-service-locations.md).

business.description: Information about business locations. Required when `type` is `BUSINESS`.

id.description: GUID of the business [location](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/locations/introduction.md). When setting a business location, specify only the location GUID. Other location details are overwritten.

custom.description: Information about custom locations. Required when `type` is `CUSTOM`.

subdivision.description: Code for a subdivision (such as state, prefecture, or province) in [ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2) format.

formattedAddress.description: Full address of the location.

bookingPolicy.description: [Policy](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/policies/booking-policies/introduction.md) determining under what conditions this service can be booked. For example, whether the service can only be booked up to 30 minutes before it begins.

id.description: The GUID to the policy for the booking.

intakeFormPolicy.description: Rule for requiring customers to complete an [intake form](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/forms/other-services/intake-forms/introduction.md) during or after booking.

enabled.description: Whether intake form integration is enabled for the service. Default: `false`

formId.description: GUID of the intake form to integrate with the service.

timing.description: When to present the intake form to the customer.

schedule.description: The service's [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/introduction.md), which can be used to manage the service's [events](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/events-v3/introduction.md).

sessionDurations.description: List of supported session durations in minutes.  - For appointment-based services, specify `sessionDurations` when creating a service. - For appointment-based services with varied pricing by session length, you must still specify `sessionDurations`, but the values are ignored. Actual durations are taken from the [service variants](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/services/service-options-and-variants/introduction.md). - For classes or courses, don't specify `sessionDurations` when creating a service.

timeBetweenSessions.description: The number of minutes between the end of a session and the start of the next.

durationRange.description: Duration range for the service. When set, the customer picks a duration within the configured min/max range instead of a fixed session duration. Mutually exclusive with `sessionDurations`. A service uses one or the other. Can't be combined with `workingHours`, unless `workingHours.mode` is `INTERSECT_BUSINESS_WORKING_HOURS`.  Use `durationRange` for services where the customer chooses how long to book, such as equipment or space rentals. The `unitType` determines whether the range is measured in hours or days.

hourOptions.description: Configuration for hourly duration ranges. Set when `unitType` is `HOUR`.

minDurationInMinutes.description: Minimum bookable duration in minutes. The customer can't book for less than this duration.

maxDurationInMinutes.description: Maximum bookable duration in minutes. The customer can't book for more than this duration.  Must be greater than or equal to `minDurationInMinutes`.

dayOptions.description: Configuration for daily duration ranges. Set when `unitType` is `DAY`.

minDurationInDays.description: Minimum bookable duration in days. The customer can't book for less than this number of days.

maxDurationInDays.description: Maximum bookable duration in days. The customer can't book for more than this number of days.  Must be greater than or equal to `minDurationInDays`.

unitType.description: The unit type for this duration range. Determines which configuration to use in the `config` union.

staffMemberIds.description: IDs of the [resources](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/resources/resources-v2/introduction.md) associated with the [staff members](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/staff-members/staff-members/introduction.md) providing the service. Note that these are the resource GUIDs, not the staff member GUIDs.  For appointment-based services, set this field when creating or updating the service. For classes and courses, this field is read-only and is automatically derived from staff assigned to the service's recurring scheduled sessions. Staff assigned only to single, non-recurring events are not included. Once all of a staff member's upcoming recurring sessions have ended, their GUID is removed from this field. To retrieve the full list of staff for classes or courses, query the service's calendar events instead. Learn more about [retrieving staff for classes and courses](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/services/services-v2/sample-flows.md#retrieve-staff-members-for-a-class-or-course).

staffMemberDetails.description: Staff members details. Returned only if `STAFF_MEMBER_DETAILS` conditional field was specified.

staffMembers.description: Staff members providing the service. For appointments only.

serviceResources.description: Information about which resources must be available so customers can book the service. For example, a meeting room or equipment. Some nested fields are only returned when specific conditional fields are requested: pass `RESOURCE_TYPE_DETAILS` to retrieve `resourceType.name`, and `RESOURCE_DETAILS` to retrieve `resourceDetails.resources`.

resourceIds.description: IDs of specific [resources](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/resources/resources-v2/introduction.md) assigned to this service resource. Each GUID must reference a resource within the specified `resourceType`.  When set, only these resources are considered for availability and booking. When not set, all resources of the specified resource type are eligible.

values.description: Values of the resource GUIDs.

extendedFields.description: Extensions enabling users to save custom data related to the service.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. primaryResourceType.description: GUID of the [resource type](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/resources/resource-types-v2/introduction.md) that serves as the primary resource for this appointment service. For example, when set to a "Meeting Rooms" resource type, availability is calculated based on the rooms' schedules rather than staff schedules.  Default: The staff resource type.

These fields are excluded from the response by default because retrieving them requires additional calls to other services.
