props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

actions.name: get_deleted_draft_post
actions.description: Get deleted draft post. Retrieves a deleted draft post from the trash bin by the provided GUID.

actions.name: remove_from_trash_bin
actions.description: Remove from trash bin. Permanently deletes a draft post that is currently in the trash bin.  This action is permanent and can't be reversed.

actions.name: list_deleted_draft_posts
actions.description: List deleted draft posts. Retrieves a list of up to 100 deleted draft posts.  List Draft Posts runs with these defaults, which you can override: - `editedDate` is sorted in descending order. In this case,`editedDate` implies the date the post was deleted. - `paging.limit` is `50`. - `paging.offset` is `0`.

fieldsets.description: List of additional draft post fields to include in the response. For example, use the `URL` fieldset to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the draft post's base fields. Base fields don’t include any of the supported fieldset values. By default only the draft post's base fields are returned.

language.description: Language filter.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. If omitted, deleted draft posts in all languages are returned.

paging.offset.description: Number of items to skip in the current sort order.   Default: `0`

paging.limit.description: Number of items to return.   Default:`50`

paging.cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.

actions.name: publish_draft_post
actions.description: Publish draft post. Publishes a draft post by GUID. This creates a new [post](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/blog/posts-stats/post-object.md) with the data from the draft post.  If the draft post was already published, the published post will be updated with the latest values from the draft post.  Fails with the `POST_TITLE_REQUIRED` application error when the draft post has no title.

actions.name: restore_from_trash_bin
actions.description: Restore from trash bin. Restores a deleted draft post from the trash bin by the provided GUID.

actions.name: translate_draft
actions.description: Translate draft. Creates a draft post in the specified language by copying an existing draft post or published post.  The created draft post contains the source draft's title, rich content, excerpt, cover and hero images, hashtags, pricing plan GUIDs, preview text paragraph, and commenting and featured settings. Tags, related posts, SEO data, and the slug aren't copied. Category GUIDs are replaced with the GUIDs of the categories' translations in the specified language. Categories that have no translation in that language are omitted.  The created draft post shares the source's `translationId` and keeps the source's `memberId`. If the source doesn't have a `translationId` yet, one is gene...

fieldsets.description: Predefined sets of fields to return in the created draft post, in addition to the core draft post fields.  - `URL`: Returns the draft post's preview URL. - `CONTENT`: Returns the draft post's content. - `RICH_CONTENT`: Returns the draft post's rich content. - `GENERATED_EXCERPT`: Returns an excerpt generated from the content if a custom excerpt isn't set.  Default: Core draft post fields only.

language.description: Language to translate the post into, in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. For example, `de` for German, or `pt-br` for Brazilian Portuguese.

actions.name: update_draft_post_language
actions.description: Update draft post language. Changes the language of a draft post and replaces its categories with their translations in the specified language.  Category GUIDs are replaced with the GUIDs of the categories' translations in the specified language. Categories that have no translation in that language are removed. Tag GUIDs and related post GUIDs are cleared, because tags and related posts are language specific. If the draft post is published, the published post is updated in the same way.  Changing the language to the draft post's current language fails with an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` error. Changing it to a language that already exists in the same translation group fails with an `ALREADY_EXISTS...

fieldsets.description: Predefined sets of fields to return in the updated draft post, in addition to the core draft post fields.  - `URL`: Returns the draft post's preview URL. - `CONTENT`: Returns the draft post's content. - `RICH_CONTENT`: Returns the draft post's rich content. - `GENERATED_EXCERPT`: Returns an excerpt generated from the content if a custom excerpt isn't set.  Default: Core draft post fields only.

language.description: New language of the draft post, in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. For example, `de` for German, or `pt-br` for Brazilian Portuguese.

actions.name: get_post
actions.description: Get post. Retrieves a post by the specified GUID.

fieldsets.description: List of additional post fields to include in the response. For example, use the `URL` fieldset to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the post’s base fields. Base fields don’t include any of the supported fieldset values. By default only the post’s base fields are returned.

actions.name: query_posts
actions.description: Query posts. Retrieves a list of up to 100 posts, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting.  Query Posts runs with these defaults, which you can override: - `firstPublishedDate` is sorted in descending order, with pinned posts first. - `paging.limit` is `50`. - `paging.offset` is `0`.  To learn about working with _Query_ endpoints, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language), [Sorting and Paging](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/sorting-and-paging), and [Field Projection](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/field-projection).

fieldsets.description: List of additional post fields to include in the response. For example, use the `URL` fieldset to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the post’s base fields. Base fields don’t include any of the supported fieldset values. By default only the post’s base fields are returned.

cursorPaging.description: Cursor token pointing to a page of results. Not used in the first request. Following requests use the cursor token and not `filter` or `sort`.

limit.description: Number of items to load.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  You can get the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object in the following format: `"filter" : { "fieldName1": "value1", "fieldName2":{"$operator":"value2"} }` Example of operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$startsWith`, `$contains`

sort.description: Sort object in the following format: `[{"fieldName":"sortField1","order":"ASC"},{"fieldName":"sortField2","order":"DESC"}]`

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

origin.description: Origin point for geo-distance sorting on a GEO field results are ordered by distance from this point (ASC = nearest first, DESC = farthest first).

skipCount.description: When true, omit `pagingMetadata.total`. `hasNext` and next cursor still come from the extra fetched row.

actions.name: list_posts
actions.description: List posts. Retrieves a list of up to 100 published posts per request.  List Posts runs with these defaults, which you can override: - `firstPublishedDate` is sorted in descending order, with pinned posts first. - `paging.limit` is `50`. - `paging.offset` is `0`.

categoryIds.description: Category filter.  Pass an array of category GUIDs to return only posts with any of the provided categories. If omitted, all posts with or without associated categories are returned.

featured.description: Whether to return only featured posts.  Default: `false`

fieldsets.description: List of additional post fields to include in the response. For example, use the `URL` fieldset to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the post’s base fields. Base fields don’t include any of the supported fieldset values. By default only the post’s base fields are returned.

hashtags.description: Hashtag filter.  Pass an array of hashtags to return only posts containing any of the provided hashtags. If omitted, all posts with or without hashtags are returned.

language.description: Language filter.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. Pass a language to only receive posts that are in that language. If omitted, posts in all languages are returned.

paging.offset.description: Number of items to skip in the current sort order.   Default: `0`

paging.limit.description: Number of items to return.   Default:`50`

paging.cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.

tagIds.description: Tag filter.  Pass an array of tag GUIDs to return only posts with any of the provided tags. If omitted, all posts with or without tags are returned.

actions.name: get_post_by_slug
actions.description: Get post by slug. Retrieves a post with the provided slug.  The slug is the end of a post's URL that refers to a specific post. For example, if a post's URL is `https:/example.com/blog/post/my-post-slug`, the slug is `my-post-slug`. The slug is case-sensitive, and is generally derived from the post title, unless specified otherwise.

fieldsets.description: List of additional post fields to include in the response. For example, use the `URL` fieldset to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the post’s base fields. Base fields don’t include any of the supported fieldset values. By default only the post’s base fields are returned.

language.description: Language of the post.

slug.description: Slug of the post to retrieve.

actions.name: get_post_metrics
actions.description: Get post metrics. Retrieves a post's metrics.  A post's metrics include the comments, likes, and views the post receives.

actions.name: get_total_posts
actions.description: Get total posts. Retrieves the total amount of published posts of the blog.

language.description: Language filter.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. Pass a language to receive the total amount of posts in that specified language.

actions.name: query_post_count
actions.description: Query post count. Retrieves the number of published posts per month within a specified time range.  The time range is set using the `rangeStart` and `months` properties. The time range always starts on the 1st day of the month set in `rangeStart` and includes the number of `months` following `rangeStart`. For example, if `rangeStart` is set to `'2022-03-13'` and `months` is set to `4`, the time range will be from `'2022-03-01'` until `'2022-06-30'`. The time range always ends on the last day of the month. > Note: If there are no published posts in a month within the time range, that month is not included in the response. For example, let's say a blog has `0` posts dated in February 2022. ...

language.description: Language filter.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. Pass a language to only receive the period post count for that specified language.

months.description: Number of months to include in response.

rangeStart.description: Start of time range to return, in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date and time format.

timeZone.description: Time zone to use when calculating the start of the month.  [UTC timezone offset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UTC_offsets) format. For example, New York time zone is `-05`.

actions.name: view_post
actions.description: View post. Increments a post's view count.  Call this method when a site visitor views a published post. The post must already be published. The response returns the post's updated total number of views.  This method accepts up to 100 calls per minute from an IP address on the site, and up to 100 calls per minute from an IP address for a single post. Further calls are rejected.

actions.name: category_create_category
actions.description: Create category. Creates a category.

label.description: Category label. Displayed in the Category Menu.

displayPosition.description: Position of the category in the [Category Menu](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-blog-adding-and-customizing-a-category-menu). Categories are displayed in ascending order. Categories with a position of `-1` appear at the end of the sequence.  Default: `-1`

translationId.description: GUID of the category's translations. All translations of a single category share the same `translationId`.

language.description: Category language.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format.

slug.description: Part of a category's URL that refers to a specific category. For example, the slug of `https:/example.com/blog/category/famous-cats` is `famous-cats`.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

url.description: Image URL.

fieldsets.description: List of additional category fields to include in the response. By default only the category’s base fields are returned. Base fields are all category fields that don't appear in the fieldset enum.  To retrieve a field, pass the relevant fieldset in the enum in the `fieldsets` array. For example, add the `URL` fieldset to `fieldsets` to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the category’s base fields.

actions.name: list_categories
actions.description: List categories. Retrieves a list of up to 100 categories per request.  If you pass a language filter to the method, it returns a list of up to 100 categories in the requested language.  The categoies are displayed in order of their `displayPosition`, starting with `0`. The `displayPosition` is the position in which the categories are displayed in the Category Menu page. By default, categories get added to the bottom of the Category Menu page with a `displayPosition` of `-1`.  List Categories runs with these defaults, which you can override: - `paging.limit` is `50`. - `paging.offset` is `0`.  List Categories is sorted by `displayPosition` in descending order. This cannot be overridden.

fieldsets.description: List of additional category fields to include in the response. By default only the category’s base fields are returned. Base fields are all category fields that don't appear in the fieldset enum.  To retrieve a field, pass the relevant fieldset in the enum in the `fieldsets` array. For example, add the `URL` fieldset to `fieldsets` to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the category’s base fields.

language.description: Language filter.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. Pass a language to only receive categories that are in that language. If omitted, categories in all languages are returned.

paging.offset.description: Number of items to skip in the current sort order.   Default: `0`

paging.limit.description: Number of items to return.   Default:`50`

paging.cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.

actions.name: category_query_categories
actions.description: Query categories. Retrieves a list of up to 100 categories, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting. Query Categories runs with these defaults, which you can override. - `displayPosition` is sorted in `DESC` order. - `paging.limit` is `50`. - `paging.offset` is `0`.  To learn about working with _Query_ endpoints, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language), [Sorting and Paging](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/sorting-and-paging), and [Field Projection](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/field-projection).

For example, add the `URL` fieldset to `fieldsets` to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the category’s base fields.

paging.description: Paging options to limit and skip the number of items.

limit.description: Number of items to load.

offset.description: Number of items to skip in the current sort order.

filter.description: Filter object in the following format: `"filter" : { "fieldName1": "value1", "fieldName2":{"$operator":"value2"} }` Example of operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$startsWith`, `$contains`

sort.description: Sort object in the following format: `[{"fieldName":"sortField1","order":"ASC"},{"fieldName":"sortField2","order":"DESC"}]`

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

origin.description: Origin point for geo-distance sorting on a GEO field results are ordered by distance from this point (ASC = nearest first, DESC = farthest first).

actions.description: Get category by slug. Gets a category with the specified slug.  The slug is at the end of the URL of a specific category. For example, if a category's URL is `https://example.com/blog/categories/famous-cats`, the slug is `famous-cats`. The slug is a case-sensitive string that is derived from the category's label, unless specified otherwise.

For example, add the `URL` fieldset to `fieldsets` to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the category’s base fields.

language.description: 2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. Language of the category to retrieve.

slug.description: Slug of the category to retrieve.

Base fields don’t include any of the supported fieldset values. By default only the tag's base fields are returned.

label.description: Tag label. The label for each tag in a blog must be unique.

language.description: Tag language.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format.

slug.description: Preferred tag slug. For example, `'tag-slug'`.

actions.name: get_tag_by_label
actions.description: Get tag by label. Retrieves a tag by the provided label.  Sub-labels can also be specified using a `/`. For example, you can have `'dessert/icecream'` and `'dessert/pie'` as two different tag labels.  > **Note:** The full URL path following `labels/` is counted as 1 label. Adding a `/` to a label does _not_ create multiple labels. This means that `'dessert/icecream'` is a single label.

fieldsets.description: List of additional tag fields to include in the response. For example, use the `URL` fieldset to retrieve the url field in the response in addition to the tag's base fields. Base fields don’t include any of the supported fieldset values. By default only the tag's base fields are returned.

language.description: Tag language.  2-or-4-letter language code in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. If omitted, tags in all languages are returned.

actions.name: get_tag_by_slug
actions.description: Get tag by slug. Retrieves a tag with the provided slug.  The `slug` is the end of a tag's URL that refers to a specific tag. For example, if a tag's URL is `https://example.com/blog/tag/{my-tag-slug}`, the slug is `my-tag-slug`. The `slug` is case-sensitive and derived from the tag's `label`.

slug.description: The slug

actions.name: create_like
actions.description: Create like. Creates a like for blog content.  >**Note:** >This method requires [visitor or member authentication](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/authentication/about-identities.md).

like.description: A like represents a positive reaction to blog content.  Likes are associated with specific blog content using their FQDN and entity GUID, allowing likes to be created for various types of blog content such as posts or comments.

entityId.description: GUID of the specific blog content being liked, such as a blog post or comment.

fqdn.description: Fully qualified domain name that identifies the type of blog content being liked. For example, `wix.blog.v3.post` for blog posts.

actions.name: get_like
actions.description: Get like. Retrieves a like created by the currently authenticated site visitor or member.  >**Note:** >This method requires [visitor or member authentication](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/authentication/about-identities.md).

actions.name: delete_like
actions.description: Delete like. Deletes a like created by the currently authenticated site visitor or member.  >**Note:** >This method requires [visitor or member authentication](https://dev.wix.com/docs/go-headless/coding/rest-api/visitors-and-members/make-api-calls-with-oauth.md).

actions.name: query_likes
actions.description: Query likes. Retrieves a list of likes created by the currently authenticated site visitor or member, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting.  This method: - Only returns likes [created](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/blog/likes/create-like.md) by the current authenticated user through the API. - Doesn't include likes created through the blog UI. - Doesn't include likes created by other users.  Up to 100 likes can be returned per request.  Query Likes runs with these defaults, which you can override:  - `createdDate` is sorted in `DESC` order - `paging.limit` is `50` - `paging.offset` is `0`  >**Note:** >This method requires [visitor or member authent...

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object.  Learn more about [filtering](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#filters).

sort.description: Sort object.  Learn more about [sorting](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#sorting).

actions.name: delete_like_by_fqdn_and_entity_id
actions.description: Delete like by fqdn and entity id. Deletes a site visitors' or members' like by blog content FQDN and entity GUID.  >**Note:** >This method requires [visitor or member authentication](https://dev.wix.com/docs/go-headless/coding/rest-api/visitors-and-members/make-api-calls-with-oauth.md).

actions.name: get_blog_settings
actions.description: Get blog settings. Retrieves the site's blog settings.  A site has one blog settings object. If the site has none yet, this method creates the default blog settings and returns them.  Specify `language` to retrieve `allPostsFeedLabel` in that language. Comments are not translated.

language.description: Language of `allPostsFeedLabel` to retrieve, in IETF BCP 47 language tag format. Typically, this is a lowercase 2-letter language code, followed by a hyphen, followed by an uppercase 2-letter country code. For example, `en-US` for U.S. English, and `de-DE` for Germany German.  When omitted, the language of the current request is used when the request includes one. Otherwise the primary language is used. If that language has no translation, the primary label is returned.

actions.name: update_blog_settings
actions.description: Update blog settings. Updates the site's blog settings.  Each time the blog settings are updated, `revision` increments by 1. The current `revision` must be passed when updating the blog settings. This ensures you're working with the latest blog settings and prevents unintended overwrites.  Only fields included in the request are updated. To update comments, include `enabled`, `anonymousEnabled`, `ratingsEnabled`, and `ratingsMandatory` together.  Specify `language` to update `allPostsFeedLabel` for that language. When `language` is a secondary language, the primary label is left unchanged. An unsupported language is rejected.

blogSettings.description: Blog settings control the label of the all-posts feed and whether visitors can comment. A site has one blog settings object.

revision.description: Revision number, which increments by 1 each time the blog settings are updated. To prevent conflicting changes, the current revision must be passed when updating the blog settings.

allPostsFeedLabel.description: Label of the feed that lists all posts.  Translatable. Specify `language` on Get Blog Settings or Update Blog Settings to read or write this label in a specific language.  Default: `All posts` when the site has no saved blog settings.

comments.description: Comment settings for the blog.  When updating comments, include `enabled`, `anonymousEnabled`, `ratingsEnabled`, and `ratingsMandatory` together. A partial comments object is rejected.

enabled.description: Whether comments are turned on for the blog.  Default: `true` when the site has no saved blog settings.

anonymousEnabled.description: Whether visitors can comment without signing in.  Default: `false` when the site has no saved blog settings.

ratingsEnabled.description: Whether visitors can rate a post when they comment.  Default: `false` when the site has no saved blog settings.

ratingsMandatory.description: Whether a rating is required when a visitor leaves a comment.  Default: `false` when the site has no saved blog settings.

language.description: Language of `allPostsFeedLabel` to update, in IETF BCP 47 language tag format. Typically, this is a lowercase 2-letter language code, followed by a hyphen, followed by an uppercase 2-letter country code. For example, `en-US` for U.S. English, and `de-DE` for Germany German.  When omitted, the primary language is updated. When the value is the site's primary language, the primary label is updated. When the value is a secondary language, only that language's label is updated.

actions.name: create_plan
actions.description: Create plan. Creates a plan with specified billing terms and a pricing strategy.   To create the most common types of plans: - **One-time**: Specify a `billingCycle` that's the desired duration and set `endType` to `CYCLES_COMPLETED` and `cyclesCompletedDetails.billingCycleCount` to `1`. - **Recurring**: Define the recurrence rule using the plan's `billingCycle` object. - **Free plan**: Set the plan's `flatRate.amount` to `0` and `maxPurchasesPerBuyer` to `1`.

idempotencyKey.description: Unique key to prevent duplicate plan creation. If the same key is used within a short time period, the original plan will be returned instead of creating a duplicate.

description.description: Plan description that explains what customers get with this plan.

image.description: Plan image displayed during checkout and on the site's **Plans & Pricing** page.

slug.description: Unique identifier for this plan within the Wix site. If not provided, generated automatically from the plan name.

termsAndConditions.description: Terms and conditions text that customers must agree to when purchasing this plan.

pricingVariants.description: Pricing variants that define different billing and pricing options for this plan. Currently limited to 1 variant per plan.

name.description: Name for this pricing variant, such as "Monthly" or "Yearly".

freeTrialDays.description: Number of days customers can use the plan for free before the first charge. Set to `0` for no free trial.

fees.description: Additional fees applied to this pricing variant.

fixedAmountOptions.description: Fixed monetary amount for the fee.

priceType.description: Pricing type used for this fee.

name.description: Fee name displayed to customers, such as "Setup Fee" or "Processing Fee".

appliedAt.description: When this fee is charged during the customer's plan lifecycle.

billingTerms.description: Billing configuration that defines when and how often customers are charged.

cyclesCompletedDetails.description: How many billing cycles the plan lasts.

billingCycleCount.description: Number of billing cycles before the plan automatically ends. For example, if `billingCycle` is 3 months and `billingCycleCount` is 4, the customer will be charged 4 times over 12 months before the plan expires. Only applicable if `endType` is `CYCLES_COMPLETED`.

billingCycle.description: Duration of each billing cycle, such as 1 month or 2 weeks. Can't be less than 7 days. Only applicable for recurring plans.

endType.description: How long the plan remains active. Plans can run until canceled or for a specific number of billing cycles. Plan duration can't exceed 10 years.

promotion.description: Promotional message displayed with this pricing variant.

pricingStrategies.description: Pricing strategies that determine how much customers pay. Currently limited to 1 strategy per variant.

flatRate.description: Single fixed cost charged regardless of usage.

visible.description: Whether this pricing variant is visible to customers. Defaults to `true` when not set. At least one variant per plan must remain visible. Variant-level visibility is independent from plan-level visibility (`Plan.visibility`).

categoryIds.description: IDs of the categories this variant belongs to. Categories group variants across plans (for example into a "Monthly / Yearly" selector) independently of billing cycle. Optional.

priceOverrides.description: Rules that override this pricing variant's price for purchases that meet their conditions. Applied during purchase. An override that matches the purchase always replaces the variant's original price, even when the resulting price is higher. If multiple overrides match the same purchase, the lowest resulting price among them wins - the original price doesn't participate in this comparison. The overridden price applies to every billing cycle of the resulting subscription, not only the first payment. Updates replace the entire list of overrides. To remove all overrides, set this field to `null` - an empty overrides list isn't accepted.

id.description: Price override GUID. Must be unique within the pricing variant.

conditions.description: Conditions a purchase must meet for this override to apply.

overrideType.description: How the pricing variant's price is overridden.

feeOverrides.description: Rules that override specific fees of this pricing variant for purchases that meet their conditions. Applied during purchase. If multiple overrides apply to the same fee, the lowest resulting fee amount wins, with a waived fee counting as `0`. Updates replace the entire list of overrides. To remove all overrides, set this field to `null` - an empty overrides list isn't accepted.

id.description: Fee override GUID. Must be unique within the pricing variant.

feeId.description: GUID of the fee on the same pricing variant that this override applies to.

conditions.description: Conditions a purchase must meet for this override to apply.

perks.description: List of text snippets describing what the plan offers. For display purposes only.

visibility.description: Plan visibility. Determines whether the plan is returned to site visitors and site members.  Default: `PUBLIC`

formId.description: GUID of the form associated with the plan at checkout.

buyerCanCancel.description: Whether buyers can cancel their subscription to this plan.

purchaseLimits.description: Caps how many subscriptions buyers can have or the site can sell for this plan. When multiple types are present, all must pass (AND logic). Duplicate types are rejected by the server.

maxCount.description: The maximum number of subscriptions allowed.

benefitDistributionSettings.description: The settings of the benefit distribution for subscriptions to this plan

unit.description: Duration unit: DAY, WEEK, MONTH, YEAR

count.description: Amount of units. For example,  1 MONTH, 1 YEAR, 2 WEEKS, etc. Optional. Default is 1.

distributionStrategyType.description: The distribution strategy of the benefits for this subscription, which is used to determine how the benefits are distributed in each cycle.

startDateSettings.description: Settings that control when subscriptions to this plan start. Applied during purchase to calculate the subscription start date and validate customer-selected start dates. The settings apply only to pricing variants with a compatible `billing_terms.start_type`: `FIXED_DATE` and `DAY_OF_MONTH` apply to variants with the `ON_PURCHASE` start type, while `DATE_RANGE` applies to variants with the `CUSTOM` start type.

fixedDateOptions.description: Subscription starts on the earliest of the configured fixed dates that hasn't passed.

startDates.description: Dates on which a subscription can start. A purchase starts the subscription on the earliest listed date that hasn't passed in the site's time zone. A purchase made on one of the dates starts the subscription immediately. When every date has passed the plan can't be purchased and `start_date_unavailable_message` is displayed. Only the calendar date in the site's time zone is used, the time of day is ignored. Order doesn't matter. Dates must be unique.

dayOfMonthOptions.description: Subscription starts on a specific day of each month.

dayOfMonth.description: Day of the month the subscription starts. For months with fewer days, the subscription starts on the last day of the month. If the purchase happens on the configured day, the subscription starts on that same day. Only determines the subscription start date - subsequent billing cycles follow the pricing variant's `billing_terms.billing_cycle` from that start date.

dateRangeOptions.description: Customer selects a start date within a date range.

startDate.description: Date and time from which the customer can select the subscription start date. The selected start date must be on or after this exact instant.

endDate.description: Date and time until which the customer can select the subscription start date. If not set, the range is open-ended. The selected start date must be before this exact instant. Must be later than `start_date`.

type.description: How the subscription start date is determined.

startDateUnavailableMessage.description: Message displayed to customers when no start date is available. For example, when every fixed start date or the end of the date range has passed. Applicable only when `type` is `FIXED_DATE`, or `DATE_RANGE` with `date_range_options.end_date` set - in other configurations a start date is always available and the message is ignored.

tags.description: Tags that can be assigned to this plan for classification and filtering.

privateTags.description: Tags that require an additional permission in order to access them, normally not given to site members or visitors.

publicTags.description: Tags that are exposed to anyone who has access to the labeled entity itself, including site members and visitors.

extendedFields.description: Data extensions. Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/schema-plugins/about-schema-plugin-extensions.md).

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions.  Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md).

actions.name: query_plans
actions.description:
Query plans. Retrieves a list of plans, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting. Query plans runs with these defaults, which you can override: - `createdDate` is sorted in `ASC` order - `cursorPaging.limit` is `100`
To learn about working with queries, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language).

cursorPaging.description: Cursor token pointing to a page of results. Not used in the first request. Following requests use the cursor token and not `filter` or `sort`.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object.  Learn more about [filtering](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#filters).

sort.description: Sort object.  Learn more about [sorting](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#sorting).

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

actions.name: search_plans
actions.description: Search plans. Retrieves a list of plans that match the provided search query and optionally performs aggregations on the data queried.  To learn about working with queries, see [Search, Query and List Methods](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/get-started/search-query-and-list-methods.md).

cursorPaging.description: Cursor token pointing to a page of results. Not used in the first request. Following requests use the cursor token and not filter or sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object.  Learn more about [filtering](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#filters).

sort.description: Sort object.  Learn more about [sorting](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#sorting).

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

aggregations.description: Logical groupings of data into facets, with summaries for each facet. For example, use aggregations to allow site visitors to narrow down their search results by selecting specific categories.

value.description: Value aggregation

includeOptions.description: Options for including missing values

addToBucket.description: Can specify custom bucket name. Defaults are [string -> "N/A"], [int -> "0"], [bool -> "false"] ...

sortType.description: Should sort by number of matches or value of the field

sortDirection.description: Should sort in ascending or descending order

limit.description: How many aggregations would you like to return? Can be between 1 and 250. 10 is the default.

missingValues.description: Should missing values be included or excluded from the aggregation results. Default is EXCLUDE

buckets.description: List of range buckets, where during aggregation each entity will be placed in the first bucket where its value falls into based on provided range bounds

from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the range. Required if to is not given

to.description: Exclusive upper bound of the range. Required if from is not given

type.description: Define the operator for the scalar aggregation

interval.description: Interval for date histogram aggregation

nestedAggregations.description: Flattened list of aggregations, where each next aggregation is nested within previous one

value.description: Value aggregation

name.description: User-defined name of aggregation, should be unique, will appear in aggregation results

type.description: Type of aggregation, client must provide matching aggregation field below

fieldPath.description: Field to aggregate by, use dont notation to specify json path

name.description: User-defined name of aggregation, should be unique, will appear in aggregation results

type.description: Type of aggregation, client must provide matching aggregation field below

fieldPath.description: Field to aggregate by, use dot notation to specify json path

search.description: Free text to match in searchable fields.

mode.description: Defines how separate search terms in `expression` are combined

fields.description: Fields to search in. If empty - will search in all searchable fields. Use dot notation to specify json path

fuzzy.description: Flag if should use auto fuzzy search (allowing typos by a managed proximity algorithm)

timeZone.description: Time zone to adjust date-time-based filters and aggregations, in ISO 8601 (including offsets) or IANA time zone database (including time zone GUIDs) format.

actions.name: count_plans
actions.description: Count plans. Counts plans by the provided filter.  To learn about working with queries, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language).

filter.description: Filter object in the following format: `"filter" : { "fieldName1": "value1", "fieldName2":{"$operator":"value2"} }` Example of operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$startsWith`, `$contains`

mode.description: Defines how separate search terms in `expression` are combined

fields.description: Fields to search in. If empty - will search in all searchable fields. Use dot notation to specify json path

fuzzy.description: Flag if should use auto fuzzy search (allowing typos by a managed proximity algorithm)

actions.name: bulk_update_plan_tags
actions.description: Bulk update plan tags. Adds or removes tags on multiple plans.  Specify which tags to assign and which tags to unassign. A tag that appears in both the list to assign and the list to unassign is assigned. Tags that don't exist are ignored.

assignTags.description: Common object for tags. Should be used as in this example: message Foo { string id = 1; ... Tags tags = 5 }  example of taggable entity { id: "123" tags: { public_tags: { tag_ids:["11","22"] }, private_tags: { tag_ids: ["33", "44"] } } }

publicTags.description: Tags that are exposed to anyone who has access to the labeled entity itself, including site members and visitors.

planIds.description: IDs of plans whose tags to update.

unassignTags.description: Common object for tags. Should be used as in this example: message Foo { string id = 1; ... Tags tags = 5 }  example of taggable entity { id: "123" tags: { public_tags: { tag_ids:["11","22"] }, private_tags: { tag_ids: ["33", "44"] } } }

actions.name: bulk_update_plan_tags_by_filter
actions.description: Bulk update plan tags by filter. Asynchronously updates tags on multiple plans that match the provided filter criteria.  Specify which tags to assign and which tags to unassign. props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

actions.description: Query projects. Retrieves a list of projects, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting. Up to 100 projects can be returned per request.  The default `sort` is `id` in `ASC`.  To retrieve projects in the site-wide display order, as shown on the All Projects page, sort by `sortOrder` in `ASC`, then by `createdDate` in `DESC`, then by `id` in `ASC`. Projects without a `sortOrder` come first in that sort, newest first. Projects created before the field existed have no value until a one-time migration assigns one, so don't use this sort for a site until that migration has completed. actions.name: create_donation_campaign
actions.description: Create donation campaign. Creates a new donation campaign.  The campaign is created in an active state and can immediately accept donations.  > **Note:** Other than the fields marked as required, **one or both** of the following fields must be passed on create: > + `customAmountEnabled` > + `predefinedDonationAmounts`  To create multiple donation campaigns in a single call, use [Bulk Create Donation Campaigns](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/donations/donation-campaigns/bulk-create-donation-campaigns.md).

donationCampaign.description: A donation campaign represents a fundraising initiative that allows collecting donations for a specific cause or goal. Campaigns can be configured with various donation options, including one-time and recurring payments, predefined amounts, and campaign goals.  Use the Donation Campaigns API to create and manage donation campaigns on your site.

archived.description: Whether the donation campaign is archived and hidden from site visitors. Archived campaigns can't accept donations.  Default: `false`

coverImage.description: Cover image for the donation campaign.

url.description: Image URL.

customAmountEnabled.description: Whether donors can specify their own donation amount. If custom amounts are disabled, at least one predefined amount must be provided.  Default: `false`

customAmountOptions.description: Optional settings for custom donation amounts.

predefinedDonationAmounts.description: Predefined donation amounts.  Each amount can include an optional description explaining its impact. For example, "Feed 5 families for a week".

id.description: Predefined amount GUID. You must provide this GUID when creating or updating campaigns.

price.description: Donation amount.  Currently supports the site's default currency only.

description.description: Description explaining the impact of this donation amount. For example, "Feed 5 families for a week" or "Plant 10 trees".

targetAmount.description: Target fundraising amount.  Currently supports the site's default currency only.

endDate.description: Campaign end date in [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Combined_date_and_time_representations) format.  The behavior after this date is controlled by `acceptDonationsAfterEndDate`.

acceptDonationsAfterEndDate.description: Whether donations are accepted after `endDate`. This field is ignored if `endDate` is not set.  Default: `false`

acceptDonationsAfterGoal.description: Whether donations are accepted after reaching `targetAmount`.  Default: `true`

commentsEnabled.description: Whether donors can add comments to their donations.  Default: `false`

donationFrequencies.description: Donation frequencies available for this campaign.  At least one frequency must be specified.

askDonorCoverFee.description: Whether to ask donors during checkout if they want to add 2.9% to their donation to cover fees.  When `false`, fees are deducted from the donation amount, meaning the campaign receives less than the donor's original contribution.  When `true`, donors are presented with an option in the checkout UI to add a 2.9% fee on top of their donation. This fee helps offset processing costs, ensuring more of the original donation reaches the campaign. The donor always has the choice — they are never automatically charged the fee.  For recurring donations, if the donor opts to cover fees, the 2.9% fee is applied to each recurring payment (not just the first one).  > **Notes:** > + The 2.9% rate is fixed and cannot be customized by campaign owners. > + This feature works with all payment methods and currencies.  Default: `false`

actions.name: bulk_update_donation_campaigns
actions.description: Bulk update donation campaigns. Updates multiple donation campaigns in a single request.  Each update increments the campaign's `revision` by 1. To prevent conflicts, you must provide the current `revision` for each campaign in the request.  You can update campaign settings like payment options, goals, and frequencies while maintaining existing donation history.  To update a single donation campaign, use [Update Donation Campaign](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/donations/donation-campaigns/update-donation-campaign.md).

revision.description: Revision number, which increments by 1 each time the donation campaign is updated. To prevent conflicting changes, the current `revision` must be specified when updating the donation campaign.  Ignored when creating a donation campaign.

archived.description: Whether the donation campaign is archived and hidden from site visitors. Archived campaigns can't accept donations.  Default: `false`

coverImage.description: Cover image for the donation campaign.

url.description: Image URL.

customAmountEnabled.description: Whether donors can specify their own donation amount. If custom amounts are disabled, at least one predefined amount must be provided.  Default: `false`

customAmountOptions.description: Optional settings for custom donation amounts.

predefinedDonationAmounts.description: Predefined donation amounts.  Each amount can include an optional description explaining its impact. For example, "Feed 5 families for a week".

id.description: Predefined amount GUID. You must provide this GUID when creating or updating campaigns.

price.description: Donation amount.  Currently supports the site's default currency only.

description.description: Description explaining the impact of this donation amount. For example, "Feed 5 families for a week" or "Plant 10 trees".

targetAmount.description: Target fundraising amount.  Currently supports the site's default currency only.

endDate.description: Campaign end date in [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Combined_date_and_time_representations) format.  The behavior after this date is controlled by `acceptDonationsAfterEndDate`.

acceptDonationsAfterEndDate.description: Whether donations are accepted after `endDate`. This field is ignored if `endDate` is not set.  Default: `false`

acceptDonationsAfterGoal.description: Whether donations are accepted after reaching `targetAmount`.  Default: `true`

commentsEnabled.description: Whether donors can add comments to their donations.  Default: `false`

donationFrequencies.description: Donation frequencies available for this campaign.  At least one frequency must be specified.

askDonorCoverFee.description: Whether to ask donors during checkout if they want to add 2.9% to their donation to cover fees.  When `false`, fees are deducted from the donation amount, meaning the campaign receives less than the donor's original contribution.  When `true`, donors are presented with an option in the checkout UI to add a 2.9% fee on top of their donation. This fee helps offset processing costs, ensuring more of the original donation reaches the campaign. The donor always has the choice — they are never automatically charged the fee.  For recurring donations, if the donor opts to cover fees, the 2.9% fee is applied to each recurring payment (not just the first one).  > **Notes:** > + The 2.9% rate is fixed and cannot be customized by campaign owners. > + This feature works with all payment methods and currencies.  Default: `false`

actions.name: products_create_product
actions.description: Create product. Creates a product in the Marketplace.  Products must include all required fields for the specified types. The first image in `media.items` becomes the main image.

product.description: A product provided by a business partner and displayed in the Wix Marketplace.  Products can be of type DROPSHIPPING, WHOLESALE, or both. Wix users can discover and add these products to their stores.

providerInfo.description: Information about the business partner providing this product.

productId.description: Unique product identifier on the provider's platform.  This field serves as the external system's primary key for synchronization and prevents duplicate products from being created. Once set, you can't change this field.

productCreatedDate.description: Date and time the product was created on the provider's platform.  This field helps maintain the connection to the original product source. Once set, you can't change this field.

url.description: Product URL on the provider's platform.

visible.description: Whether the product is visible in the Marketplace.  Default: `true`

media.description: Product media.

items.description: Product images. The first image becomes the main image.

url.description: Image URL.

types.description: Business model types this product supports.

options.description: Product options that customers can choose from.  Options display available product variations like size and color to help buyers make purchase decisions. Currently, options are informational only and don't create separate inventory items or variants.  There are 2 predefined option types you can use: - `color`: Color choices for the product. Values should be standard color names. For example, `"Black"`, `"White"`, `"Yellow"`. - `size`: Size choices for the product. Values should be standard size labels. For example, `"S"`, `"M"`, `"L"`, `"XL"`.

name.description: Option name.  There are 2 predefined options you can use: - `color`: Represents color choices for the product. Values should be standard color names. For example, `"Black"`, `"White"`, `"Yellow"`. - `size`: Represents size choices for the product. Values should be standard size labels. For example, `"S"`, `"M"`, `"L"`, `"XL"`.

values.description: Available values for this option.  All values within a single option must be the same type. For example, an option can't mix `color` values with `text` values.

color.description: Color option with name, hex code, and sort order.

name.description: Color name.  For example, `"Black"` or `"Navy Blue"`. Use 'Multicolor' for mixed colors. When using 'Multicolor', do not provide a hex value.

hex.description: Hex color code.  For example, `"#000000"` for black. Omit for 'Multicolor'.

sortIndex.description: Zero-based index that hints at the display order of this color relative to the option's other values.  For best results, use contiguous values starting at `0` with no gaps. When omitted, the client determines the display order.

text.description: Text-based option value with display name and sort order. Use for all option types other than `"color"`. Mismatching option names and value types may cause the product to display incorrectly in the Marketplace.

name.description: Display name for this option value. For example, `"L"` for size or `"Cotton"` for material.

sortIndex.description: Zero-based index that hints at the display order of this value relative to the option's other values.  For best results, use contiguous values starting at `0` with no gaps. When omitted, the client determines the display order.

ribbonName.description: Promotional ribbon text displayed on the product.  For example, `"New Arrival"` or `"Bestseller"`.

brand.description: Brand name.

orderProcessingTime.description: Time required to process orders before shipping.

min.description: Minimum time in the range.

value.description: Numeric time value. For example, `2` for "2 days".

unit.description: Time unit for the value.

max.description: Maximum time in the range.

shippingDestinations.description: Countries and regions where this product can be shipped, with location-specific pricing and timing.

countrySelections.description: Indicates if shipping applies to selected countries or to all other regions.

minimumShippingCost.description: Minimum shipping cost to this destination in USD.

shippingTime.description: Expected shipping time to this destination.

minimumProductCost.description: Minimum Product Cost to the Shipping Location

inventory.description: Current inventory information including stock level tier, calculated as the sum of all variant quantities.  Providers update inventory by calling [Update Product](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/suppliers-hub/products/update-product.md) with the new `quantity`. The `tier` is computed automatically and changes to the tier trigger a Product Updated webhook with `inventory.tier` in the modified fields.

quantity.description: Exact inventory quantity across all variants.  When null, inventory hasn't been reported yet. A value of `0` means out of stock.

productOrigin.description: Country where the product is manufactured or originates from, in [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) format.

directCategories.description: List of categories that directly contain this product.  Each category's namespace must match at least one of the product's types. For example, if a product has type `DROPSHIPPING`, its categories must use `DROPSHIPPING_NAMESPACE`. Products with both `DROPSHIPPING` and `WHOLESALE` types can have categories from both namespaces.

namespace.description: The namespace of the category tree this assignment belongs to.

wholesaleOptions.description: Wholesale-specific configuration including tiered pricing and minimum order quantities.  Required when `types` includes `WHOLESALE`.

priceTiers.description: Tiered pricing based on order quantity ranges.  Price tiers must be continuous with no gaps in quantity ranges. For example, if tier 1 covers quantities 1-100, tier 2 must start at 101. The system validates tier continuity when creating or updating products.

priceFrom.description: Minimum price for this quantity tier in USD.  If `priceTo` isn't specified, this price applies to all quantities in the tier.

priceTo.description: Maximum price for this quantity tier in USD.  Optional for fixed-price tiers.

countFrom.description: Minimum quantity for this price tier, inclusive.

countTo.description: Maximum quantity for this price tier, inclusive.  If not specified, this tier applies to all quantities greater or equal to `countFrom`.

minimumOrderQuantity.description: Minimum quantity required for wholesale orders.

supplierInfo.description: Information about the supplier including name, rating, and trust status.

id.description: Supplier GUID.  When provided, references a supplier in the Marketplace Supplier service. The system automatically retrieves and populates the supplier's name, rating, and verification status.

printOnDemandOptions.description: Print-on-demand-specific configuration including supported print technologies and mockup assets.  Required when `types` include `PRINT_ON_DEMAND`.

printTechnologies.description: Set of possible print technologies for the Product

description.description: Text description of the size guide

imageDescription.description: Text description of the image content

category.description: What is measured, e.g. chest, waist, sleeve

dropshippingOptions.description: Configuration specific to dropshipping products.  Required when `types` includes `DROPSHIPPING`, and not allowed otherwise.

salesVolume.description: Total number of units the supplier has sold for this product across all sales channels.  Provide this value when creating or updating a dropshipping product. It's write-only: the Marketplace uses it internally and never returns it in responses.
