actions.name: products_query_products
actions.description: Query products. Retrieves a list of products with filtering, sorting, and cursor-based pagination.  Provides real-time, strongly consistent results with filtering, sorting, and pagination.  Use Query Products when you need accurate, up-to-date data such as for operational tasks or inventory checks. For product discovery and browsing with full-text search capabilities, use [Search Products](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/suppliers-hub/products/search-products.md) instead.

cursorPaging.description: Cursor token pointing to a page of results. Not used in the first request. Following requests use the cursor token and not `filter` or `sort`.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object in the following format: `"filter" : { "fieldName1": "value1", "fieldName2":{"$operator":"value2"} }` Example of operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$startsWith`, `$contains`

sort.description: Sort object in the following format: `[{"fieldName":"sortField1","order":"ASC"},{"fieldName":"sortField2","order":"DESC"}]`

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

selectItemsBy.description: Filters to specify which element to use for sorting when `fieldName` refers to a repeated field marked as `MATCH_ITEMS`.  These filters ensure the correct element is selected from the collection for sorting. Multiple filters are combined using the `AND` operator.  For example, for a document like `{"id": "1", "nestedField": [{"price": 10, "region": "EU"}, {"price": 20, "region": "US"}]}`, if `nestedField` is marked as `MATCH_ITEMS`, sorting by price in the US region requires: `{fieldName: "nestedField.price", "selectItemsBy": [{"nestedField.region": "US"}]}`.

actions.name: products_search_products
actions.description: Search products. Retrieves a list of products, given the provided filtering, search expression, sorting, and cursor paging.  Provides eventually consistent results optimized for product discovery and browsing. Search supports full-text queries, filters, sorting, and aggregations for faceted search.  Use Search Products for user-facing product catalogs and discovery features. For real-time accuracy in operational tasks, use [Query Products](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/suppliers-hub/products/query-products.md) instead.

cursorPaging.description: Cursor pointing to page of results. When requesting 'cursor_paging.cursor', no `filter`, `sort` or `search` can be provided.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: A filter object. See documentation [here](https://bo.wix.com/wix-docs/rnd/platformization-guidelines/api-query-language#platformization-guidelines_api-query-language_defining-in-protobuf)

sort.description: Sort object in the form [{"fieldName":"sortField1"},{"fieldName":"sortField2","direction":"DESC"}]

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

selectItemsBy.description: Filters to specify which element to use for sorting when `fieldName` refers to a repeated field marked as `MATCH_ITEMS`.  These filters ensure the correct element is selected from the collection for sorting. Multiple filters are combined using the `AND` operator.  For example, for a document like `{"id": "1", "nestedField": [{"price": 10, "region": "EU"}, {"price": 20, "region": "US"}]}`, if `nestedField` is marked as `MATCH_ITEMS`, sorting by price in the US region requires: `{fieldName: "nestedField.price", "selectItemsBy": [{"nestedField.region": "US"}]}`.

For example, for a document like `{"id": "1", "nestedField": [{"price": 10, "region": "EU"}, {"price": 20, "region": "US"}]}`, if `nestedField` is marked as `MATCH_ITEMS`, sorting by price in the US region requires: `{fieldName: "nestedField.price", "selectItemsBy": [{"nestedField.region": "US"}]}`.

actions.name: create_gift_card

Gift card codes can be custom-provided or automatically generated by the system. When notification info is included, the gift card can be sent via email to recipients with personalized messaging.

name.description: Display name shown in the gift card email.

actions.name: ricos_documents_generate_file_download_url
actions.description: Generate file download url. Generates a temporary URL for downloading the file referenced by a file node in a Ricos document.  Specify the file node's `fileData.src.id` as `fileId`. The returned URL downloads the original file as an attachment and expires after 10 hours. Private files are supported, so you can use this method to let site visitors download files that aren't publicly accessible.  The method doesn't check whether the file appears in a specific document. Any file of the site can be retrieved by its GUID, so control which file GUIDs you expose to site visitors in your app.  If the file doesn't exist, the method fails with a `MEDIA_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` error.

fileId.description: GUID of the file, as specified in the file node's `fileData.src.id`.  Can include a path prefix. For example, `ugd/1a2b3c_4d5e6f.pdf` and `1a2b3c_4d5e6f.pdf` refer to the same file.

actions.name: ricos_documents_generate_file_upload_url
actions.description: Generate file upload url. Generates a URL for uploading a file to the site's Media Manager, so you can add the file to a Ricos document.  To upload the file, send a `PUT` request to `uploadUrl` with the file content as the request body and a `Content-Type` header that matches `mimeType`. If you didn't specify `fileName`, add the file name as the `filename` query parameter. For example, `PUT {uploadUrl}?filename=report.pdf`. The URL expires after 24 hours. Learn more about the [Upload API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/upload-api.md). To approve multiple members, call [Bulk Approve Members](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/members-contacts/members/member-management/members/bulk-approve-members.md).  To block a member, call [Block Member](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/members-contacts/members/member-management/members/block-member.md).

actions.name: block_member
actions.description: Block member. Blocks a member.  A blocked member can't log in to members-only pages.  To block multiple members, call [Bulk Block Members](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/members-contacts/members/member-management/members/bulk-block-members.md).  To unblock a member, call [Approve Member](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/members-contacts/members/member-management/members/approve-member.md).

actions.name: bulk_approve_members
actions.description: Bulk approve members. Changes status of multiple members to `"APPROVED"`, and gives access to members-only pages.  Call this API to: - Approve pending members. - Unblock blocked members.  To approve a single member, call [Approve Member](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/members-contacts/members/member-management/members/approve-member.md).

actions.description: Delete member addresses. Clears a member's street addresses.  Members are typically associated with a contact, each having a distinct member GUID and contact GUID. actions.name: delete_member_emails
actions.description: Delete member emails. Clears a member's email addresses.  Members are typically associated with a contact, each having a distinct member GUID and contact GUID. When specifying the GUID as a parameter, don't presume the GUIDs are identical since they represent separate entities.  > Note: A member can still log in with their `loginEmail`, which is not cleared when this method is called.

actions.name: delete_member_phones
actions.description: Delete member phones. Clears a member's phone numbers.  Members are typically associated with a contact, each having a distinct member GUID and contact GUID. When specifying the GUID as a parameter, don't presume the GUIDs are identical since they represent separate entities.

actions.name: disconnect_member
actions.description: Disconnect member. Disconnects a member.  A disconnected member can't log in to members-only pages, isn't visible in the dashboard, and their `status` changes to `OFFLINE`.  Use this when you want to permanently remove access without deleting member data.  >**Note:** This action is irreversible. To connect the same member again, you have to create a member with a new slug.

actions.name: join_community
actions.description: Join community. Joins the current member to the site community and sets their profile to public. actions.name: leave_community
actions.description: Leave community. Removes the current member from the site community and sets their profile to private. actions.description: Mute member. Mutes a member.  Muted members can't engage with a community. For example, they can't leave comments, like posts or comments, or share content.  You can mute members in [Wix Blog](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/blog/introduction.md) and [Wix Forum](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/forum/introduction.md). actions.name: query_member_abouts
actions.description: Query member abouts. Retrieves a list of content from the "About" sections, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting. Query Member Abouts runs with these defaults, which you can override: - `createdDate` is sorted in `ASC` order - `paging.limit` is `100` - `paging.offset` is `0`  To learn about working with _Query_ endpoints, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md), [Sorting and Paging](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/sorting-and-paging.md), and [Field Projection](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/field-projection.md).

limit.description: Number of items to load.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  You can get the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object in the following format: `"filter" : { "fieldName1": "value1", "fieldName2":{"$operator":"value2"} }` Example of operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$startsWith`, `$contains`

sort.description: Sort object in the following format: `[{"fieldName":"sortField1","order":"ASC"},{"fieldName":"sortField2","order":"DESC"}]`

When calling Get Contact for a merged contact, you can use the source or target contact GUID. In both bases, the target contact is returned.  This is supported only when calling Get Contact on merged contacts. Previously deleted source contact GUIDs can't be used for any other method.

fields.description: List of projected fields to return. If both `fields` and `fieldsets` are sent in the request, the union of both lists is returned. `id` and `revision` are always returned.  Supported properties: `source`, `createdDate`, `updatedDate`, `lastActivity`, `primaryInfo`, `info.name`, `info.emails`, `info.phones`, `info.addresses`, `info.company`, `info.jobTitle`, `info.picture`, `info.birthdate`, `info.locale`, `info.labelKeys`, `info.locations`, `info.extendedFields`

fieldsets.description: Predefined sets of fields to return. If both `fields` and `fieldsets` are sent in the request, the union of both lists is returned.  - `BASIC`: Returns `id`, `revision`, `primaryInfo`, `info.name`. - `COMMUNICATION_DETAILS`: Returns `id`, `revision`, `primaryInfo`, `info.name`, `info.emails`, `info.phones`, `info.addresses`. - `EXTENDED`: Returns `id`, `revision`, `primaryInfo`, `info.name`, `info.extendedFields`. - `FULL`: Returns all fields.  Default: If `fields` is omitted from the request, `FULL`.

actions.name: delete_contact
actions.description: Delete contact. Deletes a contact.  Deleting a contact permanently removes it from the contact list. If a contact is also a site member or Wix user, or has a valid billing subscription, the contact can't be deleted. The related site member or Wix user must first be deleted and any valid billing subscriptions must be canceled, before the contact can be deleted.  Members are typically linked to contacts, and while they share a relationship, the member GUID and contact GUID are distinct identifiers. Make sure to specify the contact GUID when calling Delete Contact.

actions.name: update_contact
actions.description: Update contact. Updates a contact.  Each time the contact is updated, `revision` increments by 1. The existing `revision` must be included when updating the contact. This ensures you're working with the latest contact information, and it prevents unintended overwrites.  You can't call Update Contact to update the `primaryEmail` of a contact who is also a member. Instead, use the Members API to update the member's login email, which will also update the contact's primary email.  Members are typically linked to contacts, and while they share a relationship, the member GUID and contact GUID are distinct identifiers. Make sure to specify the contact GUID when calling Update Contact.  >**Note:...

allowDuplicates.description: Controls whether the call will succeed if the new contact information contains an email or a phone number already used by another contact.  If set to `true`, the call will succeed even if an email address or phone number is used by another contact. If set to `false`, the call will fail if the given email address is used by another contact or, if the email address is not given and the given phone number is used by another contact.  Default: `false`

Merging contacts has the following effects on the target contact:  - No target contact data is overwritten or deleted. - Arrays (emails, phone numbers, addresses, and labels) from the source contacts are added to the target contact's arrays. - If you merge more than one source contact, the 1st source contact specified is added first, then the 2nd, and so on. - If there is duplicate information between the target contact and the source contact, the information isn't duplicated in the target contact's arrays.  <blockquote class="important">  __Important:__ Merges cannot be undone. contact.description: A contact represents a person in a site's contact list. It stores profile details such as name, email addresses, phone numbers, and addresses, and can optionally be linked to a site member.

externalId.description: Contact external GUID. Used to identify contacts from external systems. This field can only be set once and can't be updated after creation.

name.description: Contact's name information including first and last name.

email.description: The main email of the contact with subscription status and deliverability information. This email is used for contact matching and deduplication logic.
Main email address for the contact. Used for communication and contact matching.  Stored in normalized form: leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and the address is lowercased.

additionalEmails.description: Additional emails of the contact. These emails do not affect subscription status or contact matching/deduplication. The main email field must be set before additional emails can be added.

email.description: Additional email address for the contact. Does not affect subscription status or contact matching logic.

phone.description: The main phone of the contact with subscription status and deliverability information. This phone is used for contact matching and deduplication logic. At least one of name, email, or phone is required for contact creation.

tag.description: Phone type classification. Helps categorize the phone number's purpose.  Default: `OTHER`

phone.description: Primary phone number for the contact. Used for communication and contact matching.

additionalPhones.description: Additional phones of the contact. These phones do not affect subscription status or contact matching/deduplication. The main phone field must be set before additional phones can be added.

tag.description: Phone type classification for the additional phone number.  Default: `OTHER`

phone.description: Additional phone number for the contact. Does not affect subscription status or contact matching logic.

addresses.description: Contact's physical addresses. Each address can be tagged (HOME, WORK, BILLING, SHIPPING, OTHER) and one can be set as default. If no address is marked as default, the first address automatically becomes the default.

tag.description: Address type classification. Helps categorize the address purpose.  Default: `OTHER`

address.description: Physical address information including street, city, country, and postal code. Contains structured address data following common address formatting standards.

streetAddress.description: Street address object, with number and name in separate fields.

formattedAddressLine.description: Optional formatted version of the street address line.

addressLine.description: Main address line, usually street and number, as free text.

subdivision.description: Subdivision shorthand. Usually, a short code (2 or 3 letters) that represents a state, region, prefecture, or province. For example, `NY`.

addressLine2.description: Free text providing more detailed address information, such as apartment, suite, or floor.

formattedAddress.description: Human-readable address string. If not provided, the value is generated from the available address data.

hint.description: Instructions to help someone find the address, such as landmarks or where the entrance is.

subdivisions.description: Hierarchical list of subdivisions, where the first array item is the highest level of hierarchy, and so on.

typeInfo.description: Free text description of subdivision type. Examples: `"state"`, `"province"`, `"prefecture"`.

defaultAddress.description: Whether this address is the contact's default address. Only one address can be designated as default per contact. If no address is explicitly set as default, the first address automatically becomes the default.

recipient.description: Address recipient information for delivery purposes.

company.description: Contact's company information including company name and job title.

locale.description: Locale in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. Typically, this is a lowercase 2-letter language code, followed by a hyphen, followed by an uppercase 2-letter country code. For example, `en-US` for U.S. English, and `de-DE` for Germany German.

birthdate.description: Birth date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. For example, `2020-03-15`.

Upsert modes: Set `upsertMode` to control how an existing contact is updated: - `OVERWRITE` (default): Replaces existing field values. - `APPEND`: Sets a non-array field only if it doesn't already have a value, and appends to array fields. - `OVERWRITE_APPEND_ARRAYS`: Overwrites non-array fields and appends to array fields. ...

contact.description: A contact represents a person in a site's contact list. It stores profile details such as name, email addresses, phone numbers, and addresses, and can optionally be linked to a site member.

externalId.description: Contact external GUID. Used to identify contacts from external systems. This field can only be set once and can't be updated after creation.

name.description: Contact's name information including first and last name.

email.description: The main email of the contact with subscription status and deliverability information. This email is used for contact matching and deduplication logic.
Main email address for the contact. Used for communication and contact matching.  Stored in normalized form: leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and the address is lowercased.

additionalEmails.description: Additional emails of the contact. These emails do not affect subscription status or contact matching/deduplication. The main email field must be set before additional emails can be added.

email.description: Additional email address for the contact. Does not affect subscription status or contact matching logic.

phone.description: The main phone of the contact with subscription status and deliverability information. This phone is used for contact matching and deduplication logic. At least one of name, email, or phone is required for contact creation.

tag.description: Phone type classification. Helps categorize the phone number's purpose.  Default: `OTHER`

phone.description: Primary phone number for the contact. Used for communication and contact matching.

additionalPhones.description: Additional phones of the contact. These phones do not affect subscription status or contact matching/deduplication. The main phone field must be set before additional phones can be added.

phone.description: Additional phone number for the contact. Does not affect subscription status or contact matching logic.

addresses.description: Contact's physical addresses. Each address can be tagged (HOME, WORK, BILLING, SHIPPING, OTHER) and one can be set as default. If no address is marked as default, the first address automatically becomes the default.

tag.description: Address type classification. Helps categorize the address purpose.  Default: `OTHER`

address.description: Physical address information including street, city, country, and postal code. Contains structured address data following common address formatting standards.

streetAddress.description: Street address object, with number and name in separate fields.

formattedAddressLine.description: Optional formatted version of the street address line.

addressLine.description: Main address line, usually street and number, as free text.

subdivision.description: Subdivision shorthand. Usually, a short code (2 or 3 letters) that represents a state, region, prefecture, or province. For example, `NY`.

addressLine2.description: Free text providing more detailed address information, such as apartment, suite, or floor.

formattedAddress.description: Human-readable address string. If not provided, the value is generated from the available address data.

hint.description: Instructions to help someone find the address, such as landmarks or where the entrance is.

subdivisions.description: Hierarchical list of subdivisions, where the first array item is the highest level of hierarchy, and so on.

typeInfo.description: Free text description of subdivision type. Examples: `"state"`, `"province"`, `"prefecture"`.

defaultAddress.description: Whether this address is the contact's default address. Only one address can be designated as default per contact. If no address is explicitly set as default, the first address automatically becomes the default.

recipient.description: Address recipient information for delivery purposes.

company.description: Contact's company information including company name and job title.

locale.description: Locale in [IETF BCP 47 language tag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format. Typically, this is a lowercase 2-letter language code, followed by a hyphen, followed by an uppercase 2-letter country code. For example, `en-US` for U.S. English, and `de-DE` for Germany German.

birthdate.description: Birth date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. For example, `2020-03-15`.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone identifier for the contact's location. Valid values are IANA time zone GUIDs, such as 'Europe/Rome' or 'America/New_York'.

assigneeId.description: Site contributor user GUID assigned to manage communication with this contact. Must be a valid GUGUID referencing an existing site contributor. Only one assignee can be set per contact.

locationIds.description: List of business location GUIDs associated with this contact. Used for multi-location businesses to organize contacts by physical business locations. Each GUID must be a valid GUGUID referencing an existing business location.

image.description: Contact's profile image. If the contact is also a site member, clients should prefer to view `member_info.profile_info.photo` when it exists, as it reflects the member's current profile photo.

url.description: Image URL. The URL is valid until the date in `urlExpirationDate`.

source.description: Details about the origin of the contact. This field is immutable and set automatically when the contact is created.

additionalInfo.description: Additional information about the contact's origin or creation context.

tags.description: Tags assigned to the contact for organization and filtering.

privateTags.description: Tags that require an additional permission to access, normally not given to site members or visitors.

tagIds.description: A list of tag GUIDs. To create a tag, use the [Tags API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/tags/introduction.md) with the contacts FQDN: `wix.contacts.*.contact`.

extendedFields.description: Extended fields for storing custom contact data beyond the standard fields. Allows adding custom properties specific to business needs. To define a custom extended field, use the [Schema Service API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/data-extension-schema/about-the-data-extension-schema-api.md) with the contacts FQDN: `wix.contacts.*.contact`.

identifier.description: Identification for the field, describing its purpose. For example, `TEXT_INPUT` or `CONTACTS_EMAIL`.  Set this to the known value for the kind of field you're creating. Wix accepts an unrecognized value, such as a custom string or a GUID: the request succeeds, and Wix stores the field, returns it in `formFields`, and accepts its submissions. But Wix apps use `identifier` to recognize a field, so the Wix Forms editor doesn't render it, and the Wix user can't see or edit that field. A form whose fields all carry unrecognized identifiers opens empty in the editor. Always map a field onto a known identifier, and set its display name with the component's label.  Several fields share a general-purpose `componentType`, so `identifier` is often the only value that distinguishes them. For example, both a short answer field and a long answer field use the `TEXT_INPUT` component, and are told apart by their `TEXT_INPUT` and `TEXT_AREA` identifiers. identifier.description: Identification for the field, describing its purpose. For example, `TEXT_INPUT` or `CONTACTS_EMAIL`.  Set this to the known value for the kind of field you're creating. Wix accepts an unrecognized value, such as a custom string or a GUID: the request succeeds, and Wix stores the field, returns it in `formFields`, and accepts its submissions. But Wix apps use `identifier` to recognize a field, so the Wix Forms editor doesn't render it, and the Wix user can't see or edit that field. A form whose fields all carry unrecognized identifiers opens empty in the editor. Always map a field onto a known identifier, and set its display name with the component's label.  Several fields share a general-purpose `componentType`, so `identifier` is often the only value that distinguishes them. For example, both a short answer field and a long answer field use the `TEXT_INPUT` component, and are told apart by their `TEXT_INPUT` and `TEXT_AREA` identifiers.  For the full list of known values, see [About Form Fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/forms/form-schemas/about-form-fields.md).

Set `namespace` to the app that owns the forms, `wix.form_app.form` for the Wix Forms app. A first-page query without a namespace fails with `namespace filter is required`. contactMapping.description: Mapping configuration for automatically saving field values to contact properties.  When specified, form submissions automatically create or update contacts with the field data.

contactField.description: The [Contact](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/crm/members-contacts/contacts/contacts/introduction.md) field that this form field maps to.

readOnly.description: Whether the field is read-only.  Default: `false`

displayOptions.description: Configuration for display fields that show information without collecting input.

richContentOptions.description: Configuration for rich content display fields.

richContent.description: Rich content to display in the field.

maxShownParagraphs.description: Maximum number of paragraphs to show initially. Additional content is hidden behind an expandable section. If not specified, all content is visible.

pageNavigationOptions.description: Configuration for page navigation display fields such as navigation or submit buttons.

nextPageText.description: Text displayed on the button when it navigates to the next page. Only applicable when the button is not on the final form page.

previousPageText.description: Text displayed on the button when it navigates to the previous page. Only applicable when the button is not on the first form page.

submitText.description: Text displayed on the button when it submits the form. Only applicable when the button is on the final form page.

displayFieldType.description: Type of display field that determines its appearance and behavior.

id.description: Field GUID.  The GUID is stored in lowercase. Because the form's layout references each field by this GUID, pass a lowercase GUGUID so that `id` and the layout's `fieldId` still match after the form schema is stored. GUIDs must be unique in the form.

hidden.description: Whether the field is hidden from submitters.  Default: `false`

identifier.description: Identification for the field, describing its purpose. For example, `TEXT_INPUT` or `CONTACTS_EMAIL`.  Set this to the known value for the kind of field you're creating. Wix accepts an unrecognized value, such as a custom string or a GUID: the request succeeds, and Wix stores the field, returns it in `formFields`, and accepts its submissions. But Wix apps use `identifier` to recognize a field, so the Wix Forms editor doesn't render it, and the Wix user can't see or edit that field. A form whose fields all carry unrecognized identifiers opens empty in the editor. Always map a field onto a known identifier, and set its display name with the component's label.  Several fields share a general-purpose `componentType`, so `identifier` is often the only value that distinguishes them. For example, both a short answer field and a long answer field use the `TEXT_INPUT` component, and are told apart by their `TEXT_INPUT` and `TEXT_AREA` identifiers.  For the full list of known values, see [About Form Fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/forms/form-schemas/about-form-fields.md).

Every field in `formFields`, including the submit button, must be placed by a layout item whose `fieldId` matches the field's `id`. A field that isn't placed still stores submitted values, but the Wix dashboard renders it, and the submissions made against it, as empty.  Use a single step unless the form is split across pages.

hidden.description: Whether the step is hidden.

layout.description: Layout configuration that defines how form fields are arranged within this step.

large.description: Layout configuration for large screen breakpoints (desktop).

items.description: Configuration for the layout of items in the breakpoint. Every field of the step must have exactly 1 corresponding item in each breakpoint that is defined.

columns.description: Number of columns in the layout grid.

rowHeight.description: Height of each row in the layout grid, measured in pixels.

margin.description: Margin spacing configuration for the form elements.

padding.description: Padding spacing inside form elements in pixels.

medium.description: Layout configuration for medium screen breakpoints (tablet).

small.description: Layout configuration for small screen breakpoints (mobile).

extendedFields.description: Data extensions for storing additional custom properties.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions.  Learn more about [extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md).

namespace.description: Unique identifier for the app that owns this form schema.  For example, for creating a form visible in the Wix Forms app, use `wix.form_app.form`, the namespace of the Wix Forms app, whose app GUID is `225dd912-7dea-4738-8688-4b8c6955ffc2`.  See a list of namespaces for [apps made by Wix](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/forms/form-schemas/introduction.md#namespaces-of-apps-made-by-wix) section. To retrieve the GUID for a Wix app, see [Apps Created By Wix](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/get-started/apps-created-by-wix.md).

limitationRule.description: Submission limits that can automatically disable the form when reached.

maxAllowedSubmissions.description: Limitation by submission count, disables form when a set amount of submissions is reached.

dateTimeDeadline.description: Limitation by submission date, disables form when a set date and time is reached.

submissionLimitPerUser.description: Limitation per user submission count, disables form when a set amount of submissions per user is reached.

spamFilterProtectionLevel.description: Level of spam protection applied to form submissions.  Default: `ADVANCED`

requiredIndicatorProperties.description: Configuration for how required field indicators are displayed to the submitter.

requiredIndicator.description: Type of visual indicator used to mark required fields.

requiredIndicatorPlacement.description: Position where the required indicator appears relative to the field title.

submitSettings.description: Configuration for actions taken after a form is successfully submitted.

thankYouMessageOptions.description: Configuration for displaying a thank you message after submission.

durationInSeconds.description: Duration in seconds before the thank you message automatically disappears. If set to 0, the message remains visible until manually dismissed.

richContent.description: Rich content message displayed to users after successful form submission.

redirectOptions.description: Configuration for redirecting submitters to a URL after submission.

redirectUrl.description: URL to which the user should be redirected after successfully submitting the form.

target.description: How the redirect URL should be opened in the browser.

popupOptions.description: Configuration for displaying a popup after submission.

popupId.description: GUID of the site popup to open after successful form submission.

submitSuccessAction.description: Action that's triggered after a form is successfully submitted.

disabledFormMessage.description: Message displayed to visitors when the form is disabled. This allows you to inform submitters why the form isn't available.

enabled.description: Whether the form is effectively active — `true` only when the user has not disabled the form **and** no system service has placed an `activationBlock` on it.  Writing `enabled: true` records the user's intent to activate the form, but the value read back may still be `false` if `activationBlock` is present (for example, a plan restriction is in effect). Once the block is lifted the form becomes active automatically without any additional write.  Default: `true`

name.description: Display name of the form schema.  Names are unique in a namespace. If the name you pass is already taken, the request still succeeds, and the form schema is stored under a numbered variation of that name instead of returning an error. formRules.description: Business logic rules that can modify form behavior based on user input or other conditions. These rules can show/hide fields, change validation, or trigger actions.

expression.description: Conditional expression that determines when this rule should be applied. The overrides defined in this rule are applied when this expression evaluates to true.  The root of the expression must be an `and` or `or` group. To evaluate a single condition, wrap it in a group with 1 condition.

and.description: Logical AND condition with 1 or more child conditions. All child conditions must be true.

conditions.description: List of conditions that must all evaluate to true.

or.description: Logical OR condition with 1 or more child conditions. At least 1 child condition must be true.

conditions.description: List of conditions where at least 1 must evaluate to true.

condition.description: Single condition to evaluate. Not supported as the root of a rule's expression.

target.description: Human readable identifier used to reference a field. Supports dot notation for nested properties. For example, `"address.city"`.

operator.description: Comparison operator to use for evaluating the condition.

value.description: Value to compare against the value in the target field.

overrides.description: Form modifications that are applied when the rule expression evaluates to true. Each override specifies how a form element should be changed.

entityType.description: Type of form element being modified by this override.

namespaceRule.description: Namespace rules are part of business logic of app owning namespace, have limited editing possibilities

tags.description: Tag GUIDs collections associated with the current entity.

privateTags.description: Tags that require an additional permission in order to access them, normally not given to site members or visitors.

tags.description: Tags that are exposed to anyone who has access to the labeled entity itself, including site members and visitors.

quizSettings.description: Quiz configuration for a scored form. passingScorePoints.description: Score required to pass the quiz (in points).

passingScorePercentage.description: Score required to pass the quiz as a percentage (0-100).

passingStatusOptions.description: Configuration for displaying only the pass/fail message.

passMessage.description: Message displayed when the user passes the quiz.

failMessage.description: Message displayed when the user fails the quiz.

scoreAndPassingStatusOptions.description: Configuration for displaying both the score and pass/fail message.

message.description: Rich-content message shown on the quiz result (confirmation) page, alongside any score or pass/fail status configured in `results_display`.

resultsDisplay.description: How to display quiz results in the confirmation page. Default: `DO_NOT_DISPLAY`

autoFillContact.description: Source used for contact autofill when filling form fields. Default: FORM_INPUT.

submissionAccess.description: Controls who can read submissions of this form beyond the standard permission.  Default: `OWNER_AND_COLLABORATORS`

Create submission. > **Note:** The Form Submission API only works with the Wix Forms app. Call [GetAppInstance](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/api-reference/app-management/apps/app-instance/get-app-instance.md) to confirm that the app named `wix_forms` is installed on the site.
Creates a new submission.

additionalMetadata.description: Optional metadata passed to SPI implementer, allowing clients to include additional business-specific data.

submission.description: Form submission that was created or retrieved.

formId.description: GUID of the form which the submission belongs to.

status.description: Status of the submission.  The status a submission is created with depends on the form's namespace and on whether the form collects payment, so read it from the response rather than assuming.  A submission for a form that collects payment starts as `PAYMENT_WAITING`. Otherwise, most namespaces record the submission immediately as `CONFIRMED`. Namespaces that need to complete another step first, such as taking payment for a pricing plan, create the submission as `PENDING` and confirm it later with Confirm Submission.  A `PENDING` submission isn't recorded yet, and is deleted automatically if it isn't confirmed in time.

submissions.description: Values the visitor submitted.  Each key is the `target` of a field in the form schema, which is the field's stable storage key rather than its GUID or label. Only keys matching a field target are accepted.  Each value's shape follows that field's `inputType`: `STRING` fields submit a string, `NUMBER` a number, `BOOLEAN` a boolean, and `ARRAY` an array of the selected option values. Date and time fields are strings. A choice field submits an option's `value`, not its GUID or its label.  3 input types submit structured values: `ADDRESS` submits an address object, `PAYMENT` an array holding 1 product object per item bought, and `SCHEDULING` an appointment object.  For the full mapping, see [About Submission Values](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/forms/form-submissions/about-submission-values.md).

submission.description: Form submission that was created or retrieved.

formId.description: GUID of the form which the submission belongs to.

status.description: Status of the submission.  The status a submission is created with depends on the form's namespace and on whether the form collects payment, so read it from the response rather than assuming.  A submission for a form that collects payment starts as `PAYMENT_WAITING`. Otherwise, most namespaces record the submission immediately as `CONFIRMED`. Namespaces that need to complete another step first, such as taking payment for a pricing plan, create the submission as `PENDING` and confirm it later with Confirm Submission.  A `PENDING` submission isn't recorded yet, and is deleted automatically if it isn't confirmed in time.

submissions.description: Values the visitor submitted.  Each key is the `target` of a field in the form schema, which is the field's stable storage key rather than its GUID or label. Only keys matching a field target are accepted.  Each value's shape follows that field's `inputType`: `STRING` fields submit a string, `NUMBER` a number, `BOOLEAN` a boolean, and `ARRAY` an array of the selected option values. Date and time fields are strings. A choice field submits an option's `value`, not its GUID or its label.  3 input types submit structured values: `ADDRESS` submits an address object, `PAYMENT` an array holding 1 product object per item bought, and `SCHEDULING` an appointment object.  For the full mapping, see [About Submission Values](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/forms/form-submissions/about-submission-values.md).

A form whose fields all carry unrecognized identifiers opens empty in the editor. Always map a field onto a known identifier, and set its display name with the component's label. For example, both a short answer field and a long answer field use the `TEXT_INPUT` component, and are told apart by their `TEXT_INPUT` and `TEXT_AREA` identifiers. actions.description: Query intake form submissions. Retrieves a list of intake form submissions, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting.  Submissions belonging to deleted intake forms aren't returned by Query Intake Form Submissions.  Query Intake Form Submissions runs with these defaults, which you can override:  - `createdDate` is sorted in `DESC` order. - `paging.limit` is `50`. - `paging.offset` is `0`.  Learn more about [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md).

actions.name: cancel_intake_form_submission
actions.description: Cancel intake form submission. Changes an intake form submission's status to `CANCELED`.  The submission remains in the system for record-keeping, but is no longer valid. You can't reactivate it, the contact must create a new submission to have a valid submission again.

actions.name: count_submissions_by_intake_form_ids
actions.description: Count submissions by intake form ids. Counts intake form submissions by form GUIDs.  Returns the total number of submissions per intake form.  If you include a deleted intake form GUID in the request, that form is omitted from the response.  Use this method for analytics, reporting, or checking if a form has submissions before deleting it.

actions.name: delete_intake_form_submission
actions.description: Delete intake form submission. Deletes an intake form submission.

actions.name: exempt_intake_form_submission
actions.description: Exempt intake form submission. Exempts a customer from having to submit an intake form. Creates a submission with `EXEMPT` status for the specified [contact](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/crm/members-contacts/contacts/contacts/introduction.md) and intake form.  Use this when you want to waive the form requirement for a contact so they count as compliant without filling out the form. For example, when approving all forms for a customer group such as VIPs or special circumstances.

fields.description: Additional fields to include in the response. Pass `INTAKE_FORM_INFO` to include `intakeFormInfo` in each returned submission.

actions.name: extend_intake_form_submission
actions.description: Extend intake form submission. Extends an intake form submission's expiration date.  The new expiration date is the time of the extend call plus the intake form's expiration period in months. If the submission had already expired, this also changes the status from `EXPIRED` back to `VALID`.

fields.description: Additional fields to include in the response. Pass `INTAKE_FORM_INFO` to include `intakeFormInfo` in each returned submission.

actions.name: list_intake_form_data_by_contacts
actions.description: List intake form data by contacts. Retrieves intake form data for specified contacts.  Returns both intake forms without submissions and the most recent submission per contact and form GUID. If you include a deleted intake form GUID in the request, that form is omitted from the response.  Call this method to see which forms each contact has submitted and which they haven't. You can use it for a single contact or many at once.

actions.name: list_form_templates
actions.description: List form templates. Retrieves the form templates in a namespace, optionally filtered by template GUIDs.  Templates are returned only for apps installed on the site, together with templates from apps made by Wix. If the app that owns the namespace isn't installed on the site, the response is empty.  Returned template content, such as field labels, is served in the language resolved from the request.

namespace.description: Namespace whose templates to retrieve. A namespace groups the templates and forms that belong to the same app or use case, such as a bookings or pricing plans checkout. The value is defined by the app that owns the templates in the app dashboard.

actions.name: get_restrictions
actions.description: Get restrictions. Retrieves the form limits and premium features in force for the site, and the number of forms it currently has.  Call Get Restrictions before creating or updating a form to check the change against the site's plan. A form that exceeds a limit, or that uses a feature absent from `restrictions.features`, is rejected. Compare `totalFormCount` with `restrictions.formsLimit` to check whether the site can add another form, and use each limit's `warnThreshold` to warn a site owner who is approaching it.  The limits come from the site's premium plan and change when the plan changes. When a plan change leaves a form over a limit, the form is disabled rather than deleted: it stops...

actions.name: bulk_moderate_draft_content

subscriptionStatus.description: Indicates the recipient's opt-in or opt-out status for marketing emails.  - `NOT_SET`: No status specified. This is the default, initial value before any info about the email address is known. - `PENDING`: Subscription confirmation was requested, but recipient hasn't confirmed yet. - `SUBSCRIBED`: Recipient has opted in to marketing emails. - `UNSUBSCRIBED`: Recipient has opted out of marketing emails.  Defaults to `NOT_SET`.

deliverabilityStatus.description: Indicates last reported status of sent emails.  - `NOT_SET`: No status specified. This is the default, initial value before any info about the email address is known. - `VALID`: Emails to this email address are being delivered successfully. - `BOUNCED`: The last email to the recipient bounced or was rejected. - `SPAM_COMPLAINT`: The recipient registered a spam complaint with their email provider. - `INACTIVE`: Multiple campaigns have been delivered to this address without any engagement from the recipient. (No emails were opened and no content was clicked.) This status might impact subsequent emails sent to this address.  Defaults to `NOT_SET`.

This is the default, initial value before any info about the email address is known. - `PENDING`: Subscription confirmation was requested, but recipient hasn't confirmed yet. - `SUBSCRIBED`: Recipient has opted in to marketing emails. - `UNSUBSCRIBED`: Recipient has opted out of marketing emails.  Defaults to `NOT_SET`.

deliverabilityStatus.description: Indicates last reported status of sent emails.  - `NOT_SET`: No status specified. This is the default, initial value before any info about the email address is known. - `VALID`: Emails to this email address are being delivered successfully. - `BOUNCED`: The last email to the recipient bounced or was rejected. - `SPAM_COMPLAINT`: The recipient registered a spam complaint with their email provider. - `INACTIVE`: Multiple campaigns have been delivered to this address without any engagement from the recipient. actions.name: adjust_points
actions.description: Adjust points. Adjusts the point balance of a loyalty account.  You can adjust the balance in two ways: - `balance` allows you to set the total points balance to this new amount. The transaction `type` will return as `"ADJUST"`. - `amount` allows you to adjust the points balance by this amount. This amount can be a positive number to increase the points balance or a negative number to decrease the balance. The transaction `type` will return as `"GIVE"`.  An account may not be adjusted to result in a negative balance. If you pass an integer in both the `balance` and the `amount` parameters then the `balance` adjustment takes effect and the `amount` adjustment is ignored.

accountId.description: The accountId

description.description: Description to explain the reason for the points adjustment.

revision.description: Each time the loyalty account is updated, `revision` increments by 1.  The current `revision` must be passed when adjusting points in the loyalty account. This ensures you're working with the latest version of the loyalty account and prevents unintended overwrites.

balance.description: Sets the account's point balance to this amount. Must be a positive, whole number or zero.  The net difference between this new balance and the previous balance will be reflected in the `adjusted` field of the customer's account.  Min: `0`  Max: `999999999`

amount.description: Adjusts the account's point balance by this amount. Must be a whole number with a maximum of 7 digits. The amount can be negative, but cannot be `0`.  Min: `-9999999`  Max: `9999999`

actions.name: bulk_adjust_points
actions.description: Bulk adjust points. Updates the points balance of multiple accounts.  You can adjust the balance in two ways: - `balance` allows you to set the total points balance to this new amount. The transaction `type` will return as `"ADJUST"`. - `amount` allows you to adjust the points balance by this amount. This amount can be a positive number to increase the points balance or a negative number to decrease the balance. The transaction `type` will return as `"GIVE"`.  You can use the job GUID from the response to call [Get Async Job](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/async-job/get-async-job.md) to retrieve the job details and metadata.

actions.name: create_account
actions.description: Create account. Creates a loyalty account for a site contact.  To create a new loyalty account, a customer must first be a site contact with a contact GUID, see the Contacts API. actions.name: earn_points
actions.description: Earn points. Adds points to a loyalty account.  Only a positive amount can be added using this method. To adjust an account's balance for a negative amount, use Adjust Points.  This method allows customers to manually earn points to their loyalty accounts. To use this method you must include an `appId` and an `idempotencyKey`. Any string can be set as the `appId` or `idempotencyKey`. In contrast to when an account earns points through an action taken on your site, then, the `appId` automatically sets to the source app that generates the points. In both cases, the transaction `type` is `"EARN"`.

accountId.description: The accountId

activityType.description: Activity type.  If points were earned through automation it should be set to the trigger key.

amount.description: Amount of points to earn. Must be a positive, whole number.  Min: `1`  Max: `9999999`

appId.description: GUID of the app that initiated the transaction.  If points were earned manually, then the `appId` is the Loyalty app's `wixAppId` of `553c79f3-5625-4f38-b14b-ef7c0d1e87df`. If points were earned in an automatic event, then the `appId` is from that automation's `sourceAppId`.

description.description: Description of how the points were earned.  Max: 100 characters

idempotencyKey.description: Unique string identifier generated by the app. Wix uses this identifier to recognize subsequent retries of the same request.  Please use `GUID` format.

limitApplied.description: Whether the points amount was adjusted by an earn points limit provider.

orderId.description: Order GUID which was source of this transaction.

actions.description: Get account by secondary id. Retrieves the account belonging to the specified contact or member.  This method retrieves loyalty accounts using either a customer's contact GUID or member GUID. You can also retrieve an account using the loyalty account GUID with Get Account.

actions.name: get_current_member_account

actions.name: get_program_totals
actions.description: Get program totals. Retrieves the total amount of points earned, redeemed, and adjusted for the entire loyalty program.  The `balance` is the current total of points outstanding, while the `earned`, `adjusted`, and `redeemed` amounts are the all-time accumulated amounts. The totals include the amounts for all loyalty accounts.

actions.description: Update widget settings. Updates widget settings.  Use this method to update specific settings fields. Only the fields specified in the field mask will be updated.

widgetSettings.description: Widget settings for the AI Site Chat (v2).  This version introduces mode-based configuration for chat handlers and enhanced scheduling options. It replaces the v1 widget settings.

activeHours.description: Times the AI assistant is available on the site with new mode-based configuration.

schedule.description: Array of time frames during which the AI assistant or Wix user are available to respond to site visitors. Only used when `mode` is `SCHEDULED`. Ignored for all other modes.

start.description: Start time of the active hours in milliseconds since midnight. For example, 9:00 AM = 32400000.

end.description: End time of the active hours in milliseconds since midnight. For example, 5:00 PM = 61200000.

timeZone.description: Time zone used for the schedule.

mode.description: Determines who responds to site visitors in the chat. Use `SCHEDULED` to define availability per time frame via the `schedule` field.

autoOpen.description: Whether to open the AI assistant automatically when the site loads.  When `true`, the widget will open automatically when a site visitor lands on the site. When `false`, the widget will remain closed until the visitor clicks to open it. This setting applies across all modes (AI active hours, Wix user active hours, and offline hours).

contactForm.description: Settings for the contact form.  The contact form will be shown to site visitors based on the timing settings in `WixUserBehavior` and `AIBehavior`, or when the chat is offline based on `OfflineBehavior`.  The contact form is shown only once per conversation.

fields.description: Contact form fields.

includeName.description: Whether to include a name field in the form.

includeEmail.description: Whether to include an email field in the form.

includePhone.description: Whether to include a phone number field in the form.

includeMessage.description: Whether to include a message field in the form.

requiredName.description: Whether the name field is required for submission.

requiredEmail.description: Whether the email field is required for submission.

requiredPhone.description: Whether the phone number field is required for submission.

requiredMessage.description: Whether the message field is required for submission.

introMessage.description: Message shown before the contact form.

successMessage.description: Message shown after the contact form is submitted.

aiBehavior.description: Defines how the AI assistant functions during AI active hours.  For instance, when WidgetSettings.active_hours.mode is set to ALWAYS_WITH_AI or SCHEDULED with a schedule that includes time frames with FrameHandler set to AI_CHAT, these settings will determine the behavior of the chat for site visitors during those hours.

includeNavigationSummary.description: Whether the AI assistant should send a summary of the site visitor's navigation on the site.

showContactFormWhenCannotAnswer.description: Whether the AI assistant should send the contact form if the AI is unable to answer the site visitor's question.

showContactFormWhenRequestForPerson.description: Whether the AI assistant should send the contact form if the site visitor requests to chat with a real person.

showContactFormBeforeChat.description: Whether the AI assistant should send the contact form before chat starts.

introduction.description: This is shown in the chat when a site visitor starts a new conversation.

enabled.description: Whether the message is enabled.

text.description: Message content.

engage.description: Message shown as popup to engage the site visitor with the AI assistant.

suggestions.description: Suggested questions shown to the site visitor to help them get started.

enabled.description: Whether suggesting questions is enabled.

questions.description: Suggested questions shown to the site visitor to help them get started.

introduction.description: Introduction message for the suggested questions.

displayWhenMinimized.description: Whether suggested questions should be displayed while the widget is minimized.

avatar.description: Wix Media image GUID used for the AI assistant.

offlineBehavior.description: Defines how the AI assistant functions during offline hours.  Valid field combinations: - `hide_widget: true` — hides the widget entirely. `show_contact_form` and `allow_chat` are ignored. - `hide_widget: false, allow_chat: false, show_contact_form: true` — shows a contact form only, no chat input. - `hide_widget: false, allow_chat: true, show_contact_form: false` — allows visitors to type messages with no contact form. - `hide_widget: false, allow_chat: true, show_contact_form: true` — shows the chat input and a contact form.

hideWidget.description: Hides the AI assistant widget from the site. When `true`, all other fields are ignored.

showContactForm.description: Shows a contact form to the site visitor when the chat is offline.

allowChat.description: Allows the site visitor to type and send messages when the chat is offline.

introduction.description: This is shown in the chat when a site visitor starts a new conversation.

allowFileUpload.description: Allows the site visitor to upload files when the chat is offline. This setting applies only to offline mode; file upload availability during AI or Wix user active hours is not configurable via this API.

wixUserBehavior.description: Defines how the AI assistant functions during Wix User active hours.  For instance, when WidgetSettings.active_hours.mode is set to ALWAYS_WITH_WIX_USER or SCHEDULED with a schedule that includes time frames with FrameHandler set to WIX_USER_CHAT, these settings will determine the behavior of the chat for site visitors during those hours.

contactFormBeforeChat.description: Show the contact form before starting a conversation.

contactFormOnFirstMessage.description: Show the contact form after the site visitor's first message.

introduction.description: This is shown in the chat when a site visitor starts a new conversation.

engage.description: Message shown as popup to engage the site visitor with the AI assistant.

avatar.description: Wix Media image GUID used for the AI assistant.

name.description: Display name shown for the Wix user in the chat.

faqQuestions.description: FAQ questions shown to the site visitor.

enabled.description: Whether FAQ questions are enabled.

introduction.description: Introduction message shown above the FAQ questions.

revision.description: Revision number, which increments by 1 each time the widget settings are updated. To prevent conflicting changes, the current revision must be passed when updating the widget settings.

socialButtons.description: Social buttons shown in the widget header, offering site visitors alternative channels to reach the site owner.

enabled.description: Whether the WhatsApp button is shown in the widget header.

phone.description: Phone number of the WhatsApp account to contact, in international format (e.g. "+12345678900").

infoText.description: Info text shown above the WhatsApp button when a site visitor opens it.

prefilledMessage.description: Message pre-filled into the WhatsApp chat when a site visitor opens it.

For example, let's say the Workflows `Card moved` trigger has 2 filters:  - Select a workflow, with filter GUID `466d2067-05bd-44f9-99c7-d029b93e4feb`. - Select a step, with filter GUID `b45f8475-bd44-4971-8820-7031ee12a708`. actions.name: create_branch

branch.description: A branch is a version of draft site content that can be edited independently. Also known as a test site.  Branches let site owners and developers create isolated versions of a site for testing changes without affecting the live site. Each branch maintains its own content, design, and settings while sharing the same site infrastructure.  Learn more about [branches](https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-test-sites).

branchRevision.description: Revision number of the source branch when this branch was created. To prevent conflicting changes, the current revision must be passed when updating the branch.

sourceType.description: Source type for this branch's content. Must be aligned with the corresponding source properties below.

editorType.description: Wix editor type. Provide this field only when the new branch uses a different editor than the branch it was created from, and the branch is not created from a template. Only `STUDIO_TWO` may be provided explicitly; otherwise the editor type is calculated automatically.

extendedFields.description: Custom field data for the branch. [Extended fields](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/extended-fields.md) must be configured in the app dashboard before they can be accessed with API calls.

namespaces.description: Extended field data. Each key corresponds to the namespace of the app that created the extended fields. The value of each key is structured according to the schema defined when the extended fields were configured.  You can only access fields for which you have the appropriate permissions. actions.name: events_v3_create_event
actions.description: Create event. Creates an event.   ### Required fields  What you need to provide depends on the type of event:  - **Single-occurrence event**, for example a vacation day or one-off time block: Only `event.scheduleId`, `event.start.localDate`, and `event.end.localDate` are required. Don't include `recurrenceRule`, omitting it creates a single-occurrence event. All other fields like `location`, `resources`, and `conferencingDetails` are optional. - **Recurring MASTER event**, for example weekly working hours: In addition to the fields above, you must also provide `recurrenceRule` with at least `frequency` and `days`. Currently only `WEEKLY` frequency is supported, and only a single day per e...

event.description: An event is a scheduled entry on a calendar that includes details like timing, location, and participants. Each event is associated with a [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/introduction.md), from which it may [inherit default values](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/default-values.md). Events can either be standalone, part of a recurring series, or define a recurrence pattern. You can also specify whether events block time on the schedule or allow other events to be scheduled concurrently.

scheduleId.description: GUID of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md) the event belongs to. After creating an event, you can't assign it to a different schedule.

type.description: Event type. You can set the event type but you can't update it.  Supported values: + `DEFAULT`: A standard event that's not further specified. + `WORKING_HOURS`: The event adds working hours to a schedule. By default not returned in [Query Events](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/events-v3/query-events.md). To retrieve working hour events, specify `"type": "WORKING_HOURS"` in the query filter. Additional supported values, if Wix Bookings is installed: + `APPOINTMENT`: Bookings appointment event. + `CLASS`: Bookings class event. + `COURSE`: Bookings course event.

title.description: Event title.  Min: 1 character Max: 200 characters

start.description: Information about when the event starts.

localDate.description: Local date time in [ISO-8601 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601). For example, `2024-01-30T13:30:00`. Wix Calendar APIs ignore seconds.

end.description: Information about when the event ends.  Maximum allowed date: Year 2100, or up to 100 years from the event's start date (whichever comes first).

timeZone.description: Time zone the event is associated with in [IANA tz database format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database). Only regional time zones and UTC are supported. For example, `America/New_York` or `UTC`.  Default: `timeZone` of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md).

allDay.description: Whether the event spans one or more full days.  When `true`, `start` and `end` represent full-day boundaries: + `start.localDate`: First day at `00:00:00`. + `end.localDate`: Day after the last day at `00:00:00` (exclusive). Midnight boundaries are interpreted in the event's `timeZone`.  Default: `false`

recurrenceRule.description: Recurrence pattern for a series of events. This field is required when creating a `MASTER` event and isn't available for non-recurring events. You can't update the recurrence rule for `INSTANCE` or `EXCEPTION` events.  For example, an event that repeats every second Monday until January 7, 2026, at 8:00 AM has the following `recurrenceRule`: - `frequency = WEEKLY` - `interval = 2` - `days = [MONDAY]` - `until = 20260107T08:00:00Z`

frequency.description: Frequency how often the event repeats. Works together with `interval`.  Supported values: + `WEEKLY`: The event's recurrence pattern is based on weeks.

interval.description: Interval how often the event repeats. Works together with `frequency`. For example, `frequency` set to `WEEKLY`  and `interval` set to `2` means the event repeats every 2 weeks.  Min: `1` Max: `4` Default: `1`

days.description: Days of the week when the recurring event takes place. Currently, only a single day is supported.  Min: 1 day Max: 1 day

until.description: Date until when the event repeats. If not specified, the event repeats forever.

transparency.description: Specifies whether the event blocks time in the schedule it belongs to.  Supported values: + `OPAQUE`:  The schedule is blocked during the event, preventing other events that involve the same entities (for example, Booking staff members) from being scheduled at the same time. + `TRANSPARENT`: The schedule remains open during the event, allowing other events to be scheduled concurrently.  Default: `OPAQUE`

location.description: Event location.  Default: `defaultLocation` of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md) the event belongs to

type.description: Location type.  Supported values: + `BUSINESS`: The event is held at a business location. + `CUSTOMER`: The event is held at the customer's location, such as their home or office. + `CUSTOM`: The event is held at an address or venue not tied to the business or customer.

name.description: Location name. For `BUSINESS` locations, it's identical to the [location](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/locations/location-object.md) `name`.  Min: 1 character Max: 150 characters

address.description: Location address. For `BUSINESS` locations, it's identical to the [location](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/locations/location-object.md)'s `formattedAddress`.

resources.description: List of [Wix Bookings resources](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/staff-members-and-resources/resource-v2/resource-object.md) affected by the event. This could include, for example, the [Wix Bookings staff member](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/staff-members-and-resources/staff-member-v1/staff-member-object.md) providing the service or the room where the appointment takes place.  Max: 100 resources

transparency.description: Specifies whether the event blocks time in the resource's schedule.  Supported values: + `OPAQUE`: The schedule is blocked during the event, preventing other events that involve the same resource from being scheduled at the same time. + `TRANSPARENT`: The schedule remains open during the event, allowing other events to be scheduled concurrently.  Default: `OPAQUE`.

totalCapacity.description: Maximum number of participants who can participate in the event.  Omit this field to inherit the schedule's `defaultCapacity`. Specifying it overrides that default, even when the value matches, and the event stops reflecting later changes to the schedule. Only specify it when a single event's capacity differs from the rest of the schedule. To change capacity for all of a schedule's future events, update the schedule's `defaultCapacity` instead. Some event types enforce capacity at the schedule level, where an event-level value doesn't affect bookability.  Default: `defaultCapacity` of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md) the event belongs to

actions.name: events_v3_update_event
actions.description: Update event. Updates an event.   When updating an event with `{"recurrenceType": "INSTANCE"}`, the `recurrenceType` automatically changes to `EXCEPTION`.  When updating an event with `{"recurrenceType": "MASTER"}`: + Past `INSTANCE` and `EXCEPTION` events remain unchanged. + For future `INSTANCE` events, all relevant fields are updated. + For future `EXCEPTION` events, only changes to the `inheritedFields` are applied, while other fields remain unchanged.

event.description: An event is a scheduled entry on a calendar that includes details like timing, location, and participants. Each event is associated with a [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/introduction.md), from which it may [inherit default values](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/default-values.md). Events can either be standalone, part of a recurring series, or define a recurrence pattern. You can also specify whether events block time on the schedule or allow other events to be scheduled concurrently.

scheduleId.description: GUID of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md) the event belongs to. After creating an event, you can't assign it to a different schedule.

type.description: Event type. You can set the event type but you can't update it.  Supported values: + `DEFAULT`: A standard event that's not further specified. + `WORKING_HOURS`: The event adds working hours to a schedule. By default not returned in [Query Events](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/events-v3/query-events.md). To retrieve working hour events, specify `"type": "WORKING_HOURS"` in the query filter. Additional supported values, if Wix Bookings is installed: + `APPOINTMENT`: Bookings appointment event. + `CLASS`: Bookings class event. + `COURSE`: Bookings course event.

title.description: Event title.  Min: 1 character Max: 200 characters

start.description: Information about when the event starts.

localDate.description: Local date time in [ISO-8601 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601). For example, `2024-01-30T13:30:00`. Wix Calendar APIs ignore seconds.

end.description: Information about when the event ends.  Maximum allowed date: Year 2100, or up to 100 years from the event's start date (whichever comes first).

timeZone.description: Time zone the event is associated with in [IANA tz database format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database). Only regional time zones and UTC are supported. For example, `America/New_York` or `UTC`.  Default: `timeZone` of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md).

allDay.description: Whether the event spans one or more full days.  When `true`, `start` and `end` represent full-day boundaries: + `start.localDate`: First day at `00:00:00`. + `end.localDate`: Day after the last day at `00:00:00` (exclusive). Midnight boundaries are interpreted in the event's `timeZone`.  Default: `false`

recurrenceRule.description: Recurrence pattern for a series of events. This field is required when creating a `MASTER` event and isn't available for non-recurring events. You can't update the recurrence rule for `INSTANCE` or `EXCEPTION` events.  For example, an event that repeats every second Monday until January 7, 2026, at 8:00 AM has the following `recurrenceRule`: - `frequency = WEEKLY` - `interval = 2` - `days = [MONDAY]` - `until = 20260107T08:00:00Z`

frequency.description: Frequency how often the event repeats. Works together with `interval`.  Supported values: + `WEEKLY`: The event's recurrence pattern is based on weeks.

interval.description: Interval how often the event repeats. Works together with `frequency`. For example, `frequency` set to `WEEKLY`  and `interval` set to `2` means the event repeats every 2 weeks.  Min: `1` Max: `4` Default: `1`

days.description: Days of the week when the recurring event takes place. Currently, only a single day is supported.  Min: 1 day Max: 1 day

until.description: Date until when the event repeats. If not specified, the event repeats forever.

transparency.description: Specifies whether the event blocks time in the schedule it belongs to.  Supported values: + `OPAQUE`:  The schedule is blocked during the event, preventing other events that involve the same entities (for example, Booking staff members) from being scheduled at the same time. + `TRANSPARENT`: The schedule remains open during the event, allowing other events to be scheduled concurrently.  Default: `OPAQUE`

location.description: Event location.  Default: `defaultLocation` of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md) the event belongs to

type.description: Location type.  Supported values: + `BUSINESS`: The event is held at a business location. + `CUSTOMER`: The event is held at the customer's location, such as their home or office. + `CUSTOM`: The event is held at an address or venue not tied to the business or customer.

name.description: Location name. For `BUSINESS` locations, it's identical to the [location](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/locations/location-object.md) `name`.  Min: 1 character Max: 150 characters

address.description: Location address. For `BUSINESS` locations, it's identical to the [location](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/locations/location-object.md)'s `formattedAddress`.

resources.description: List of [Wix Bookings resources](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/staff-members-and-resources/resource-v2/resource-object.md) affected by the event. This could include, for example, the [Wix Bookings staff member](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/bookings/staff-members-and-resources/staff-member-v1/staff-member-object.md) providing the service or the room where the appointment takes place.  Max: 100 resources

transparency.description: Specifies whether the event blocks time in the resource's schedule.  Supported values: + `OPAQUE`: The schedule is blocked during the event, preventing other events that involve the same resource from being scheduled at the same time. + `TRANSPARENT`: The schedule remains open during the event, allowing other events to be scheduled concurrently.  Default: `OPAQUE`.

permissionRole.description: Permission role associated with the resource. Refer to the [permissions article](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/permissions.md#roles) for more information.

totalCapacity.description: Maximum number of participants who can participate in the event.  Omit this field to inherit the schedule's `defaultCapacity`. Specifying it overrides that default, even when the value matches, and the event stops reflecting later changes to the schedule. Only specify it when a single event's capacity differs from the rest of the schedule. To change capacity for all of a schedule's future events, update the schedule's `defaultCapacity` instead. Some event types enforce capacity at the schedule level, where an event-level value doesn't affect bookability.  Default: `defaultCapacity` of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md) the event belongs to
