actions.name: events_v3_query_events
actions.description: Query events. Retrieves a list of events, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting.   ### Defaults  Query Events runs with these defaults, which you can override: - Sorted by `start` in `ASC` order. - `cursorPaging.limit` is `50`. - `WORKING_HOURS` events are excluded from the results. To retrieve working hour events, specify `"type": "WORKING_HOURS"` in the query filter.  ### Filters  #### Date filters  Do not specify filters for start and end dates inside `query.filter`, instead specify `fromLocalDate` and `toLocalDate`.  #### Unsupported filters  You can't filter by the following fields:  - `eventId`: To query by event GUID call either [Get Event](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-...

fields.description: Information about which fields containing personal data to return. Refer to the [permissions article](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/permissions.md) for more information.  Supported values: + `PI_FIELDS`: Returns all fields with personal data. Your app must have `Read Calendars - Including PI` or `Manage Calendars` permission scope. + `OWN_PI_FIELDS`: Returns only fields containing your own personal data.  Max: 1 field Default: No personal data is returned.

fromLocalDate.description: Local start date and time from which events are returned in [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. For example, `2024-01-30T13:30:00`.  Events that start before the `fromLocalDate` but end after it are included in the results. Must be earlier than `toLocalDate` unless the sort order is descending.

cursorPaging.description: Cursor token pointing to a page of results. Not used in the first request. Following requests use the cursor token and not `filter`.

limit.description: Number of events to return. Defaults to `50`. Maximum `1000`.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  You can get the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object. See [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/get-started/api-query-language.md) for more information.  Example of operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$startsWith`, `$contains`.  Do not specify filters for start and end dates inside `query.filter`, instead specify `fromLocalDate` and `toLocalDate`.

sort.description: Whether to sort events by their start date in ascending order or by their end date in descending order. Default is start ascending.

fieldName.description: The field to sort by. Either `start` or `end`. Default is `start`.

recurrenceType.description: Filters events based on their `recurrenceType`.  Max: 5 recurrence types can be specified. Default: Events with `recurrenceType` of `NONE`, `INSTANCE`, and `EXCEPTION` are returned.

timeZone.description: Time zone in [IANA tz database format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database) for `fromLocalDate`, `toLocalDate`, and for calculating `adjustedStart` and `adjustedEnd`. For example, `America/New_York` or `UTC`.  Default: `timeZone` specified in the business [site properties](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/site-properties/properties/get-site-properties.md).

toLocalDate.description: Local end date and time up to which events are returned in [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. For example, `2024-01-30T13:30:00`.  Events that start before `toLocalDate` but end after it are included in the results. Must be later than `fromLocalDate` unless the sort order is descending.

transparency.description: Specifies whether the event blocks time in the resource's schedule.  Supported values: + `OPAQUE`: The schedule is blocked during the event, preventing other events that involve the same resource from being scheduled at the same time. + `TRANSPARENT`: The schedule remains open during the event, allowing other events to be scheduled concurrently. totalCapacity.description: Maximum number of participants who can participate in the event.  Omit this field to inherit the schedule's `defaultCapacity`. Some event types enforce capacity at the schedule level, where an event-level value doesn't affect bookability.  Default: `defaultCapacity` of the [schedule](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/calendar/schedules-v3/schedule-object.md) the event belongs to

actions.name: create_conference
actions.description: Create conference. Creates a conference with a conferencing provider.  The provider creates the conference and returns its details, including the join URL and password.  Specify the provider with `appId`. When `appId` is omitted, the service uses the resource's latest connection. If the resource has no connection of its own, the service falls back to the site's business resource. This fallback applies only when creating a conference.

After authorization, the provider redirects to `redirectUrl` with `?connectionId=<id>` on success or `?error=<code>` on failure. - `CREDENTIALS` (`credentialsOptions`): validates the credentials and returns the established connection. - `CUSTOM` (`customOptions`): stores a static URL, password, and description, then returns the established connection. actions.name: add_recent_search
actions.description: Add recent search. Adds a term to the top of the calling user's recent searches on this site.  An earlier copy of the same term, in any letter case, is removed, and only the newest 10 terms are kept. Call this once the user settles on a term, not on every keystroke.  When the user edits a term you added earlier in the same session, pass the earlier one in `replacedSearchTerm` so the list doesn't keep both. Don't pass a term that was already in the list when the session started, or an older search the user made is removed.  An invalid term is rejected. Saving a valid one is best effort: if it can't be stored, the call still succeeds, so a successful call doesn't confirm the term was kept. ...

replacedSearchTerm.description: Earlier term to remove, which the user edited into this one, such as `dom` before they typed on to `domain`. Only pass a term you added in the same session.

searchTerm.description: Term the user searched for. Spaces at the start and end are trimmed before the term is checked and saved.

actions.name: get_recent_searches
actions.description: Get recent searches. Retrieves the terms the calling user searched for on this site, newest first, up to 10.  Recent searches are kept per user and per site, and expire 30 days after the user last added a term. An empty list means the user hasn't searched on this site, cleared their recent searches, or they couldn't be read: a read failure isn't returned as an error.  To add a term, call [Add Recent Search](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/dashboard/back-office-search/add-recent-search.md). To remove all of them, call [Clear Recent Searches](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/dashboard/back-office-search/clear-recent-searches.md).

actions.name: clear_recent_searches
actions.description: Clear recent searches. Clears the calling user's recent searches on this site.  Unlike adding, a failure to clear is returned as an error, so a successful call means the list was cleared. An add sent at the same time may put a term back.  To add a term again, call [Add Recent Search](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/dashboard/back-office-search/add-recent-search.md).

actions.name: search_dashboard
actions.description: Searches the site's dashboard for a term and returns the matches grouped into sections.  Each section is one category, such as Tools & Settings, Apps or Contacts, and the sections come in the order to show them, up to 10. A category has no section when the caller can't see it, when it matched nothing, or when it failed: a missing section doesn't mean the category has no matches. A category that didn't answer in time comes back as a section with no items, after the others, when there's room left among the 10.  Each category returns only what the caller may see: a user's own permissions, or an app's.  To keep the terms the user searched for, call [Add Recent Search](https://dev.wix.com/docs...

disableStatusChange.description: Whether to disable the option to change the automation's `configuration.status`.  Default: `false`.

readonlyActionIds.description: IDs of read-only actions. Read-only actions cannot be modified.  When empty and the automation's `settings.readonly` is `false`, all actions are modifiable.

archiveDate.description: Date when to archive the automation If this date in the past, nothing will happen (automation will not go into archived state) If this date in the future, on this date the automation will be updated with archived = true and configuration.status = INACTIVE After this date the automation may be unarchived and archived again, this date will have no influence

actions.name: query_invoices
actions.description: Query invoices. Retrieves a list of up to 100 invoices per page, based on the specified cursor paging, filtering, and sorting.   Query Invoices runs with this default, which you can override:  - `createdDate` is sorted in `DESC` order  Query Invoices supports cursor paging only. It doesn't support offset paging and doesn't return a total count. To retrieve the next page, pass the cursor from `pagingMetadata.cursors.next` in `cursorPaging.cursor`, and don't include `filter` or `sort` in that request. The cursor already applies them, and a request that includes them fails with `INVALID_CURSOR`.  To learn about working with Query methods, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api...

actions.name: search_invoices
actions.description: Search invoices. Retrieves a list of up to 100 invoices, given the provided filtering, search expression, sorting, and cursor paging.   Unlike [Query Invoices], Search Invoices supports free-text search across fields like `title`, `numbering.displayNumber`, and customer contact details. It also returns aggregation data.  To retrieve the next page, pass the cursor from `pagingMetadata.cursors.next` in `cursorPaging.cursor`, and don't include `filter`, `search`, or `aggregations` in that request. The cursor already applies them, and a request that includes them fails.

actions.name: enable_invoice_payments
actions.description: Enable invoice payments. Enables payments for an invoice.   Use this to record manual (offline) or MOTO (Mail Order/Telephone Order) payments against an invoice. Creates a Wix eCommerce order if one doesn't exist, which enables payment recording against the invoice. To generate a checkout URL for online payment instead, call [Initiate Payment](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/get-paid/invoices/invoices/initiate-payment.md).

actions.name: generate_pdf_document
actions.description: Generate pdf document. Generates a PDF document for an invoice.   PDF generation is asynchronous. Poll the invoice using [Get Invoice](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/get-paid/invoices/invoices/get-invoice.md) and check `documentInfo.status` until it's `AVAILABLE`, then use `documentInfo.downloadUrl` to access the file.

actions.name: generate_receipt
actions.description: Generate receipt. Generates a receipt document for a specific payment on an invoice. Requires the `paymentId` of a confirmed payment on the invoice.

actions.name: get_latest_invoice_number
actions.description: Get latest invoice number. Retrieves the highest invoice number currently in use.   Invoice numbering is managed in the [Invoices Settings API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/get-paid/invoices/invoices-settings/introduction.md).

prefix.description: Invoice number prefix to filter by.

actions.name: initiate_payment
actions.description: Initiate payment. Initiates payment for an invoice.   Creates a Wix eCommerce order if one doesn't exist, generates a payment request, and returns a checkout URL for the customer.

actions.name: mark_invoice_as_sent
actions.description: Mark invoice as sent. Marks an invoice as sent.   Adds the `SENT` status qualifier to the invoice and records the send timestamp and recipient in `activityInfo`. For details, see [Status Qualifiers](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/get-paid/invoices/status-qualifiers.md).

actions.name: mark_invoice_as_viewed
actions.description: Mark invoice as viewed. Marks an invoice as viewed.   Adds the `VIEWED` status qualifier to the invoice and records the view timestamp in `activityInfo`. For details, see [Status Qualifiers](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/get-paid/invoices/status-qualifiers.md).

actions.name: publish_invoice
actions.description: Publish invoice. Publishes an invoice.   Transitions the invoice status from `DRAFT` to `PUBLISHED`, finalizing it and assigning an invoice number. For details on status transitions, see [Invoice Lifecycle](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/get-paid/invoices/standalone-invoice-payment-lifecycle.md).

actions.name: send_invoice
actions.description: Send invoice. Sends an invoice to one or more contacts.   Specify `contactIds` in the request to choose recipients. If `contactIds` isn't provided, the invoice is sent to the customer contact on the invoice.

contactIds.description: List of contact GUIDs to send the invoice to. If not provided, the invoice is sent to the customer contact.

actions.name: unarchive_invoice

For field support for filters and sorting, see [OAuth Apps: Supported Filters and Sorting](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-management/headless-authentication/oauth-apps/filters-sorting.md)  To learn about working with _Query_ endpoints in general, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language).

limit.description: Number of items to load.

actions.name: login_v_2
actions.description: Login v 2. Logs in an existing member.  Typically, after a successful login, you generate and use member tokens for the logged-in member so that subsequent API calls are called as part of a member session. Use the `sessionToken` in the response to [get the site member's access and refresh tokens](https://dev.wix.com/docs/go-headless/coding/rest-api/visitors-and-members/handle-members-with-custom-login.md#get-the-site-members-access-and-refresh-tokens).

captchaTokens.description: CAPTCHA tokens, when CAPTCHA setting is on.

recaptchaForClientSiteKey.description: Use this when the client has registered their own reCAPTCHA site key (e.g., branded apps, headless apps).

siteKeyId.description: The site key GUID registered in ReCAPTCHA service SDL for this client's reCAPTCHA configuration.

hcaptcha.description: Passive hCaptcha token minted by the client's invisible hCaptcha widget, sent in addition to a reCAPTCHA token. Only observed, never decides the request: a request carrying only this token still fails as missing a CAPTCHA token. Single use, expires 120 seconds after minting. Local safety limit; hCaptcha does not define a maximum token size.

Returns the following: - `body`: HTML content for the logout response - `statusCode`: HTTP status code (200 for success, 302 for redirect) - `headers`: Array of key-value pairs including: - `Set-Cookie` headers to remove all session cookies - `Location` header (when `postLogoutRedirectUri` is provided, with 302 status)

If the email used to register the member already exists as a contact email, the registering member need to verify the email address using a code that is sent to the address.

actions.name: create_redirect_session
actions.description: Create redirect session. Creates a URL for redirecting a visitor from an external client site to a Wix page for Wix-managed functionality.  The Create Redirect Session method enables your external Wix Headless client site, built on any platform, to integrate Wix-managed frontend functionality for specific processes. For example, your site can temporarily redirect a visitor to Wix for authentication, or for a checkout process for bookings, eCommerce, events, or paid plans transactions.  To initiate a redirect session:  1. Call Create Redirect Session with the details required for Wix to take care of one specific process (for example, authentication or a bookings checkout). Provide one or m...

thankYouPageUrl.description: The URL for a custom thank you page implemented on a site outside of Wix. The visitor is directed to this page after the Wix-managed process is completed. When redirecting to this URL, Wix passes different query parameters depending on the preceding transaction:  After a pricing plans checkout: + `planOrderId`: GUID of a pricing plan order.  After an eCommerce checkout: + `orderId`: GUID of an eCommerce order.  After an Events checkout: + `orderNumber`: Unique order number for the transaction. + `eventId`: GUID of the event.  If the process is abandoned or interrupted, the visitor is redirected to the URL specified in `postFlowUrl` instead.  Default: If you don't specify a URL, the visitor is redirected to a Wix thank you page, and from there to the URL specified in `postFlowUrl`.

postFlowUrl.description: The URL Wix should redirect the visitor to when the Wix-managed process is completed, abandoned, or interrupted.  **Note**: For an authentication redirect, don't specify a URL here. Instead, specify one in `auth.authRequest.redirectUri`.

loginUrl.description: The URL for a custom login page implemented outside of Wix.  Default: If you don't specify a URL, a Wix login page is used.

bookingsServiceListUrl.description: The URL for a custom bookings services page implemented outside of Wix.  Default: If you don't specify a URL, a Wix bookings services page is used.

cartPageUrl.description: The URL for a custom eCommerce cart page implemented outside of Wix.  Default: If you don't specify a URL, a Wix cart page is used.

planListUrl.description: The URL for a custom pricing plans page implemented outside of Wix. When redirecting to this URL, Wix specifies the following query parameters: + `planIds`:  GUIDs of the pricing plans on the custom page. + `checkoutData`: Pass this string back in `paidPlansCheckout.checkoutData` when redirecting back to Wix for checkout.  Default: If you don't specify a URL, a Wix pricing plans page is used.

bookingsCheckout.description: Information required for generating a custom URL for a Wix Bookings checkout.

timezone.description: The timezone to use when presenting the selected slot to users, in [tz database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones) format. For example, `America/Santiago`.  Default: If you don't specify a timezone, the timezone in `slotAvailability.slot.timezone` is used.

slotAvailability.description: Required. The selected calendar slots to begin a booking checkout.

slot.description: The slot for the corresponding session, when the session is either a single session or a specific session generated from a recurring session.

startDate.description: The start time of this slot in [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) format.  If `timezone` is specified, dates are based on the local date/time. This means that the timezone offset in the `start_date` is ignored.

endDate.description: The end time of this slot in [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) format.  If `timezone` is specified, dates are based on the local date/time. This means that the timezone offset in the `end_date` is ignored.

timezone.description: The timezone for which slot availability is to be calculated.  Learn more about [handling Daylight Savings Time (DST) for local time zones](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/wix-bookings/availability-calendar/query-availability#wix-bookings_availability-calendar_query-availability_handling-daylight-savings-time-dst-for-local-time-zones) when calculating availability.

resource.description: The resource required for this slot. Currently, the only supported resource is the relevant staff member for the slot.

id.description: Business location GUID. Available only for locations that are business locations, meaning the `location_type` is `"OWNER_BUSINESS"`.

formattedAddress.description: The full address of this location.

formattedAddressTranslated.description: The full translated address of this location.

eventId.description: GUID for the slot's corresponding event, when the event is either a single event or a specific event generated from a recurring event.

bookable.description: Whether the slot is bookable. Bookability is determined by checking a session's open slots and booking policies. Locks are not taken into account.

totalSpots.description: Total number of spots for this slot. For example, if a session has a total of 10 spots and 3 spots are booked, `spotsTotal` is 10 and `openSpots` is 7.

openSpots.description: Number of open spots for this slot.

waitingList.description: An object describing the slot's waitlist and its occupancy.

totalSpots.description: Total number of spots and open spots for this waitlist. For example, a Yoga class with 10 waitlist spots and 3 registered on the waitlist has 10 `total_spots` and 7 `open_spots`.

openSpots.description: Number of open spots for this waitlist.

bookingPolicyViolations.description: Booking policy violations for the slot.

tooEarlyToBook.description: Bookings policy violation. Too early to book this slot.

tooLateToBook.description: Bookings policy violation. Too late to book this slot.

validSubmissionRequired.description: Bookings policy violation. Intake Form submission is required for this slot.

login.description: Specify an empty object in this parameter to generate a URL for Wix login without first checking whether the visitor is authenticated.

auth.description: Information required for generating a custom URL for Wix authentication.

clientId.description: GUID of the Wix OAuth app requesting authorization, or the https URL of a personal agent's client metadata document. Any other value is refused with `invalid_client`.

responseType.description: Desired authorization [grant type](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/protocols/oauth#grant-types).  Supported values: + `code`: The endpoint returns an authorization code that can be used to obtain an access token.

redirectUri.description: URI to redirect the browser to after authentication and authorization. The browser is redirected to this URI whether the authentication and authorization process is successful or not.

scope.description: Desired scope of access. If this field is left empty, only an access token is granted. To received a refresh token, pass `offline_access` as the value of this field.

state.description: A value used to confirm the state of an application before and after it makes an authorization request. If a value for this field is set in the request, it's added to the `redirectUri` when the browser is redirected there. Learn more about [using the state parameter](https://auth0.com/docs/secure/attack-protection/state-parameters).

responseMode.description: esired response format.  Supported values: + `query`: The response parameters are encoded as query string parameters and added to the `redirectUri` when redirecting. + `fragment`: The response parameters are encoded as URI fragment parameters and added to the `redirectUri` when redirecting. + `web_message`: The response parameters are encoded as a JSON object and added to the body of a [web message response](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-sakimura-oauth-wmrm-00).  Default value: `query`

codeChallenge.description: Code challenge to use for PKCE verification. This field is only used if `responseType` is set to `code`.

codeChallengeMethod.description: Code challenge method to use for PKCE verification. This field is only used if `responseType` is set to `code`.  Supported values: + `S256`: The code challenge is transformed using SHA-256 encyption. + `S512`: The code challenge is transformed using SHA-512 encyption.

sessionToken.description: Token returned by a successful [login](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/headless/authentication/login-v-2.md) or [register](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/headless/authentication/register-v-2.md) call that identifies the authenticated member.  In the default SDK flow, session context is passed through a hidden iframe automatically. When using a [full-page redirect](https://dev.wix.com/docs/go-headless/develop-your-project/self-managed-headless/authentication/members/custom-login-page/custom-login/custom-login-using-the-js-sdk.md#use-a-full-page-redirect-desktop-and-mobile-browsers) instead, you must pass this field explicitly because there is no iframe to carry the session context.

nonce.description: OIDC nonce, bound to the authorization request and echoed back in the id_token.

actions.name: send_email_transmission
actions.description: Send email transmission. Creates and sends an email transmission to one or more recipients.  The email is sent asynchronously. The returned transmission has `ACCEPTED` status. Call [Get Email Transmission](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/emails/email-transmission-v1/get-email-transmission.md) or listen for the Email Transmission Updated webhook to track delivery status.

emailTransmission.description: An email transmission represents a single email send request, including its recipients, HTML content, sender information, type, and delivery status. Creating an email transmission triggers the email to be sent asynchronously to all specified recipients.

marketingOptions.description: Options for marketing emails.  Used only when `type` is `MARKETING`.

unsubscribeUrlPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in `emailHtmlContent` that gets replaced with a recipient-specific unsubscribe URL before the email is sent. Case-sensitive. For example, `{{unsubscribe_url}}` or `[UNSUBSCRIBE_URL]`. The placeholder must be unique within the HTML content.  If not set, an unsubscribe link in the site's default language is appended to the bottom of the email.

emailHtmlContent.description: Full HTML content of the email.  Not returned in `queryEmailTransmissions`. Use `getEmailTransmission` to retrieve the HTML content of a specific transmission.  Stored for 30 days after the transmission is created. After that, this field returns `"<expired>"`.

metadata.description: Custom key-value pairs attached to the transmission to identify the context in which the email was sent. These values are passed to the email service provider and included in domain event payloads. Keys and values support letters, numbers, and hyphens only (no spaces or other special characters).  Default: `{}`

senderName.description: Display name shown as the sender.  Default: None (no display name is set).

senderEmailAddress.description: Sender email address. Must be verified using the Sender Emails API before use.  If the provided address can't be used as a FROM address (for example, addresses from free email providers such as gmail.com), the email is sent from `no-reply@et.wixsitemail.com` and the provided address is automatically used as the reply-to address instead.  Default: `no-reply@et.wixsitemail.com`

replyTo.description: Recipient that receives replies to this email. When a recipient replies, the reply is directed to this address instead of the sender address.  Default: When `senderEmailAddress` is provided and the email is sent from the Wix shared sender address, replies are automatically directed to `senderEmailAddress`.

contactId.description: GUID of the contact to send the email to. The contact's email address is retrieved from the Contacts API.

userId.description: GUID of the Wix user to send the email to. The user must be a site collaborator.  The user's email address is retrieved from the Users API.

emailAddress.description: Email address to send the email to. A contact is created with this address if one doesn't already exist.

toRecipients.description: List of recipients the email is sent to.

customHeaders.description: Custom headers to include in the email. Keys should have max length of 64 and must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and hyphens. Keys are case insensitive and must be unique (for example, "X-Foo" and "x-foo" cannot both be provided). Values should have max length of 900 and must contain only printable ASCII characters (0x20-0x7E). The keys should not contain reserved headers (case insensitive) from this list: * BCC * CC * Content-Type * Content-Transfer-Encoding * DKIM-Signature * Feedback-GUID * From * Precedence * Received * Reply-To * Return-Path * Sender * Subject * To * X-Abuse-Id If provided header happens to be also set by the system internally (for example "List-Unsubscribe"), provided header value will then be overridden.

emailTextContent.description: Plain text content of the email (optional).  Not returned in `queryEmailTransmissions`. Use `getEmailTransmission` to retrieve the text content of a specific transmission.  Stored for 30 days after the transmission is created. After that, this field returns `"<expired>"`.

attachments.description: TODO: implement limits for single file and for total Email attachments. Total size for all attachments must not exceed 20 MB when base64-encoded. Emails are either sent with all attachments or not sent at all. If any attachment fails to process, email transmission status is set to `ABORTED`.

remote.description: Remote file that will be downloaded from provided URL once.

fetchUrl.description: File download URL. It must be publicly accessible without authentication and stay valid until status has changed to `PROCESSED`. Download must finish in less than 30 seconds, max supported file size is 10 MB after base64 encoding.

local.description: Base64-encoded content of the local file.

contentBase64.description: Base64-encoded content of the attachment file. This field is not returned in `getEmailTransmission`, `queryEmailTransmissions` nor domain events.

fileName.description: Name of the attached file. Following extensions are not supported: // TODO: list unsupported extensions

contentType.description: MIME type of the attached file (optional). If not provided, the MIME type is inferred from the file name extension.

idempotencyKey.description: Unique key used to prevent duplicate transmissions. If a request with the same idempotency key is received, the original response is returned without creating a new transmission.  Keys are remembered for about 1 hour. This period isn't guaranteed and may change. After it passes, a request with the same key can create a new transmission.

actions.description: Generate action input mapping. Generates the input mapping of a new send email action, along with the email content it sends. action.description: An automation email action represents the email sent by an automation's `triggered-emails` action: its type, recipients and sender. The email content is managed separately, with [Get Email Content](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/emails/automation-email-action/get-email-content.md) and [Set Email Content](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/emails/automation-email-action/set-email-content.md).  An action isn't identified by an GUID of its own. An existing action is addressed together with the automation it belongs to, and a new one is described before it's added to an automation, so it has no identifiers yet.

emailType.description: Type of the email, which determines whether contacts can unsubscribe from it.  Default: `PROMOTIONAL`

notificationTopicId.description: GUGUID of the notification topic contacts unsubscribe from to stop receiving the email.  - `PROMOTIONAL`: A promotional topic. - `BUSINESS_TRANSACTIONAL`: A transactional topic.  Required if `emailType` is `BUSINESS_TRANSACTIONAL`. Can't be specified if `emailType` is `BUSINESS_CRITICAL`, since contacts can't unsubscribe from these emails, and isn't returned for them.  The topic isn't validated when the action is saved, so make sure it exists and matches `emailType`.  Default: For a `PROMOTIONAL` email, the general promotional topic.

senderDetailsId.description: GUGUID of the sender details to send the email with, as in [Assign Sender Details](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/emails/automation-email-action/assign-sender-details.md).  Returned only when sender details are explicitly assigned to the action.  Default: The site's default sender details if they exist, and Wix-branded sender details otherwise.

recipients.description: Who the email is sent to.  `CUSTOM` recipients whose single audience is the trigger contact (an `explicitData_triggerMainContact` audience) or the site owner are returned as the equivalent `TRIGGER_CONTACT` or `SITE_OWNER` recipients.  Default: The site owner.

contactIdPath.description: Path in the trigger payload schema to the GUGUID of the contact to send the email to. For example, `contactId` or `contact.id`. Usually the property marked with `"identityType": "contact"`.  Supports a path of property names and array indexes, such as `items[0].contactId`, rather than an expression. Property names can contain letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.  The path isn't checked against the trigger payload schema, so make sure it exists in the trigger's payload.

audiences.description: Audiences to send the email to, as in the [Audience API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/notifications/audiences/audience-v1/introduction.md). Each audience's `audienceProviderId` is the GUID of a provider returned by [List Audience Providers](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/notifications/audiences/audience-v1/list-audience-providers.md), or one of these providers, which resolve participants from the trigger payload when the automation runs: - `explicitData_triggerMainContact`: `{"participants": [{"type": "CONTACT", "value": "{{var(\"contactId\")}}"}]}`, where `type` is `CONTACT` or `EMAIL` and `value` refers to a path in the trigger payload. - `explicitData_accountUser`: `{"participants": [{"type": "WIX_USER", "value": "{{var(\"userId\")}}"}]}`, where `value` refers to a path in the trigger payload.  Each `audienceProviderId` is validated, but `audienceProviderData` isn't, so make sure it's the input its provider expects.  Min: 1 audience

audienceProviderData.description: audience provider data is needed in order to list participants of each provider

composer.description: Editor content and placeholder fallback values, using the canonical Email Marketing [Composer](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/emails/email-marketing/campaign/update-composer.md) contract.  Supports a `composer.composerDataJson` of up to 2,000,000 bytes when UTF-8 encoded.

composerDataJson.description: Editor content for the campaign. The format depends on `campaignEditorType`:  - `WEB`: Wix proprietary JSON format used by the drag-and-drop email editor. - `MOBILE`: A subset of the `WEB` format, used by the mobile email editor. - `MJML`: MJML markup wrapped in a JSON object under key "mjml". - `HTML`: HTML code wrapped in a JSON object under key "html".  Passing the wrong format for the given `campaignEditorType` causes a silent failure when sending or previewing the campaign.

defaultValues.description: Fallback values for dynamic placeholders in the campaign content.

map.description: Map of placeholder keys to their default values.

editorType.description: Editor type that produced `composer.composerDataJson`, and therefore the format that field is in. Set it whenever the content being written is in a different format than what is stored. The content is rendered according to this type, so a mismatch fails silently when previewing or sending. Leaving it unset on update keeps the existing type.  Supports `WEB`, `MJML` and `HTML`. To write content from scratch, use `MJML`: `WEB` content is a proprietary structure.  The type can be changed only on an email whose content is in the default language alone, since all of an email's languages share one format.

If the site's plan doesn't include email design themes, the cap is `0`, so every call fails with `OUT_OF_QUOTA` until the plan is upgraded.  If a site downgrades to a plan with a lower cap, its existing email design themes are kept and can still be retrieved, updated, and deleted. emailDesignTheme.description: An email design theme is a reusable definition of an email's look and feel, such as its colors, fonts, and spacing. body.description: Styling definition of the email design theme, as a free-form JSON object. Its structure is defined by the Wix email editor. The Wix email editor doesn't render styling that doesn't follow its structure. When `body` doesn't define a style class, the editor uses its default styling for that class. actions.name: create_seo_user_config
actions.description: Create seo user config. Creates the SEO configuration for the current site.  If a configuration already exists for the site, this method returns an `ALREADY_EXISTS` error. Use [Update Seo User Config](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/seo/seo-user-config/update-seo-user-config.md) to modify an existing configuration.

seoUserConfig.description: Site-level SEO configuration.  Controls URL structure and non-existent page behavior to optimize how search engines index and resolve a site's pages.

shouldFlattenUrlHierarchy.description: Whether to flatten page URLs.  When `true`, all pages use flat URLs regardless of their position in the page hierarchy. For example, a subpage at `/parent/child-page` is accessible at `/child-page`. When `false`, page URLs reflect the full parent-child hierarchy.  This setting only affects URL structure, it doesn't change the physical page hierarchy in the site's page tree.  Default: `false`

shouldUsePartialRouteMatch.description: Whether non-existent pages return a `200` status code instead of a `404`.  When `false`, requests to non-existent pages return an HTTP `404` status code. This setting is the SEO-recommended behavior that correctly signals missing pages to search engines.  When `true`, non-existent page requests return a `200` status code. Avoid this setting unless you have a specific SEO reason, as it prevents search engines from correctly detecting missing pages.  Default: `false` for sites created on or after September 1, 2024. `true` for sites created before that date.

This setting only affects URL structure, it doesn't change the physical page hierarchy in the site's page tree.  Default: `false`

shouldUsePartialRouteMatch.description: Whether non-existent pages return a `200` status code instead of a `404`.  When `false`, requests to non-existent pages return an HTTP `404` status code. This setting is the SEO-recommended behavior that correctly signals missing pages to search engines.  When `true`, non-existent page requests return a `200` status code. actions.name: publish_item_by_id
actions.description: Publish item by id. Publishes a previously created item by its `id`.  The item can be a draft or a scheduled item. To schedule the item for a future date, set `scheduledDate`; otherwise it's published immediately.  Published items appear on the site's Social Media Marketing page in the dashboard.

id.description: GUID of the item to publish.

scheduledDate.description: Date and time to publish the item. If omitted, the item is published immediately.

actions.name: publish_multi_story_draft
actions.description: Publish multi story draft. Publishes a multi-story draft as a sequence of single-media story items.  The draft's media list is split into individual story items that are published sequentially in media order, stopping on the first failure. Each story item gets a derived `referenceId` of `{draftReferenceId}:story:{index}` (the draft `id` is used when the draft has no `referenceId`). Story items already published by a previous call are skipped, so the method can be safely retried after a partial failure. The draft is deleted only after all story items are published. To schedule the story sequence, set `schedulingInfo.scheduledDate`; otherwise it's published immediately.

id.description: GUID of the multi-story draft to publish.

scheduledDate.description: Date and time the item is scheduled to be published.

actions.name: item_v1_query_items
actions.description: Query items. Retrieves a list of items, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting.  Query Items runs with these defaults, which you can override: - `paging.limit` is `50` - `paging.offset` is `0`  Query Items supports a fixed set of filterable fields: - `status`: `PUBLISHED`, `SCHEDULED`, `DRAFT`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, `PROCESSING`, or `IN_QUEUE`. - `channel`: a channel name, such as `FACEBOOK` or `INSTAGRAM`. - `type`: `POST`, `STORY`, `REEL`, `VIDEO`, or `SHORT`. - `mediaType`: `IMAGE` or `VIDEO`. - `suggested`: `true` or `false`. - `ids`: a list of item GUIDs.  Each of these supports the `$eq` and `$in` operators, and a bare value as shorthand for `$eq`, except for `ids`, which...

filter.description: Filter object in the following format: `"filter" : { "fieldName1": "value1", "fieldName2":{"$operator":"value2"} }` Example of operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$startsWith`, `$contains`

sort.description: Sort object in the following format: `[{"fieldName":"sortField1","order":"ASC"},{"fieldName":"sortField2","order":"DESC"}]`

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

origin.description: Origin point for geo-distance sorting on a GEO field results are ordered by distance from this point (ASC = nearest first, DESC = farthest first).

paging.description: Paging options to limit and skip the number of items.

limit.description: Number of items to load.

offset.description: Number of items to skip in the current sort order.

fields.description: Array of projected fields. A list of specific field names to return. If `fieldsets` are also specified, the union of `fieldsets` and `fields` is returned.

fieldsets.description: Array of named, predefined sets of projected fields. A array of predefined named sets of fields to be returned. Specifying multiple `fieldsets` will return the union of fields from all sets. If `fields` are also specified, the union of `fieldsets` and `fields` is returned.

actions.name: reschedule_item
actions.description: Reschedule item. Changes the scheduled publish date of a scheduled item.  Only an item with a `status` of `SCHEDULED` can be rescheduled.

scheduledDate.description: Date and time to publish the item. If omitted, the item is published immediately.

actions.name: account_v1_disconnect
actions.description: Disconnects a social channel account from the site.  After disconnecting, the channel can't publish until it's reconnected. To reconnect, call Get Connect Url.

actions.name: get_connect_url
actions.description: Get connect url. Retrieves a channel's OAuth authorization URL that a site owner opens to connect the channel.  Use this to connect a channel without a browser popup: retrieve the URL, surface it to the site owner, and have them authorize the channel in their browser. The channel's OAuth redirect then completes the connection server-side, after which the channel becomes connected. Poll Get Long Lived Token Status until the status is `VALID` to confirm the channel is connected.

actions.name: get_long_lived_token_status
actions.description: Get long lived token status. Retrieves the connection status of a site's social channel account.  Use this to check whether a channel is connected and able to publish before creating or publishing items.

actions.name: list_accounts
actions.description: List accounts. Retrieves the connected accounts for a social channel.  Specify the `channelName` to retrieve the accounts the site owner has connected for that channel.

actions.name: update_account_settings
actions.description: Update account settings. Updates the settings for a connected social channel account, such as the default page, board, or account to publish to.

actions.name: generate_image
actions.description: Generate image. Generates an image from a text prompt and a source image.  Image generation runs asynchronously. This method starts the process and returns an `executionId`. Poll Get Generated Image with that `executionId` until the status is `READY` (the `imageUrl` and `fileId` are then populated) or `FAILED`. The generated image is also added to the "Social Marketing AI Media" folder in the site's Media Manager.

imageUrl.description: URL of the source image to generate from.

userInput.description: Text prompt describing the image to generate.

actions.name: generate_post_data
actions.description: Generate post data. Generates post content for one or more social channels.  Returns per-channel post payloads matching an item's content, so you can use the result to create a draft or publish. Provide site assets, a text prompt, or both.

channels.description: Channels to generate post content for. When empty, the response includes one entry for each supported channel: Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Google Business Profile, and TikTok. A non-empty value narrows the response to the requested channels.

context.description: Additional context to incorporate into the generated content.

media.description: Candidate media for the generated post. Accepts images only. Each item carries a `type` (must be image), a `url`, and an optional Wix Media Manager `fileId` for media already in Wix.

url.description: Media URL.

fileId.description: Media Manager file GUID backing the media. Available only when the media is stored in the Media Manager.

siteAssets.description: Site assets the generated post is based on.

id.description: GUID of the asset in the Wix app that owns it. For example, a product GUID for a `STORES_PRODUCT` asset.

userInput.description: Free-form guidance for the generated post content.

actions.name: generate_text
actions.description: Generate text. Generates post captions from a text prompt.  Returns suggested captions that you can add to an item's content.

url.description: URL to reference in the captions, such as a link to promote.

withHashtags.description: Whether to include hashtags in the captions.

addLinkInBio.description: Whether to add a "link in bio" reference to the captions.

languageCode.description: 2-letter language code for the generated captions in ISO 639-1 alpha-2 format.

tone.description: Tone of voice for the captions. For example, `professional` or `playful`.

userInput.description: Text prompt describing the post to generate captions for.

actions.name: get_generated_image
actions.description: Get generated image. Retrieves the result of an asynchronous image-generation request.  Poll this with the `executionId` returned by Generate Image until the status is `READY`, when the generated image's `imageUrl` and `fileId` are populated, or `FAILED`.

actions.name: get_feature_data
actions.description: Get feature data. Retrieves the availability and usage quota for a premium feature on the site.  Use this to check whether the site's plan allows an action, such as publishing or scheduling a post, and how much quota remains before calling the relevant method.

actions.name: get_features_data
actions.description: Get features data. Retrieves the availability and usage quota for multiple premium features on the site.

actions.name: install_google_ads_if_not_installed
actions.description: Install google ads if not installed. Installs the Wix Google Ads integration on the site if it isn't already installed.  This method is idempotent. Calling it when the app is already installed has no effect.

actions.name: update_account
actions.description: Update account. Updates a Google Ads account linked to the current Wix site.

googleManagerAccountId.description: Google Ads manager account GUID that owns this account.

googleBillingSetupId.description: Google Ads billing setup GUID. Not set for test accounts.

premiumSubscriptionId.description: GUID of the premium subscription associated with this account.

latestInvoiceId.description: GUID of the most recent invoice generated for this account.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code in ISO-4217 alphabetic format. This is the currency selected by the site owner and may differ from the currency used by Google Ads directly. See `budgetInSupportedCurrency`.

budgetInSupportedCurrency.description: The current ad budget converted to a currency supported directly by Google Ads (USD, EUR, GBP, or JPY). This may differ from `currency` when the site owner selected a currency not natively supported by Google Ads.

value.description: Monetary amount. Decimal string with a period as a decimal separator (e.g., 3.99). Optionally, a single (-), to indicate that the amount is negative.

currency.description: Currency code. Must be valid ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD).

formattedValue.description: Monetary amount. Decimal string in local format (e.g., 1 000,30). Optionally, a single (-), to indicate that the amount is negative.

couponInfo.description: Legacy Google Ads coupon information assigned to the account. Use `appliedIncentive` for the full incentive lifecycle.

customerId.description: Google Ads customer account GUID associated with this coupon.

couponCode.description: Unique coupon code returned by Google Ads when the incentive was applied.

status.description: Current status of the coupon.

redemptionDate.description: Date when the account became eligible for the coupon (coupon redemption date).

expirationDate.description: Date until which spend is counted toward the coupon match requirements.

rewardGrantDate.description: Date when the coupon reward was granted to the account.

Minimum is approximately $6.40 USD for standard subscribers; maximum is approximately $127.60 USD standard, or up to $1,500 for high-spend accounts.

locations.description: Geographic locations targeted by this campaign.

geoTargetConstant.description: Google geo target constant resource name (e.g. geoTargetConstants/1023191).

proximity.description: Proximity criterion defining a circular area by geo point and radius.

address.description: Full address. The address is a description of the geo point that does not affect ad serving.

radiusUnits.description: The unit of measurement of the radius.

displayName.description: Human-readable location name shown in the UI (e.g. "New York, New York").

adSchedule.description: Weekly ad schedule defining the days and hours when ads can run.

adShowAnytime.description: Whether ads show at any time during the day. When `true`, the daily schedules below are ignored.

startTime.description: The start time of showing an ad in a specific day.

hour.description: Starting hour in 24 hour time. This field must be between 0 and 23, inclusive.

minute.description: Minutes after the start hour at which this schedule starts.

endTime.description: Stop showing the ad at this time in a specific day.

campaignBrief.description: The brief used to generate this campaign. Only present on campaigns created via the GetCampaignSuggestions endpoint of SuggestionsService.

actions.name: get_campaign_change_log
actions.description: Get campaign change log. Retrieves the full change log for a campaign — all status-changing events in chronological order.

actions.name: get_campaign_daily_budget_boundaries
actions.description: Get campaign daily budget boundaries. Retrieves the minimum and maximum allowed daily budget for the current account and currency.

actions.name: get_campaign_status_history
actions.description: Get campaign status history. Retrieves the full status change history for a campaign in chronological order.

actions.name: launch_campaign
actions.description: Launch campaign. Launches a draft campaign.  Launching enables the campaign in Google Ads. Ads start serving once Google approves them and the payment setup is complete.  To create a draft campaign, call [Create Campaign](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/ads/google-ads/campaign-v1/create-campaign.md) with `status` set to `DRAFT`. To reactivate a campaign that was paused after launch, call [Resume Campaign](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/ads/google-ads/campaign-v1/resume-campaign.md) instead.

actions.name: pause_campaign
actions.description: Pause campaign. Pauses a running campaign, stopping ad delivery immediately. An optional scheduledResumeDate can be provided to automatically reactivate the campaign at a future time.

resumeReminderDate.description: Date on which to send a dashboard notification reminding the user to resume the campaign.

scheduledResumeDate.description: Date on which the campaign will automatically resume. When set, a CampaignAutoResumedEvent is emitted at this time.

turnAutoRenewOff.description: Whether to disable subscription auto-renewal when pausing.

actions.name: resume_campaign
actions.description: Resume campaign. Reactivates a paused campaign, resuming ad delivery.

turnAutoRenewOn.description: Whether to re-enable subscription auto-renewal when resuming.

actions.name: query_asset_performance_metrics
actions.description: Query asset performance metrics. Retrieves a list of per-asset performance metrics for a Performance Max Leads campaign, given the provided filtering and sorting. Returns performance data for individual creative assets such as headlines, descriptions, and images. Not supported for other Performance Max campaign sub-types.

campaignId.description: Wix internal campaign GUID (GUID) of the Performance Max Leads campaign to query.

dateRange.description: A date range used to filter analytics queries, either predefined or custom.

custom.description: Custom date range.

from.description: Start date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

to.description: End date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

fields.description: Metrics to include in each result row. When omitted, all available fields are returned.

assetTypes.description: Asset field types to include in results. When omitted or empty, all asset types are returned.

actions.name: query_conversion_metrics
actions.description: Query conversion metrics. Retrieves aggregated conversion metrics for a campaign from Wix Analytics. Both campaignId and dateRange are required. Due to analytics query complexity, this method has a 120-second SLA.

campaignId.description: Wix internal campaign GUID (GUID) of the campaign to query.

dateRange.description: A date range used to filter analytics queries, either predefined or custom.

custom.description: Custom date range.

from.description: Start date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

to.description: End date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

actions.name: query_performance_metrics
actions.description: Query performance metrics. Retrieves a list of daily performance metrics for a campaign, given the provided filtering and sorting. Queries clicks, impressions, CTR, cost, leads, and phone calls from Google Ads in parallel. Use the fields parameter to control which metrics are returned. When includePreviousPeriod is true, the response also includes a previousPeriodSummaryRow and trends showing decimal percentage changes.

campaignResourceName.description: Google Ads resource name of the campaign to query, in the format `customers/{customerId}/campaigns/{campaignId}`.

dateRange.description: A date range used to filter analytics queries, either predefined or custom.

custom.description: Custom date range.

from.description: Start date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

to.description: End date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

fields.description: Metrics to include in each result row. When omitted, defaults to clicks, impressions, CTR, cost, phone calls, and date.

includePreviousPeriod.description: When true, the response includes previousPeriodSummaryRow and trends showing percentage changes relative to the equivalent preceding period.

actions.name: query_search_term_metrics
actions.description: Query search term metrics. Retrieves a list of search terms that triggered a Smart campaign's ads, given the provided filtering and sorting. Only supported for Smart campaigns. For Performance Max Leads campaigns, use [Query Search Term Metrics V2](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/ads/google-ads/performance-metrics-v1/query-search-term-metrics-v-2.md).

campaignResourceName.description: Google Ads resource name of the Smart campaign to query, in the format `customers/{customerId}/campaigns/{campaignId}`.

dateRange.description: A date range used to filter analytics queries, either predefined or custom.

custom.description: Custom date range.

from.description: Start date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

to.description: End date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

paging.description: Paging information for an analytics query.

nextPageToken.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results.

searchTermText.description: Filters results to search terms whose text contains this string. When omitted, all search terms are returned.

type.description: Whether to include or exclude search terms that match the provided list.

searchTermTexts.description: Exact search term texts to filter by.

actions.name: query_search_term_metrics_v_2
actions.description: Query search term metrics v 2. Retrieves a list of search terms that triggered a campaign's ads, given the provided filtering and sorting. campaignId.description: Wix internal campaign GUID (GUID) of the campaign to query.

dateRange.description: A date range used to filter analytics queries, either predefined or custom.

custom.description: Custom date range.

from.description: Start date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

to.description: End date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

paging.description: Paging information for an analytics query.

nextPageToken.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results.

searchTermText.description: Filters results to search terms whose text contains this string. When omitted, all search terms are returned.

type.description: Whether to include or exclude search terms that match the provided list.

searchTermTexts.description: Exact search term texts to filter by.

actions.name: query_shopping_performance_metrics
actions.description: Query shopping performance metrics. Retrieves a list of per-product performance metrics for a shopping or retail Performance Max campaign, given the provided filtering and sorting. The conversions and conversionRate fields always return 0 and are not queried from Google Ads. Due to product lookup complexity, this method has a 120-second SLA.

campaignId.description: Wix internal campaign GUID (GUID) of the shopping or retail Performance Max campaign to query.

dateRange.description: A date range used to filter analytics queries, either predefined or custom.

custom.description: Custom date range.

from.description: Start date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

to.description: End date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

fields.description: Metrics to include in each result row. When omitted, all available fields are returned.

nextPageToken.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results.

actions.name: get_payment_details
actions.description: Get payment details. Retrieves billing and payment details for the current site's Google Ads account.  Billing data is calculated from cached subscription information, not fetched live from Google Ads. This method has a response-time SLA of 30 seconds due to charge calculation complexity.  Errors: - ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND: Couldn't find the account.

actions.name: get_or_create_campaign_success_guide
actions.description: Get or create campaign success guide. Retrieves a campaign success guide or creates one by analyzing the campaign's landing page, campaign configuration, and relevant site connections.  The first call can take up to 120 seconds. Later calls return the saved guide unless changes to the campaign require a new analysis.

actions.name: update_campaign_success_guide_suggestion_status
actions.description: Update campaign success guide suggestion status. Updates the status of a suggestion in a campaign success guide.  Set `status` to `COMPLETED` to mark the suggestion as completed, or to `OPEN` to reopen it.

actions.name: clear_marketing_activity_posts
actions.description: Clear marketing activity posts. Removes the social post drafts from a marketing activity, leaving its story drafts unchanged.  Only drafts are removed. Posts that were already published or scheduled stay on the activity. To remove the activity's stories, use `ClearMarketingActivityStories`.

marketingActivityId.description: GUID of the marketing activity whose post drafts will be removed.

actions.name: clear_marketing_activity_stories
actions.description: Clear marketing activity stories. Removes the story drafts from a marketing activity, leaving its post drafts unchanged.  Only drafts are removed. Stories that were already published or scheduled stay on the activity. To remove the activity's posts, use [Clear Marketing Activity Posts](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/marketing-plan/marketing-plan-v1/clear-marketing-activity-posts.md).

marketingActivityId.description: GUID of the marketing activity whose story drafts will be removed.

actions.name: delete_marketing_plan
actions.description: Delete marketing plan. Deletes the marketing plan and all its activities.

actions.name: get_social_marketing_plan
actions.description: Get social marketing plan. Retrieves the marketing plan's current status and its activities for the requested timeframe.  Use this method to poll for completion after calling any of the generate or regenerate methods. When no `timeframe` is provided, the default start is today and there is no upper bound: all of the plan's activities from today onward are returned.

actions.name: delete_plan_marketing_activity
actions.description: Delete plan marketing activity. Deletes a marketing activity from the plan.

id.description: GUID of the marketing activity to delete.

actions.name: generate_marketing_plan
actions.description: Generate marketing plan. Generates a marketing plan for the site.  Generation is asynchronous. The response immediately returns a `status` of `GENERATING`. Poll `GetSocialMarketingPlan` until `status` is `ACTIVE` (ready) or `FAILED`. The plan's activities span the whole plan period (today through the end of next month), but social posts are generated automatically only for the nearest-term activities (how far ahead can depend on the site's social marketing premium plan). To generate posts for the remaining activities, call `GenerateSocialPosts`. The site should be published before calling this method, because generation draws on the published site. This isn't validated at call time: an un...

actions.name: generate_social_posts
actions.description: Generate social posts. Generates social post drafts (AI image and per-channel captions) for the given marketing activities.  Generation is asynchronous. The response returns immediately. Poll `GetMarketingActivityPosts` until posts appear on the activities. Posts are generated for all supported social channels; only posts for connected channels can be scheduled and published. Schedule the resulting drafts with `ScheduleDrafts`.

marketingActivityIds.description: IDs of the marketing activities to generate posts for.

actions.name: get_marketing_activity_posts
actions.description: Get marketing activity posts. Retrieves the social post drafts and video candidates for the given marketing activities.

marketingActivityIds.description: IDs of the marketing activities to retrieve posts for.

actions.name: regenerate_marketing_activity_posts
actions.description: Regenerate marketing activity posts. Regenerates the social post drafts (AI image and per-channel captions) for a marketing activity, leaving its story drafts unchanged.  Generation is asynchronous. The response returns a transient snapshot; regeneration continues in the background. Poll `GetMarketingActivityPosts` to check when the new posts are ready. To regenerate only the image while keeping captions, use `RegenerateMarketingActivityPostsMedia`.

marketingActivityId.description: GUID of the marketing activity whose posts will be regenerated.

actions.name: regenerate_marketing_activity_posts_media
actions.description: Regenerate marketing activity posts media. Regenerates only the image for a marketing activity's posts, leaving captions unchanged.  Generation is asynchronous. The response returns a transient snapshot; regeneration continues in the background. Poll `GetMarketingActivityPosts` to check when the new image is ready. To regenerate both the image and captions, use `RegenerateMarketingActivityPosts`.

marketingActivityId.description: GUID of the marketing activity whose post image will be regenerated.

actions.name: regenerate_marketing_activity_stories
actions.description: Regenerate marketing activity stories. Regenerates the story drafts for a marketing activity, leaving its post drafts unchanged.  Generation is asynchronous. The response returns a transient snapshot; regeneration continues in the background. Poll [Get Marketing Activity Posts](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/marketing-plan/marketing-plan-v1/get-marketing-activity-posts.md) to check when the new stories are ready.  If the activity has no story draft, nothing is regenerated and the returned snapshot is final. This method never creates a story that was not already planned.

marketingActivityId.description: GUID of the marketing activity whose stories will be regenerated.

actions.name: regenerate_marketing_plan
actions.description: Regenerate marketing plan. Regenerates the upcoming activities of the existing marketing plan. Activities whose date is already in the past are preserved.  Generation is asynchronous. The response immediately returns a `status` of `GENERATING`. Poll `GetSocialMarketingPlan` until `status` is `ACTIVE` (ready) or `FAILED`. A plan must already exist. If the plan is already generating, this method returns a `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error ("plan already generating"). Poll `GetSocialMarketingPlan` until the status is no longer `GENERATING` before calling this method. To include fresh SEO keyword research and blog activities, use `RegenerateMarketingPlanWithKeywordResearch` instead.

actions.name: regenerate_marketing_plan_with_keyword_research
actions.description: Regenerate marketing plan with keyword research. Runs fresh SEO keyword research and refreshes the content-plan inputs used for blog activities.  If no plan generation is in progress, the refreshed inputs are followed by marketing-plan regeneration. If a plan generation is already in progress, this method still refreshes the keyword research and content-plan inputs without replacing the current plan status or starting a parallel marketing-plan generation when the refresh completes.  Processing is asynchronous and multi-stage (slower than `RegenerateMarketingPlan`). The response immediately returns a `status` of `GENERATING`. actions.name: schedule_drafts
actions.description: Schedule drafts. Schedules the given draft posts for publishing via the Publisher.  Only items whose `status` is `DRAFT` are scheduled; non-draft GUIDs are silently ignored. Only drafts for channels the site has connected through the Publisher are scheduled; drafts for unconnected channels are silently skipped and remain drafts. Requires the site's plan to include the schedule-posts premium feature; otherwise the call returns a `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error.

draftIds.description: IDs of the draft posts to schedule for publishing.

actions.name: update_marketing_activity_posts_media
actions.description: Update marketing activity posts media. Updates the media on a marketing activity's post drafts with the provided media URL, leaving its story drafts unchanged.

fileId.description: Media Manager file GUID backing the media, when the media originates from the Media Manager.

marketingActivityId.description: GUID of the marketing activity whose post drafts will have their media replaced.

mediaIndex.description: Optional 0-based index of the media slide to replace within each post's existing media set (for editing a single image of a carousel). When omitted, the post's entire media set is replaced with the single new media. Posts that have no slide at this index are left unchanged.

mediaUrl.description: URL of the media to apply to the activity's posts.

actions.name: update_marketing_activity_stories_media
actions.description: Update marketing activity stories media. Updates the media on a marketing activity's story drafts with the provided media URL, leaving its post drafts unchanged.  A story draft holds one media item per frame, up to 5 frames. Specify `mediaIndex` to replace a single frame, or omit it to replace the whole story with the one new media item. A story that has no frame at that index is left unchanged.

fileId.description: Media Manager file GUID backing the media, when the media originates from the Media Manager.

marketingActivityId.description: GUID of the marketing activity whose story drafts will have their media replaced.

mediaIndex.description: Optional 0-based index of the story frame to replace. When omitted, the story's entire media set is replaced with the single new media. Stories that have no frame at this index are left unchanged.

mediaUrl.description: URL of the media to apply to the activity's stories.

actions.name: create_marketing_activity
actions.description: Create marketing activity. Creates a marketing activity.  Required fields: `title`, `description`, `targetDate`, and `marketingActivityType` (must be set and not `UNKNOWN`; one of `SOCIAL_MARKETING`, `EMAIL_MARKETING`, or `BLOG`). Missing any of these returns a `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error.

marketingActivity.description: A single planned marketing action within a site's marketing plan. Activities are generated by the AI when a marketing plan is created and represent concrete tasks such as a social media campaign, a blog post, or an email. Each activity has a title, description, target date, and type. Generating social posts for an activity is handled by the separate Marketing Plan API, not this API.

blogSeoData.description: SEO blog candidate data associated with this activity. Present only when `marketing_activity_type` is `BLOG`.

candidateData.description: IDs that identify the candidate and the flow that generated it.

briefData.description: The blog post brief itself: the suggested title, the target keywords, and the search data behind them.

h1Title.description: Suggested title for the blog post.

mainKeyword.description: Primary keyword for the page the blog post supports.  A page has a single main keyword, and several blog posts can support the same one.

serpData.description: Search engine results data for `mainKeyword`, such as its search volume and how hard it is to rank for.  List Blog Post Candidates doesn't currently return this field.

peopleAlsoAskSuggestions.description: list of people also ask questions

pageUrl.description: URL of the site page the blog post is meant to support.

seoData.description: SEO tags suggested for the blog post, such as its title tag and meta description.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

marketingActivityType.description: Category of marketing action this activity represents.

title.description: Short label for the activity, suitable for display in a marketing plan UI.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of what the activity involves and why it was suggested.

targetDate.description: Scheduled date by which the activity should be completed or published.

source.description: Origin context that the AI used when generating this activity (for example, an upcoming event or a set of keywords).

type.description: Indicates what kind of input drove the AI to generate this activity.

value.description: The specific value of the source input (for example, an event name or a keyword string).

asset.description: Site asset this activity is grounded in.

type.description: Type of the site asset (for example, product or blog post). See `SiteAsset.Type` for the closed set of values.

id.description: GUID of the asset within its provider's data store.

name.description: Display name of the asset (for example, the product title or blog post title), cached at activity-generation time.
