actions.name: get_credit_data
actions.description: Get credit data. Retrieves a site's word credit data.  For sites with a limited quota, you can calculate the available word credits by subtracting the credits used from the quota. For example, if a site has a quota of 100 credits and all credits have been used (`"creditsUsed": 100`), the available word credits will be 0. If a Wix user purchases an additional 50 credits, the `quota` will increase to `150`, and the site will have 50 available word credits.

actions.name: get_translation_job_status
actions.description: Get translation job status. Retrieves a translation job's current state, including how much content it has processed and which fields failed.  Poll this method until `jobState` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`. There's no published limit on how long a job takes. A job stays queryable indefinitely, so you can check its outcome long after it finishes.

actions.name: translate_site
actions.description: Translate site. Starts a background job that translates a site's content from one locale to another.  The call returns as soon as the job is accepted, and the response contains only the job's GUID. Pass that GUID to Get Translation Job Status to track the job.  The job reads the site's content as it goes, rather than working from a snapshot taken when it started. Content edited while the job is running may or may not be included, depending on whether the job has already reached it.  Translated fields are marked as ready to publish as the job completes them.  Several jobs can run against the same site at the same time. Each job selects its fields independently, according to its own `filter...

filter.description: Optional filter that narrows which content the job translates. Uses the same filter syntax as Translation Content, over the `schemaId` and `entityId` fields. For example, `{"schemaId": "<SCHEMA_ID>"}` translates a single schema, and `{"entityId": {"$in": ["<ID_1>", "<ID_2>"]}}` translates specific items. The `locale` key is reserved. The job already scopes itself to `mainLocale`, and supplying your own `locale` overrides that scoping.

mainLocale.description: GUID of the installed site locale to translate the content from. Get the GUID from [Query Locales](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/multilingual/locale-management/locales/query-locales.md). Use the GUID exactly as returned: if the site's locale GUIDs are `en` and `he`, use `en`; if they are `en-US` and `he-IL`, use `en-US`.

translatedLocale.description: GUID of the installed site locale to translate the content into. Get the GUID from [Query Locales](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/multilingual/locale-management/locales/query-locales.md). Use the GUID exactly as returned. Don't substitute a regional format such as `en-US` for a locale whose GUID is `en`.

Call the Notify method with this GUID as `notificationTemplateID` to trigger notifications based on that template.  If the notification template contains placeholders for dynamic values, provide those values as key-value pairs in the `dynamicValues` array. The values you specify are incorporated in the notifications sen...

price.description: Optional one-time payment price for joining the program. When creating or updating a program, provide `price.value` only. `price.currency` is read-only and is populated from the site's payment currency in Site Properties.

slug.description: Unique URL slug for the program page.

tags.description: The tags rendered into <head>, in no particular order. Render order is decided by the renderer, not by position in this list.  No maxSize: this list is already populated by data written years ago, and a bound added now could reject a page that is already stored.

props.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of HTML attributes. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag` / `MetaTag` / `LinkTag`.

meta.description: Legacy. Was an untyped bag of 16 mixed-purpose keys. In `SeoSchemaV2` its contents are split by purpose: per-page structured-data state moves to StructuredDataTag, authorship to `written_by`, and render-time preset logic (variants, enabledByExperiment, removeSchemaIf*) moved out of the stored document entirely — it belongs to the preset definition, not to the page. See the design log for the full key-by-key mapping.

children.description: Legacy. Was the tag's inner content, doubling as the JSON-LD payload for script tags. Typed replacement: `SeoSchemaV2.TitleTag.text` and `StructuredDataTag.json_ld`. No length limit, for the same reason as `type` above.

custom.description: Whether the tag is a [custom tag](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-additional-meta-tags-to-your-sites-pages) — i.e. an entry from the site's Advanced/Custom Tags list.  Setting this to `true` on a write restricts which `type` values are accepted — the same restriction the Advanced/Custom Tags UI enforces. `title` and `script` tags (including JSON-LD structured data) must be sent with `custom` omitted or `false`; sending them with `custom: true` is rejected with `TAG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.  Note this is a separate restriction from Site SEO Tags' own type restriction on `SiteSeoTags.tags`: even with `custom` unset, Site SEO Tags rejects `script` (e.g. for site-wide structured data) unconditionally. There is currently no way to set site-wide, every-page structured data through any of these APIs — write a per-page `script` tag through the Item SEO Tags API instead.  This flag is scoped to that feature only. It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

settings.description: Page-level SEO settings that are not themselves tags.

preventAutoRedirect.description: Whether to suppress the automatic redirect from this page's previous URL to its current one after a slug change.  Default false, meaning the redirect IS created. The field is named for the exception rather than the rule, which reads backwards; kept as-is because renaming a stored boolean is not worth the migration.

keywords.description: Keyword terms the user is targeting for this page. Used by the SEO assistant and checklist; never rendered into <head>.  20 is a sanity bound, not the product limit. v1 declared 5 — the number the panel happens to allow today — which is exactly the mistake we are fixing for structured data. A product decision to allow 8 should not need a proto release, so the panel owns that number and the proto only stops something absurd.

term.description: The term itself, e.g. "trail running shoes".  No maxLength, for the same reason as the legacy tag fields: keywords are already stored, and a bound added now could reject a record written before the bound existed. The flynt `missing-string-validations` warning on this field is accepted deliberately.

isMain.description: Whether this is the page's primary focus keyword. At most one per page.

origin.description: Which surface added the term, e.g. a panel or a suggestion flow. Used for attribution in BI. Opaque to the renderer.

actions.name: get_access_status

actions.name: get_certificate_download_url
actions.description: Get certificate download url. Retrieves a download URL for the participant's latest issued certificate.  The URL is returned only after the certificate document finishes rendering.

actions.name: get_participation_stats

programIds.description: IDs of the programs to retrieve participant statistics for.

actions.name: get_premium_stats

actions.name: issue_certificate
actions.description: Issue certificate. Manually issues a certificate to an active or finished participant.  A finished participant has completed or failed the program, or was automatically removed. The program must have a connected certificate reward. When authenticated as a site member, the participant must have completed the program.

fields.description: Array of conditional fields to include in the response. Use `RequestedFields.PROGRESS` to include the `progress` field, which isn't returned by default.

actions.name: get_resolved_step

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

filter.description: Filter object.  Learn more about [filtering](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#filters).

actions.name: upsert_resolved_step
actions.description: Upsert resolved step. Creates or updates a resolved step.  If a resolved step exists for the specified `participantId` and `programStepId`, the method updates it. Otherwise, the method creates a resolved step. The participant must have joined the program that contains the step.  For quiz steps, specify `quizSubmissionId`. The quiz submission must belong to the quiz associated with the program step. For non-quiz steps, omit `quizSubmissionId`.

resolvedStep.description: A resolved step represents a participant's completion or attempt of a program step.  The combination of `participantId` and `programStepId` uniquely identifies a resolved step. Upserting the same combination updates the existing resolved step.  For quiz steps, specify `quizSubmissionId`. The API copies `earnedScore` and `passingGrade` from the quiz submission and sets `status` to `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`. New submissions use the current questions; stored submissions retain their recorded answer evaluations.

rightAnswer.description: Correct numeric value. Matching is exact. multiChoice.description: Input with predefined options where multiple options can be selected.

actions.description: Clone quiz. Clones a quiz definition and returns a new quiz GUID.  A quiz with no active questions can't be cloned; the request fails with INVALID_QUIZ. Avoid modifying the source quiz while cloning it.  This operation copies the question and settings definition only. It doesn't copy Online Programs step associations or quiz submissions. Attach the returned GUID to a step separately when needed.

actions.name: create_quiz_submission
actions.description: Create quiz submission. Submits quiz answers and returns their evaluation results.  Specify `quizSubmission` and `quizSubmission.quizId`. The `answers` map can be empty when no questions require answers. Otherwise, provide answers keyed by the quiz questions' targets. The submitter is derived from the caller's authentication context. The API does not accept or return a submitter field.  If the quiz defines an attempt limit, creation fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION when the submitter's existing attempts reach that limit. Attempts are counted by groupId when supplied, otherwise by quizId. No attempt limit is enforced by this operation when the quiz has no configured limit.  Invalid quiz conf...

quizSubmission.description: Answers submitted to a quiz within an Online Program, together with their evaluation results.

groupId.description: Groups attempts for the same submitter when enforcing the quiz's attempt limit. If omitted, attempts are counted by quizId and submitter, and groupId remains absent in the response. If provided, counting uses groupId and submitter without restricting by quizId.

answers.description: Answers keyed by each quiz question's target, not its field GUID. Each response answer includes the corresponding fieldId. An unrecognized target causes submission creation to fail.

value.description: Submitted answer value, with a JSON shape determined by the question type: - Short text and long text: a string. - Single choice: the selected option's submitted string value, as described below. - Numeric: a number. - Multiple choice: an array of the selected options' submitted string values. - File upload: an array of file descriptor objects containing fileId, displayName, and fileType (MIME type), with url when supplied by the upload result. Submit uploaded-file metadata, not raw file bytes or an array of URL strings.  For questions created with Create Quiz or Bulk Create Quizzes, choice option strings also serve as their labels, unless the underlying form is later edited to store distinct values. Submit the exact selected strings from singleChoice.options or multiChoice.options. Do not submit option GUIDs or independently modified display text.  Quizzes authored or edited through Wix Forms can store distinct option values and labels. Clone Quiz and Bulk Clone Quizzes preserve these values. Submit the stored string value, falling back to the label when no string value is present. For example, an option with label "B) Associative property" and value "B" submits "B" for single choice or ["B"] for multiple choice. Get Quiz returns labels without a separate value mapping; use the underlying form's option values for these quizzes.  Short-text comparison ignores surrounding whitespace and letter case; multiple-choice comparison ignores order but retains duplicates. Long-text and file-upload answers are stored but are not evaluated for correctness. Short-text, numeric, single-choice, and multiple-choice answers are also non-evaluable when the question has no stored correct-answer key. Such answers count as correct when calculating earnedGrade, but omit correct, score, and message in the response. A correct-answer key hidden from a caller's Quiz response is not necessarily absent from the stored quiz and does not establish that the answer is non-evaluable.

actions.name: online_programs_categories_create_category

category.description: A reusable, site-level classification for Online Programs.  Categories exist independently of Programs and remain available when they have no Program assignments.

label.description: Category's display label. The primary-language label must be unique within the site. Localized reads return the Wix Multilingual translation when one exists, and otherwise fall back to the primary label.

actions.name: generate_checkout_session
actions.description: Generate checkout session. Creates a Wix-hosted checkout session for the supplied line items and returns its redirect URL and session GUID.  Each call creates a new, independent session. The method isn't idempotent, so a retry produces an additional session rather than recovering the prior one.

callbackUrls.description: URLs the buyer is redirected to after the checkout flow.  The buyer is sent to one of the URLs below: `continueBrowsingUrl` if they explicitly leave via **Continue browsing**, or `thankYouPageUrl` after a successful payment.  If the buyer abandons the page implicitly (closing the tab, navigating away, network failure), no callback URL is invoked and the checkout session isn't resumed.

thankYouPageUrl.description: URL the buyer is redirected to after a successful payment.

continueBrowsingUrl.description: URL the buyer is redirected to from the Wix checkout page when they choose to leave without completing payment, either when they click **Continue browsing** or when they navigate back to a cart-style page.

cart.description: Items, quantities, and prices the buyer is paying for, plus optional pre-fill customer details.

items.description: Line items the buyer is paying for in this checkout session.  At most 1 subscription line item (an item with `subscriptionInfo` set) is allowed per request. Wix rejects requests with 2 or more subscription items. Non-recurring items can be combined with a single subscription item. In that case the buyer is charged once at checkout for the non-recurring items and, if applicable, the first cycle of the subscription. Wix bills any subsequent cycles on the subscription's own schedule.

name.description: Name of the item, shown on the checkout page.

quantity.description: Quantity of this item to charge for.

price.description: Per-unit price as a decimal string in the merchant account currency. For example, `"19.99"`.

subscriptionInfo.description: Subscription configuration. When set, the line item follows a scheduled-billing model defined by `subscriptionSettings` instead of a single immediate charge. The recurring charge each billing cycle is `price × quantity`, and `quantity` is locked at session creation.  At most 1 line item per request may set `subscriptionInfo`. Wix rejects requests with 2 or more subscription line items with `MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIPTION_ITEMS`.

subscriptionSettings.description: Billing frequency, cycles, and free trial configuration. Required when `subscriptionInfo` is set on a line item.

frequency.description: Billing frequency unit. Required when `subscriptionSettings` is set; `UNDEFINED` is rejected.

interval.description: Number of frequency units between charges. For `DAY` frequency, the minimum is 7. The shortest billing cadence supported is weekly; values 1–6 with `frequency: DAY` are rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (rule code `MIN_VALUE`). Default: `1`.  Note that `freeTrialPeriod.interval` doesn't share this floor: a `DAY` trial may have `interval` as low as 1.

autoRenewal.description: Whether the subscription renews automatically. Can't be `true` when `billingCycles` is set.  Default: `true` when both `autoRenewal` and `billingCycles` are omitted; `false` when `billingCycles` is set and `autoRenewal` is omitted.

billingCycles.description: Number of billing cycles before the subscription stops. Can't be set when `autoRenewal` is `true`.  When omitted along with `autoRenewal`, the subscription renews indefinitely.

freeTrialPeriod.description: Free trial period before the first charge.

frequency.description: Trial period frequency unit. Required when `freeTrialPeriod` is set; `UNDEFINED` should be treated as a client mistake and isn't a valid runtime value.

interval.description: Length of the trial period in `frequency` units. For example, `interval: 14` with `frequency: DAY` gives a 14-day trial.  Unlike `SubscriptionSettings.interval`, this field's `DAY` floor is `1`. No weekly floor applies to the trial length. Values ≤ 0 are rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (rule code `MIN_VALUE`).

title.description: Subscription name shown to the buyer in the recurring-billing summary block on the Wix-hosted checkout page (the heading of that block).

description.description: Subscription description shown to the buyer in the recurring-billing summary block on the Wix-hosted checkout page (the body text below the title).

physicalProperties.description: Optional. Physical properties of the item, used when the item requires shipping.

customerInfo.description: Buyer details used to pre-fill the checkout form. The buyer can edit any of these fields on the Wix checkout page.

externalInfo.description: Optional. External key-value information to attach to this checkout session. Wix stores the values and returns them unchanged on the resulting order's line items; nothing interprets or displays them.  Use this to correlate the order with your own records, for example an internal reference or a plan name.

If the redirect would close a loop, meaning an existing redirect starts at the path this one points to, the redirect that closes the loop is deleted and the create proceeds. Both a conflicting redirect replaced this way and a loop-closing redirect are gone for good, so retrieve them first if you need to restore them.  Creating a redirect that already exists with the same `from`, `to`, and `options.groupRedirect` ch...

options.description: Extra options for creating a redirect.

When `false`, a taken `from` path fails the call with `FROM_URL_EXISTS`.  The replaced redirect is deleted for good, so retrieve it first if you might need to restore it.  Default: `false`

redirect.description: A redirect sends a visitor who requests one path on a site to another path or URL.  Redirects keep old links working after a page is renamed or removed, consolidate duplicate URLs, and point a whole section of a site somewhere else. A redirect returns a 301 permanent redirect, takes effect on the live site immediately with no site publish, and takes precedence over a page that exists at the same path.  A redirect either matches its `from` path exactly, or matches everything under it when `options.groupRedirect` is `true`. A redirect scoped to a `language` applies to that language version of a multilingual site, and one with no `language` applies to every language.

from.description: Path on the site that the redirect starts from, URL-encoded. For example, `/old-page`.  Can't be the site root. A path that differs from another redirect's `from` path only by a trailing slash counts as the same path.  For a redirect scoped to a `language`, specify the path with or without the language prefix: the prefix is stripped, so a `fr` redirect from `/fr/about` is stored and returned as `/about`.

For example, a group redirect from `/forum/questions/` to `/forum/faqs/` sends `/forum/questions/my-post` to `/forum/faqs/my-post`. When `false`, only the exact `from` path matches.  A group redirect and an exact redirect that share a `from` path are two different redirects.  Default: `false`

It is NOT an indicator of whether a standard tag (`title`, `description`, Open Graph, etc.) reflects a manually configured value versus a computed default/pattern — standard tags always resolve with `custom: false`, even when their content comes from a page's manually saved SEO title/description override. Don't use this field to verify whether a live page reflects a manual per-page SEO edit.  Limitation: when `ResolveStaticPageSeoTags` is called without `seoData`, the per-page SEO data is read only from the Vibe/Wix-managed-headless override store. That store holds nothing for classic Wix Editor or Wix Studio pages, so even genuine Advanced/Custom Tags saved on those pages are missing from the response entirely — there, `false` means this API could not tell, not that no custom tag exists. Pass `seoData` explicitly to resolve against a known set of tags.  `SeoSchemaV2.Tag` expresses this as `written_by = USER_CUSTOM`.

disabled.description: Whether the tag is excluded from the rendered <head>.  A disabled tag is still stored, so the user can re-enable it and so a pattern-provided tag stays suppressed on this page. Default false.

actions.name: list_seo_pattern_variables
actions.description: List seo pattern variables. Retrieves the variables a pattern for a page type may reference.  Call this method to retrieve the valid variables for a page type before writing a pattern.  Variables for the page's own tags and variables for its structured data are returned in separate fields, and a pattern may use either.

actions.name: list_seo_patterns
actions.description: List seo patterns. Retrieves the patterns stored for a site, one per page type.  Only returns page types that have had a pattern of the site's own stored, so a page type that has never had one is absent. A page type that was reset to its default remains in the list, with an empty `pattern` and `source` of `PATTERN_SOURCE_DEFAULT`.

actions.name: reset_seo_pattern_to_default
actions.description: Reset seo pattern to default. Removes the pattern a site has for a page type, so the Wix default applies again.  The response reports the page type after the reset, with an empty `pattern` and `source` of `PATTERN_SOURCE_DEFAULT`.

pageId.description: GUID of a single page built from a Wix Data collection, to reset the pattern of that page alone.  Supported only for the `WIX_DATA_PAGE_ITEM` page type.

actions.name: connection_v1_disconnect
actions.description: Disconnect. Removes the site's Google Search Console connection.  The site's stored Google credentials are deleted. This doesn't remove the site's `google-site-verification` tag (see Clear Verification in the GSC Site Readiness API), doesn't change anything in the connected Google account, and doesn't revoke the grant on Google's side. The account owner can revoke it from their Google account settings.

actions.name: connection_v1_get_connect_url
actions.description: Get connect url. Retrieves the Google authorization URL for the Wix user to open.  Surface the returned URL to the person connecting. After they authorize in their browser, Wix completes the OAuth exchange server-side. There is no code-exchange call to make. Poll Get Connection until the status is `VALID`.  Any Google account can be used and needs no prior Search Console setup. Site verification and property access are established afterwards through the GSC Site Readiness API.  Each call starts a new authorization attempt: the returned URL is single-use and expires after 2 hours, so request a fresh one for every attempt rather than caching or reusing one.  Any user with SEO permissions ca...

actions.name: connection_v1_get_connection
actions.description: Get connection. Retrieves the site's Google Search Console connection status.  One endpoint for both polling and steady-state reads: poll it after surfacing the URL from Get Connect URL until the status is `VALID`, or call it any time to learn whether the site is connected and as whom. When polling, every few seconds is enough. Stop after 2 hours, when the authorization attempt expires.  Returns `PENDING` while a connect started with Get Connect URL awaits the user's authorization on Google, and `NOT_CONNECTED` when the site has no Google account connected and no connect is in flight.

actions.name: add_site
actions.description: Add site. Adds the site to the connected Google Search Console account.  For a Wix site, the site is resolved from the request context and no parameter is needed. To add a site that isn't hosted on Wix, set `siteUrl` to its URL-prefix Search Console property. Add Site requires the site to be verified first, so call Verify Site before this method.  Requires the site to be published, have a connected domain, and allow search-engine indexing; otherwise fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

actions.name: clear_verification
actions.description: Clear verification. Removes the site's Google verification tag and Google connection.  Deletes the `google-site-verification` meta tag that Verify Site placed, discards the stored verification state, and also deletes the site's stored Google credentials. After this call the site's connection status is `NOT_CONNECTED`. To remove only the credentials and keep the verification tag, use the GSC Connection API's Disconnect instead. Neither call removes the site from Google Search Console.

actions.name: get_inspection
actions.description: Get inspection. Retrieves the stored results of the site's latest URL inspection.  Returns the results accumulated by Inspect URLs, including partial results while an inspection is still `ONGOING`.

actions.name: get_search_analytics
actions.description: Get search analytics. Retrieves the site's search performance data from Google Search Console.  Returns clicks, impressions, click-through rate, and average position, grouped by the requested dimensions. For example, group by `date` for a daily chart, or by `query` for top search terms.  The data is Google Search Console's search performance report for the site, so its freshness and history range follow Google Search Console.

dimensions.description: Dimensions to group the results by, in the order they should appear in each result's `keys`. Supported values are Google Search Console's search analytics dimensions: `date`, `query`, `page`, `country`, `device`, `searchAppearance`.  Default: no grouping, a single aggregate row for the whole period.

endDate.description: Last day of the requested period, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Inclusive.

rowLimit.description: Maximum number of rows to return.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

startDate.description: First day of the requested period, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

startRow.description: Zero-based index of the first row to return. Use with `rowLimit` to page through large result sets.

type.description: Search type to report on. Supported values: `web`, `image`, `video`, `news`.  Default: `web`.

actions.name: get_site
actions.description: Get site. Retrieves one Google Search Console property of the connected Google account, with the account's permission level on it.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

actions.name: get_site_readiness
actions.description: Get site readiness. Retrieves the site's readiness in Google Search Console.  Returns whether the site's Google connection and ownership verification are in place, and if not, the first blocking step. Use this to decide what to resolve next. For example, a `SITE_OWNER_NOT_VERIFIED` blocking reason means the site's ownership isn't proven to Google yet, so call Verify Site.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

actions.name: get_sitemap
actions.description: Get sitemap. Retrieves one submitted sitemap, with Google's processing details: content counts, warnings, errors, and download dates. To list every sitemap submitted for the site, use List Sitemaps.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

sitemapUrl.description: Full URL of the sitemap, as submitted.

actions.name: get_verification_token
actions.description: Get verification token. Retrieves the Google verification meta tag for a site that isn't hosted on Wix.  The tag is added to Wix sites automatically, so this method is only for a `siteUrl`. Place the returned tag in the `<head>` of the site's home page, then call Verify Site with the same `siteUrl`. The tag is issued for the connected Google account, so the same tag verifies every site that account owns. Keep it on the page after verification, because Google rechecks it.

siteUrl.description: URL of the site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported. Keep the tag on the page after verification: Google rechecks it, and removing it loses ownership.

actions.name: inspect_url
actions.description: Inspect url. Runs Google URL inspection on a single URL and returns the result.  The call is synchronous and stores nothing, and the URL doesn't have to be a page of a Wix site. To inspect many pages of a Wix site by page GUID in the background, use Inspect URLs instead.  Each call consumes Google URL-inspection quota for the connected account: up to 2,000 inspections a day per property.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

url.description: Full URL to inspect. Must belong to the site the call is made on, or to `siteUrl` when it's set.

actions.name: inspect_urls
actions.description: Inspect urls. Runs Google URL inspection on the given site pages.  To inspect one URL synchronously, including a URL that isn't a page of a Wix site, use Inspect URL instead.  Inspection starts synchronously and the response contains the results of the first chunk of pages. When the first chunk covered every requested page, the status is already `COMPLETE` and no polling is needed. When pages remain, the status is `ONGOING` and Wix keeps inspecting them server-side. Poll Get Inspection until the status is `COMPLETE` or `ERROR`.  Each page inspection consumes Google URL-inspection quota for the connected account. Inspection stops early when that quota runs out, so check `remaining_page_cou...

pageIds.description: IDs of the site pages to inspect. Each inspection result identifies its page in the `page` object, with the same `pageId`.

updateResults.description: Whether to merge the new results into the previous inspection instead of replacing it.  Default: `false`. A new inspection replaces the stored results.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_list_events
actions.description: List events. Retrieves the history of Google Search Console setup events for the site: when it was connected, verified, added, and when sitemaps and indexing were last submitted.  Events are a history, not the current state. An event stays listed after the step it records is undone, for example `ACCOUNT_CONNECTED` after Disconnect. For the current state, call Get Site Readiness, or Get Connection in the GSC Connection API.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

actions.name: list_sitemaps
actions.description: List sitemaps. Retrieves the sitemaps submitted for the site, with Google's processing details for each: content counts, warnings, errors, and download dates.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

actions.name: list_sites
actions.description: List sites. Lists the Google Search Console properties of the connected Google account, with the account's permission level on each.  Includes properties that aren't Wix sites and domain properties (`sc-domain:`). Domain properties can't be used as `siteUrl` in the other methods.

actions.name: request_page_indexing
actions.description: Request page indexing. Asks Google to recrawl the site's home page, given by its URL.  Only the home page can be submitted: any other URL fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Google discovers the site's other pages from the sitemap (see Submit Sitemap). Shares Request Site Indexing's daily limit per site; a call over the limit fails with `INDEXING_REQUEST_LIMIT_REACHED`.  Like Request Site Indexing, this is a request into Google's crawl queue, subject to Google's quotas, not an immediate re-index.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

url.description: Full URL of the site's home page, for example `https://www.my-fashion-store.com`. A trailing slash is ignored; any other page, or a URL with a query or fragment, fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. For a site that isn't hosted on Wix, the home page is `siteUrl`.

actions.name: request_site_indexing
actions.description: Request site indexing. Asks Google to recrawl the site's home page.  The request covers the home page only: Google discovers the site's other pages from the sitemap (see Submit Sitemap). A site can request indexing a limited number of times a day, counting both Request Site Indexing and Request Page Indexing; a call over the daily limit fails with `INDEXING_REQUEST_LIMIT_REACHED`.  Indexing requests are subject to Google's own quotas and scheduling; a successful call means the request was accepted, not that the site is indexed. Track progress with Inspect URLs.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

actions.name: submit_sitemap
actions.description: Submit sitemap. Submits the site's sitemap to Google Search Console.  Wix generates and hosts the sitemap; this method submits its URL to the connected Google Search Console property. Google processes sitemaps asynchronously. Check processing state with List Sitemaps.  Requires the site to be published, have a connected domain, and allow search-engine indexing; otherwise fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

sitemapUrl.description: Full URL of the sitemap to submit. Required with `siteUrl`, since the sitemap of a site that isn't hosted on Wix can't be derived. Ignored for a Wix site.

actions.name: verify_site
actions.description: Verify site. Verifies ownership of the site with Google.  For a Wix site, no parameter is needed: the `google-site-verification` meta tag is added to every page of the site automatically, and Google is asked to confirm it. To verify a site that isn't hosted on Wix, place the tag from Get Verification Token in the `<head>` of its home page, then set `siteUrl` to its URL-prefix Search Console property. Nothing is placed on a site that isn't hosted on Wix.  Verification requires a connected Google account and runs synchronously against Google, so allow up to a minute for the call to return.  For a Wix site, requires the site to be published, have a connected domain, and allow search-engine i...

siteUrl.description: URL of a site that isn't hosted on Wix, exactly as its URL-prefix property appears in Google Search Console. For example, `https://example.com/`. Place the meta tag from Get Verification Token in the `<head>` of the site's home page before calling. Leave empty for the Wix site the call is made on: setting it for a Wix site fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Domain properties (`sc-domain:example.com`) aren't supported.

actions.name: bing_webmaster_tools_connection_v1_disconnect
actions.description: Disconnect. Removes the site's Bing Webmaster Tools connection.  Only this site is disconnected. Other sites connected with the same Bing account stay connected. An authorization attempt still in flight for this site is cancelled: it can't connect the site after this call returns.  This doesn't remove the site's `msvalidate.01` verification tag (see Clear Verification in the BWT Site Readiness API), doesn't change anything in the connected Bing account, and doesn't revoke the grant on Microsoft's side. The account owner can revoke it from their Microsoft account settings.

actions.name: bing_webmaster_tools_connection_v1_get_connect_url
actions.description: Get connect url. Retrieves the connect URL for the Wix user to open.  Surface the returned URL to the person connecting. It opens a Wix page that sends them on to Bing to authorize. Open it in a top-level browser window or tab, not in a popup that keeps a reference to the page that opened it. After they authorize, Wix completes the OAuth exchange server-side. There is no code-exchange call to make. Poll Get Connection until the status is `VALID`.  Any Microsoft account can be used. Adding and verifying the site in Bing Webmaster Tools happen afterwards through the BWT Site Readiness API.  Each call starts a new authorization attempt: the returned URL is single-use and expires after 2 hour...

actions.name: bing_webmaster_tools_connection_v1_get_connection
actions.description: Get connection. Retrieves the site's Bing Webmaster Tools connection status.  One endpoint for both polling and steady-state reads: poll it after surfacing the URL from Get Connect URL until the status is `VALID`, or call it any time to learn whether the site is connected. When polling, every few seconds is enough. The person must finish on Bing within 10 minutes of opening the URL, so stop polling once that window has passed.  Returns `PENDING` while a connect started with Get Connect URL awaits the person's authorization on Bing, and `NOT_CONNECTED` when the site has no Bing account connected and no connect is in flight. An abandoned attempt can report `PENDING` for up to 2 hours. While...

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_add_site
actions.description: Add site. Adds the site to the connected Bing Webmaster Tools account.  The site is resolved from the request context, so no parameter is needed. Call this before Verify Site: Bing verifies only sites already in the account. If the account already lists the site, the call succeeds without adding it again. Right after a Bing account is connected, Bing can briefly reject the new credentials, so the call retries a few times before it fails.  Requires the site to be published, have a connected domain, and allow search-engine indexing; otherwise fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_clear_verification
actions.description: Clear verification. Removes the site's Bing verification tag and Bing connection.  Deletes the `msvalidate.01` meta tag that Verify Site placed, discards the stored verification state, and deletes this site's stored Bing credentials. Other sites connected with the same Bing account stay connected. After this call the site's blocking reason is `NOT_CONNECTED`. The call doesn't remove the site from Bing Webmaster Tools.  Only for a call made on a Wix site. Without one, the call fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_get_site_readiness
actions.description: Get site readiness. Retrieves the site's readiness in Bing Webmaster Tools.  Returns whether the site's Bing setup is complete, and if not, the first blocking step. Use this to decide what to resolve next. For example, a `SITE_NOT_ADDED` blocking reason means the site isn't in the connected Bing account yet, so call Add Site.  Setup steps are checked in order, and only the first missing one is returned: `NOT_CONNECTED`, `SITE_NOT_PUBLISHED`, `DOMAIN_NOT_CONNECTED`, `SITE_NOT_ADDED`, then `SITE_OWNER_NOT_VERIFIED`. Readiness is read live from Bing and changes nothing.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_get_sitemap
actions.description: Get sitemap. Retrieves one submitted sitemap, with Bing's processing details. When the sitemap is a sitemap index, also returns the sitemaps it lists. To list every sitemap submitted for the site, use List Sitemaps.

sitemapUrl.description: Full URL of the sitemap, as submitted.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_get_verification_token
actions.description: Get verification token. Retrieves the Bing verification meta tag of the site.  Wix places this tag on the site automatically when Verify Site runs, so the response is for display only. The tag is issued for the connected Bing account. It stays on the site after verification, because Bing rechecks it.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_list_sitemaps
actions.description: List sitemaps. Retrieves the sitemaps submitted for the site, with Bing's processing details for each: status, URL count, and submission and crawl dates.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_submit_sitemap
actions.description: Submit sitemap. Submits the site's sitemap to Bing Webmaster Tools.  Wix generates and hosts the site's sitemap; this method submits its URL to the connected Bing account. Bing processes sitemaps asynchronously. Check processing state with List Sitemaps.  Requires the site to be published, have a connected domain, and allow search-engine indexing; otherwise fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

actions.name: site_readiness_v1_verify_site
actions.description: Verify site. Verifies ownership of the site with Bing.  No parameter is needed: Wix adds the `msvalidate.01` meta tag to every page of the site, then asks Bing to confirm it. Add the site with Add Site first, because Bing verifies only sites already in the account.  Verification requires a connected Bing account and runs synchronously against Bing, so allow up to a minute for the call to return.  Requires the site to be published, have a connected domain, and allow search-engine indexing; otherwise fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

actions.name: cancel_content_plan_flow
actions.description: Cancel content plan flow. Cancels a content plan flow.  Cancellation is permanent. A canceled flow can't be resumed or restarted, and the keyword research linked to it is canceled with it. To generate a content plan afterwards, call Trigger Content Plan Generation Flow to start a flow.  Calling this method on a flow that's already canceled succeeds and changes nothing.

actions.name: get_content_plan_flow
actions.description: Get content plan flow. Retrieves a content plan flow.  While a flow is generating, poll this method with the `contentPlanFlowId` returned by Trigger Content Plan Generation Flow to follow the flow's progress.  Omit `contentPlanFlowId` to retrieve the site's most recent successful flow. This is useful for picking up a content plan that was generated in the site dashboard. A flow that's still running is never returned this way, and a site with no successful flow returns a not found error.

actions.name: trigger_content_plan_generation_flow
actions.description: Trigger content plan generation flow. Creates and starts a content plan flow for a site.  Generation runs asynchronously and takes several minutes. This method returns a `contentPlanFlowId` as soon as the flow is created, before any content is generated. Poll Get Content Plan Flow with that GUID to follow the flow's progress.  A successful response means the flow was created, not that generation succeeded. Check `status` rather than relying on the response alone.  Some flows advance automatically. For a flow at `KEYWORD_RESEARCH`, use Get Site Keyword Research to check its matching research. After research `SUCCESS`, re-read the flow and call Create Content Plan once only if it still wait...

actions.name: list_blog_post_candidates
actions.description: List blog post candidates. Retrieves a list of blog post candidates for a content plan flow.  Omit `contentPlanFlowId` to read the site's most recent successful flow. A site whose flows are all still running, failed, or canceled returns a not found error.  Omit `paging` to return every candidate in a single response. When `paging` is present, `limit` accepts 1 to 100 and defaults to 50.  Results are sorted by the order the content plan assigns them, then by descending keyword score. The sort isn't configurable.

includeOnlyUnmarked.description: Whether to return only candidates that haven't been used for a blog post yet.  A candidate is marked as used when a blog post is created from it in the Wix Blog product. An app can read this flag but can't set it, so track the posts you've written on your own side as well.  Default: `false`, which returns every candidate.

paging.limit.description: Max items per page. Default 50, max 100.

paging.cursor.description: Cursor from a previous response. Omit for the first page.

actions.name: create_content_plan
actions.description: Create content plan. Generates the blog post briefs for a content plan flow.  For a flow waiting at `KEYWORD_RESEARCH`, this method generates the briefs and lets the flow continue to `SUCCESS`. Some flows advance automatically: skip this call for an existing flow already at `CONTENT_PLAN` or `SUCCESS`, unless regeneration is intended.  The flow reaches `KEYWORD_RESEARCH` when keyword research starts, not when it finishes. Before releasing a waiting flow, poll Get Site Keyword Research with the flow's `keywordResearchId` until its status is `SUCCESS`. Verify the returned research and flow GUIDs, then re-read the same flow immediately before this call. It must still be at `KEYWORD_RESEARCH`...

actions.name: list_keyword_research_items
actions.description: List keyword research items. Retrieves the keyword research behind the site's current content plan.  Returns the research produced by the last completed generation. Research from a generation that's still running, or that failed, isn't readable. Poll Get Content Plan Flow until its status is `SUCCESS`, then call this method.  The result is scoped to the site rather than to a flow. This method always returns the site's most recent research and can't target an earlier one. If another generation finishes between your trigger and this read, you receive the newer research instead. Compare `keywordResearchId` across reads to detect that the research was replaced.  Omit `paging` to return every ...

contentPlanFlowId.description: Reserved for future use.  This method currently resolves the site's most recent keyword research, and this field is ignored.

paging.limit.description: Max items per page. Default 50, max 100.

paging.cursor.description: Cursor from a previous response. Omit for the first page.

actions.name: bulk_update_keyword_research_items
actions.description: Bulk update keyword research items. Updates multiple keyword research items.  This method has no field mask and writes every field present on each entry. `keyword` and `mainKeyword` remain the only writable fields, and `mainKeyword` only promotes, as it does for a single item. Repeating an item GUID within one call is rejected.  Validation runs across the whole request before anything is written, so a problem rejects the entire call rather than failing one entry. Every returned entry therefore reports success.  A keyword research holds at most 30 keywords, counted after the update. That limit is reached well before the request's own item limit.  This method copies AI-generated research th...

items.description: Keyword research items to update.  Each item GUID must appear at most once. The research holds at most 30 keywords once the update is applied.

id.description: GUID of the keyword research item to update.

keyword.description: New keyword.  Rejected if it's longer than 80 characters, or if it duplicates another keyword in the same research. Changing it also refreshes the item's `searchVolume` and `competition`.

mainKeyword.description: Whether to make this item its page's main keyword.  Set to `true` to promote it. `false` and omitting the field both leave the current main keyword unchanged, so this field can't demote one.

keywordResearchId.description: GUID of the keyword research the items belong to.  Use the `keywordResearchId` from your most recent read or write.

actions.name: update_keyword_research_item
actions.description: Update keyword research item. Updates a keyword research item.  `fieldMask` is required and must name at least one of `keyword` or `mainKeyword`. Those are the only writable fields, and an omitted or empty mask is rejected rather than treated as a request to write everything.  `mainKeyword` only promotes. Set it to `true` to make the item its page's main keyword. Setting it to `false`, or leaving it out, changes nothing, so a main keyword can't be demoted with this method.  This method updates an item that already exists. It can't add or delete a keyword.  The first write to AI-generated research copies that research instead of changing it, so the response can carry a different `keywordRe...

fieldMask.description: Fields to update.  Must name at least one of `keyword` or `mainKeyword`, the only writable fields. An omitted or empty mask is rejected.

id.description: GUID of the keyword research item to update.

keyword.description: New keyword.  Rejected if it's longer than 80 characters, or if it duplicates another keyword in the same research. Changing it also refreshes the item's `searchVolume` and `competition`.

mainKeyword.description: Whether to make this item its page's main keyword.  Set to `true` to promote it. `false` and omitting the field both leave the current main keyword unchanged, so this field can't demote one.

actions.name: bulk_generate_alt_text_suggestions
actions.description: Bulk generate alt text suggestions. Generates alt text suggestions for up to 20 images in one call.  Every image must be Wix-hosted media. `itemType` applies to all images in the call, and `parentItemId` is optional per image. Images are processed independently: the response reports per-image success, and the call succeeds as long as at least 1 image succeeded. A call where every image failed returns a `GENERATION_FAILED` error. An image URL that isn't Wix-hosted rejects the whole request.  To generate alt text for a single image, call [Generate Alt Text Suggestions](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/seo/tag-suggestions-v1/generate-alt-text-suggestions.md).

images.description: The images to generate alt text for.

id.description: Your reference GUID for the image. Echoed back in the result so you can match suggestions to images. It isn't interpreted.

url.description: URL of the image file. Must be Wix-hosted media, meaning a URL on a Wix media domain such as `static.wixstatic.com`. Other hosts are rejected.

parentItemId.description: GUID of the Wix item the image belongs to, for example, a page GUID or a store product GUID, matching the request's `itemType`. Optional but recommended: when passed, the item's stored SEO data gives the AI context about the image. Without it, alt text is generated from the image alone.

itemType.description: Type of the Wix item the images belong to, as an SEO item type identifier. All images in one call must belong to items of the same type. For example, `STATIC_PAGE_V2` for a regular site page, `STORES_PRODUCT` for a store product, or `BLOG_POST` for a blog post. For a site page, pass `STATIC_PAGE_V2`, not the `STATIC_PAGE` value the Item SEO Tags API uses. Other values are rejected.

actions.name: generate_alt_text_suggestions
actions.description: Generate alt text suggestions. Generates alt text suggestions for a single Wix-hosted image.  The image must be Wix-hosted media. Set `itemType` to the kind of Wix item the image belongs to, such as a site page or a store product. Passing the item's GUID as `image.parentItemId` is optional but recommended: that item's stored SEO data gives the AI context about what the image is for. Without it, alt text is generated from the image alone.  Returns up to 5 ready-to-use alt texts in the site's language.  To generate alt text for up to 20 images in a single call, call [Bulk Generate Alt Text Suggestions](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/seo/tag-suggestions-v1/bulk-ge...

image.description: A Wix-hosted image to generate alt text for.

id.description: Your reference GUID for the image. Echoed back in the result so you can match suggestions to images. It isn't interpreted.

url.description: URL of the image file. Must be Wix-hosted media, meaning a URL on a Wix media domain such as `static.wixstatic.com`. Other hosts are rejected.

parentItemId.description: GUID of the Wix item the image belongs to, for example, a page GUID or a store product GUID, matching the request's `itemType`. Optional but recommended: when passed, the item's stored SEO data gives the AI context about the image. Without it, alt text is generated from the image alone.

itemType.description: Type of the Wix item the image belongs to, as an SEO item type identifier. For example, `STATIC_PAGE_V2` for a regular site page, `STORES_PRODUCT` for a store product, or `BLOG_POST` for a blog post. For a site page, pass `STATIC_PAGE_V2`, not the `STATIC_PAGE` value the Item SEO Tags API uses. Other values are rejected.

actions.name: generate_description_suggestions
actions.description: Generate description suggestions. Generates SEO description tag suggestions for a page.  Returns up to 10 ready-to-use meta description texts, based on the page name, topic, page type, and the optional context fields. Suggestions aim for the 130 to 165 character range that displays fully in search results.  The optional context fields (primary keyword, tone of voice, business type, business location, and page content) are hints that may influence the generated text; they aren't guaranteed to appear in it.

businessLocation.description: Location of the business, for location-aware phrasing. Optional hint.

businessType.description: Type of business the site is for. Optional hint.

pageContent.description: Text content of the page, to ground the description in what the page actually says. Send page content only. Don't include personal data. Optional hint.

pageName.description: Name of the page, as shown in the site's menu or page list.

pageType.description: Kind of page the suggestion is for. Helps the AI phrase the suggestion for the page's purpose.

primaryKeyword.description: Primary keyword the page targets. When passed, suggestions try to feature it. Optional hint.

toneOfVoice.description: Tone of voice for the generated text, for example, `friendly` or `professional`. Optional hint.

topic.description: What the page is about, for example, the product name for a product page, or the article subject for a blog post.

actions.name: generate_heading_structure_suggestions
actions.description: Generate heading structure suggestions. Suggests corrected heading levels for a page's headings.  Pass the page's headings in document order, each with its raw HTML and your own reference GUIDs. The AI checks the heading hierarchy (one H1, no skipped levels, headings that match their content) and returns a suggested tag per heading that should change, echoing your reference GUIDs back so you can locate each element.  The heading nodes are the request's content, so this method works for any page, including headless projects.

headings.description: The page's heading elements, in the order they appear on the page.

id.description: Your reference GUID for the heading element. Required, and must be unique within the request together with `uiElementId` and `attributeId` if you send them.

attributeId.description: Additional reference GUID for the heading's text attribute, if you use one. Echoed back unchanged.

htmlString.description:
Raw HTML of the heading element, including its tag, for example, `

Our services

`. Elements that aren't headings are ignored for the structure check. Send page content only. Don't include personal data.

uiElementId.description: Additional reference GUID for the heading element, if you use one. Echoed back unchanged.

sectionId.description: Your reference GUID for the page section the heading belongs to. Helps the AI keep one heading hierarchy per section.

itemType.description: Type of the page's item, as an SEO item type identifier. For example, `STATIC_PAGE_V2` for a regular site page or `BLOG_POST` for a blog post. `STATIC_PAGE_V2` isn't the `STATIC_PAGE` value the Item SEO Tags API uses. Other values are rejected.

pageId.description: Your reference GUID for the page the headings belong to. For Wix pages, the page GUID, which lets the page's title be read to give the AI context.

actions.name: generate_title_suggestions
actions.description: Generate title suggestions. Generates SEO title tag suggestions for a page.  Returns up to 10 ready-to-use title texts for the page, based on the page name, page type, and primary keyword. Suggestions aim for the 45 to 65 character range that displays fully in search results.

pageName.description: Name of the page, as shown in the site's menu or page list.

pageType.description: Kind of page the suggestion is for. Helps the AI phrase the suggestion for the page's purpose.

primaryKeyword.description: Primary keyword the page targets. When passed, suggestions try to feature it.

actions.name: get_page_optimization_results
actions.description: Get page optimization results. Retrieves the optimization suggestions generated for a page.  Poll this method after a trigger call. The response's `status` reports where the job stands: while generation is still in progress the suggestions are empty and `status` is `IN_PROGRESS`; when it completes, the response carries the full suggestion set with `status` `COMPLETED`. A job that failed reports `FAILED`. Trigger again to retry. Suggestions are stored per page, so a later trigger for the same page replaces them, and a replaced job's lookup reports `NOT_FOUND`.  Look up by `predictionId` (from the trigger call), or by `pageId`. A `predictionId` can be looked up for 2 hours after the trigger...

pageId.description: GUID of the page to retrieve suggestions for. An alternative to `predictionId` that returns the page's latest generation.

predictionId.description: GUID of the generation job, from the trigger call. Can be looked up for 2 hours after the trigger call.

actions.name: trigger_home_page_optimization
actions.description: Trigger home page optimization. Starts generating optimization suggestions for the site's homepage.  The homepage gets its own method because its suggestions are generated with homepage-specific guidance, representing the whole site, not one topic. Same contract as Trigger Page Optimization: the homepage's focus keyword must be set first, the call returns a `predictionId` to poll, and triggering is idempotent per page while a job is in progress.  The method takes no parameters. Wix resolves which page is the site's homepage, so callers don't have to identify it. The response returns the resolved `pageId`, for later lookups with Get Page Optimization Results.

actions.name: trigger_page_optimization
actions.description: Trigger page optimization. Starts generating optimization suggestions for a static page.  Other site items, such as blog posts, store products, bookings services, and events, return a `PAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED` error.  The suggestions target the page's focus keyword, so set it first: run keyword research, set the chosen keyword as the page's focus keyword, then trigger. Returns a `predictionId` to poll Get Page Optimization Results with.  Triggering is idempotent per page: while a generation for the page is in progress, calling again returns the same `predictionId` instead of starting a new job, unless the page's focus keyword changed since the job started, which returns a `SUGGESTIONS_ALREADY_...

pageId.description: GUID of the static page to optimize. This is the item GUID the Item SEO Tags API uses for item type `STATIC_PAGE`. The page's focus keyword must be set.

pagePath.description: URL path of the page, relative to the site's domain. For example, `/about`.

actions.name: get_site_keyword_research
actions.description: Get site keyword research. Retrieves a site keyword research run, including its status.  A content plan flow reaches `KEYWORD_RESEARCH` when research starts, not when it finishes. Retrieve the flow with [Get Content Plan Flow](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/seo/content-plan-content-plan-flow-v1/get-content-plan-flow.md), then specify its actual `keywordResearchId` and check that the returned research GUID and `contentPlanFlowId` match. For research still `IN_PROGRESS`, use paced reads within a finite monitoring window. A brief not found error can occur before the research record exists; re-read the flow if it persists.  After matching research `SUCCESS`, re-rea...

keywordResearchId.description: GUID of the keyword research run to retrieve. Use the `keywordResearchId` of a content plan flow.  Omit to retrieve the site's most recent successful research.

actions.name: create_url_mapping
actions.description: Create url mapping. Creates a URL mapping for one type of item page.  A site can have one URL mapping per key. The business solution doesn't need to be installed on the site yet. The pattern applies to the item pages once it's installed.  The change is live on the site right away. On a published site, the item pages' old URLs stop working, so create redirects from them with [Bulk Create Redirects](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/seo/redirects/redirect-v1/bulk-create-redirects.md).

urlMapping.description: A custom URL pattern for one type of item page on a site, such as all Stores product pages.  A site has at most one URL mapping per `key`. When a site has no URL mapping for a key, the item pages use the key's default URL, which depends on the key. For example, Stores product pages default to `<prefix>/{{slug}}` and Blog category pages to `<prefix>/categories/{{slug}}`.

key.description: Type of item page this URL mapping applies to, and the variables its `mapping` must use: + `wix.stores.sub_pages.product`: Stores product page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.blog.sub_pages.post`: Blog post page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.blog.sub_pages.category`: Blog category page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.bookings.sub_pages.service_page`: Bookings service page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.online_programs.sub_pages.online_program`: Online Programs program page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.forum.sub_pages.category`: Forum category page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.forum.sub_pages.post`: Forum post page. Variables: `categorySlug`, `postSlug`. + `wix.groups.sub_pages.group`: Groups group page. Variables: `groupId`, `tabName`.  Other values aren't supported.

mapping.description: URL pattern for the item pages, relative to the site's base URL. Wrap variables in double curly braces, for example `shoes/{{slug}}`. The pattern must use every variable listed for its `key`, and no others. The pattern is saved in lowercase.  Rules: up to 1,000 characters; no spaces, emoji, or URL-reserved characters; no leading or trailing slash; no empty segments; at most one variable per segment. The resulting URLs can't collide with another page on the site or with another URL mapping.

actions.name: update_url_mapping
actions.description: Update url mapping. Replaces the URL mapping for one type of item page.  The site must already have a URL mapping for the key. To add one, call [Create URL Mapping](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/seo/url-mapping-v1/create-url-mapping.md).  The change is live on the site right away. On a published site, the old URLs stop working, so create redirects from them with [Bulk Create Redirects](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/seo/redirects/redirect-v1/bulk-create-redirects.md).

For example, Stores product pages default to `<prefix>/{{slug}}` and Blog category pages to `<prefix>/categories/{{slug}}`.

Variables: `slug`. + `wix.bookings.sub_pages.service_page`: Bookings service page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.online_programs.sub_pages.online_program`: Online Programs program page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.forum.sub_pages.category`: Forum category page. Variables: `slug`. + `wix.forum.sub_pages.post`: Forum post page. Variables: `categorySlug`, `postSlug`. + `wix.groups.sub_pages.group`: Groups group page. Variables: `groupId`, `tabName`.  Other values aren't supported.

mapping.description: URL pattern for the item pages, relative to the site's base URL. Wrap variables in double curly braces, for example `shoes/{{slug}}`. The pattern must use every variable listed for its `key`, and no others. The pattern is saved in lowercase.  Rules: up to 1,000 characters; no spaces, emoji, or URL-reserved characters; no leading or trailing slash; no empty segments; at most one variable per segment. The resulting URLs can't collide with another page on the site or with another URL mapping.

actions.name: delete_url_mapping
actions.description: Delete url mapping. Deletes the URL mapping for one type of item page.  The item pages go back to their default URL. The change is live on the site right away. On a published site, the old URLs stop working, so create redirects from them with [Bulk Create Redirects](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/seo/redirects/redirect-v1/bulk-create-redirects.md).

actions.name: get_url_mapping
actions.description: Get url mapping. Retrieves the URL mapping for one type of item page.  Returns an empty response, not an error, when the site has no URL mapping for the key. The item pages then use their default URL.

actions.name: build_customized_url
actions.description: Build customized url. Builds item page URLs from the site's URL mapping for a key.  Each item in `itemsData` gets one URL, in the same order. The site must have a URL mapping for the key.

itemsData.description: Items to build URLs for. Each item must include every variable the key requires.  Up to 10,000 items.

itemData.description: Variable values for the item, keyed by variable name without the curly braces. For example, `{"slug": "red-shoes"}` turns the pattern `shoes/{{slug}}` into `shoes/red-shoes`.  Values are inserted as is, without URL encoding. Send URL-safe values: a `/` in a value adds a path segment, and spaces or characters like `?` and `#` break the URL.

key.description: Type of item page to build URLs for. See `UrlMapping.key` for supported values. Other values aren't supported.

options.description: Options for building URLs.

baseUrl.description: Prefix added before each built URL, for example `https://www.my-store.com/`.  Default: no prefix. URLs are returned relative to the site's base URL and start with `/`, for example `/shoes/red-shoes`.

actions.name: list_url_mappings
actions.description: List url mappings. Retrieves all URL mappings on a site.  Returns an empty list when the site has no URL mappings.

actions.name: google_business_profile_connection_v1_disconnect
actions.description: Disconnect. Removes the site's Google Business Profile connection.  Wix deletes the stored Google credentials. This does not change anything in the customer's Google Business Profile account, and it does not revoke the grant on Google's side — the site owner can do that from their Google account settings.

actions.name: google_business_profile_connection_v1_get_connect_url
actions.description: Get connect url. Retrieves the Google authorization URL for the site owner to open.  Surface the returned URL to the site owner. After they authorize in their browser, Wix completes the OAuth exchange server-side; poll Get Connection until the status is `VALID`.  Each call starts a new authorization attempt: the returned URL is single-use and expires after 15 minutes, so request a fresh one for every attempt rather than caching or reusing one.  An already-connected site may call this too — reconnecting is a supported flow. Authorizing with the same Google account heals the connection in place, as long as its stored credentials are still there (Get Connection reports `VALID`); authorizing ...

actions.name: google_business_profile_connection_v1_get_connection
actions.description: Get connection. Retrieves the site's Google Business Profile connection status.  Returns `NEVER_CONNECTED` when no Google account has been connected. Poll this after sending the site owner to the URL from Get Connect URL.

actions.name: gbplocation_v1_create_location
actions.description: Create location. Imports an existing Google Business Profile location.  Specify the Google account GUID in `accountId` and the Google location GUID in `location.id`. Both are available from List Unimported Locations.  This doesn't create a listing in Google. It records a location the Google account already has, so that the site can manage it. To create a new listing, call Create Google Location.  A Google account must be connected first, or the call fails with `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`. See the [Connection API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/google-business-profile/connection-v1.md).

location.description: A GBP location is a site's stable record of one Google Business Profile location.  It holds the identifiers and operational metadata needed to work with that location on Google's behalf. It doesn't store the Google-owned profile data itself: name, address, opening hours, photos, reviews, attributes and insights are all retrieved live from Google on each call, so they're never stale here and never edited here.  `id` is Google's own location identifier, so you can use it to correlate a location with data you retrieve from Google directly.  The only personal data on a GBP location is `serviceAreaPostalAddress`, which is set for service-area businesses. It's often a home address, so it's stored encrypted and is covered by the site's data-deletion requests.  A Google account must be connected before locations can be imported, and before any call that reads or writes a specific location's profile. See the [Connection API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/google-business-profile/connection-v1.md).  Two methods work without a connection, because they read Google's public catalog rather than a site's own profile: Search Google Locations, and List Attribute Metadata when called with `categoryRegion`. Both are useful before a site owner has connected anything.

id.description: Google's opaque location identifier on the public API.

accountId.description: GUID of the Google Business Profile account that holds this location, what Google calls a location group.  One site can have locations in more than one account, because a single Google login can own several.

serviceAreaPostalAddress.description: Saved postal address for service-area businesses. Used as the `context` parameter in Google's FetchVerificationOptions call for service-area verification flows. Null for storefront businesses.

addressLines.description: Street address lines. Up to 5 lines.

feedEntityId.description: Identity this location is published under in Google partner feeds, used as the entity GUID, merchant GUID or parent entity GUID across Reserve with Google, Order with Google and Dine with Google.  Can be set once. A location that already has a value keeps it, and a request that tries to change it is rejected: Google has already ingested the value as the merchant's identity, so changing it withdraws the business from those feeds and can remove its booking and ordering buttons. Setting it on a location that doesn't have one yet is allowed.  Locations created through this API are given a value automatically, so you usually don't need to set it. Specify it only when migrating a location whose identity Google already knows.

actions.name: get_gbp_location
actions.description: Get gbp location. Retrieves a GBP location as it's stored for the site.  This doesn't call Google, so it's the cheapest way to check whether a location is recorded and to read its `accountId` or `serviceAreaPostalAddress`. To get the live Google profile as well, call Get Google Location.

actions.name: delete_location
actions.description: Delete location. Deletes a GBP location, leaving the Google Business Profile listing in place.  This is the recovery path, for when the listing is already gone from Google, or is unreachable, and the stored location needs cleaning up. For the usual delete, which removes the listing from Google too, call Delete Google Location.

actions.name: gbplocation_v1_update_location
actions.description: Update location. Updates a GBP location's stored fields.  This doesn't change anything on the Google Business Profile. Only fields the GBP location itself stores can be updated: `serviceAreaPostalAddress`, and `feedEntityId` if it doesn't have a value yet. Naming a Google-owned field in `fieldMask` has no effect. To change the profile in Google, call Update Google Location.  List the fields to change in `fieldMask`.

actions.name: query_gbp_locations
actions.description: Query gbp locations. Retrieves a list of up to 100 GBP locations, given the provided paging, filtering, and sorting.  Returns the site's stored locations. It doesn't call Google, so the response contains identifiers and stored metadata rather than live profile data. To retrieve the same locations with their current Google data, call Query Google Locations.  Supported properties for filtering and sorting: `id`, `googleLocationId`, `accountId`.  To learn about working with Query methods, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/articles/work-with-wix-apis/data-retrieval/about-the-wix-api-query-language.md), [Sorting and Paging](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/a...

cursorPaging.description: Cursor paging options.  Learn more about [cursor paging](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#cursor-paging).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

filter.description: Filter object.  Learn more about the [filter section](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#the-filter-section).

sort.description: Sort object.  Learn more about the [sort section](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/articles/getting-started/api-query-language.md#the-sort-section).

fieldName.description: Name of the field to sort by.

actions.name: bulk_create_locations
actions.description: Bulk create locations. Imports multiple existing Google Business Profile locations.  Specify `id` and `accountId` on every location. This doesn't create listings in Google, the same as Create Location. accountId.description: GUID of the Google Business Profile account that holds this location, what Google calls a location group.  One site can have locations in more than one account, because a single Google login can own several.
