returnEntity.description: Whether to return each created location in `results.item`. Defaults to `false`, which keeps the response small for a large batch.

actions.name: bulk_delete_locations
actions.description: Bulk delete locations. Deletes multiple GBP locations, leaving their Google Business Profile listings in place.  The bulk counterpart of Delete Location, and the same recovery path: use it to clean up stored locations whose listings are already gone from Google or unreachable. To remove the listings from Google too, call Delete Google Location once per location.  Locations are processed independently, so one that fails doesn't stop the others. Check the results per location rather than relying on the response status.

locationIds.description: IDs of the locations to delete. These are Google's location identifiers.

actions.name: complete_verification
actions.description: Complete verification. Completes a verification by submitting the PIN Google sent.  Specify the `pendingVerificationId` from Start Verification and the `pin` the site owner received by the method they chose.  Verification succeeding doesn't on its own mean the profile is live on Google. Call Get Voice Of Merchant to check that.

pendingVerificationId.description: The `pendingVerificationId` that Start Verification returned for this verification. Store it between starting and completing, which can span sessions.

pin.description: The PIN the site owner received by the method they chose.

actions.name: create_google_location
actions.description: Create google location. Creates a Business Profile listing in Google and records it for the site.  Use this to add a location the Google account doesn't have yet. To record a listing that already exists, call Create Location instead.  Specify at least one of `storefrontAddress` or `serviceArea`. If neither is set, the call fails with `INVALID_LOCATION_PAYLOAD`.  Both can be set together when `serviceArea.businessType` is `CUSTOMER_AND_BUSINESS_LOCATION`, which is how a business that has premises and also travels to customers is represented.  A Google account must be connected first. See the [Connection API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/google-business-profile...

accountId.description: GBP account id (numeric, no "accounts/" prefix). The server forms the Google resource name as "accounts/{account_id}".

location.description: The Google Business Profile data for a location.  Mostly the details that appear on the public profile, with the exception of `storeCode`, which is a free-form identifier only the site owner sees.  This is Google-owned data. It's retrieved from Google when you read it and sent to Google when you write it, so it's never cached for the site.  `storefrontAddress` and `serviceArea` aren't mutually exclusive. At least one is required when creating a location, and both can be set when `serviceArea.businessType` is `CUSTOMER_AND_BUSINESS_LOCATION`, which is how a business that both has premises and travels to customers is represented.

name.description: Google resource name, e.g. "locations/12345678901234567890". Empty on create request; populated on response.

title.description: Business name shown on the listing (Google's "title").

languageCode.description: BCP-47 language tag, e.g. "en-US". Required when creating a location and immutable afterwards. Not used by SearchGoogleLocations.

primaryCategory.description: Primary business category. Required by Google.

id.description: Google's category identifier, such as `categories/gcid:restaurant`.  The `categories/` prefix is optional when you send it. A bare `gcid:...` is accepted and prefixed for you.

profile.description: Optional. Google asks for a description for every category except lodging but doesn't enforce it, so neither does this API. Both an absent profile and one with an empty description are accepted.

description.description: Description of the location in the site owner's own words. Optional, and an empty value clears it on the listing. Google allows up to 750 characters.

storefrontAddress.description: Storefront postal address. Required for a business that serves customers at its premises, and allowed alongside `serviceArea` when that field's `businessType` is `CUSTOMER_AND_BUSINESS_LOCATION`.

addressLines.description: Street address lines. Up to 5 lines.

serviceArea.description: Service-area definition (for businesses that serve customers at the customer's location, exclusively or in addition to their storefront).

regionCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Required by Google for CUSTOMER_LOCATION_ONLY businesses; ignored otherwise.

websiteUri.description: Business website.  Clear it by masking `websiteUri` on Update Google Location and sending `null`. Sending an empty string is rejected.

storeCode.description: Merchant-defined store code (free-form identifier shown only to the merchant).

openDay.description: Day of the week when this open/close window starts.

openTime.description: Wall-clock time the business opens on `openDay`.

hours.description: Hour of day, from 0 to 24. `24` means midnight at the end of the day, and is valid only with `minutes` 0. Google's TimePeriod admits 00:00-24:00, and a close at midnight set in Google's own UI comes back as `24:00`, so a value read from Google must be accepted back unchanged on an update.

minutes.description: Minute of the hour, from 0 to 59.

closeDay.description: Day of the week when this open/close window ends.

closeTime.description: Wall-clock time the business closes on `closeDay`.

latitude.description: Latitude in degrees. Must be in [-90, 90].

longitude.description: Longitude in degrees. Must be in [-180, 180].

status.description: Current listing status.

canReopen.description: Whether the listing can be reopened (only relevant for CLOSED_PERMANENTLY).

validateOnly.description: Dry run. When true the payload is sent to Google's accounts.locations.create with its `validateOnly` query param set, so Google runs its full validation (categories, address, phone, hours, pin-drop requirements) and creates nothing.  A dry run reports failures exactly as a real create does — the same GOOGLE_LOCATION_VALIDATION_FAILED reasons, the same INVALID_LOCATION_PAYLOAD for the storefront_address / service_area combinations this service checks itself — which is the point: a caller can pre-flight a form before committing.  On success nothing is created at Google, nothing is persisted here, no GBPLocation.CREATED event is emitted, and the response's `location` is UNSET (Google returns no resource name for a validate-only call). Callers must treat an absent `location` as "validation passed", not as a failure.

actions.name: create_media
actions.description: Create media. Adds a media item to a location.  Specify `sourceUrl`, a publicly reachable URL that Google fetches the image from. The URL has to stay reachable until Google has fetched it. Returns the created item, including the media key needed to delete it.  Two things to plan for:  - Google doesn't deduplicate by URL. Calling this twice with the same `sourceUrl` creates two media items, so track what you've already added. - Google allows about 10 edits per minute per Business Profile, and that budget covers every write to the profile: adding and deleting media, but also Update Google Location and Update Location Attributes. Interleaving those with media writes brings the 429 closer, so...

category.description: Where a media item is shown on the listing. Mirrors Google's mybusiness v4 LocationAssociation.Category.

format.description: Format of a media item. Mirrors Google's mybusiness v4 MediaFormat.

sourceUrl.description: Publicly accessible URL of the media file to add. Google fetches the bytes from this URL server-side, so it must be reachable without auth.

actions.name: delete_google_location
actions.description: Delete google location. Deletes a Business Profile listing from Google and removes it from the site.  This is the usual way to delete a location. To remove a location from the site while leaving the Google listing alone, call Delete Location.  Google refuses to delete some listings through its API, including verified or claimed listings, chain-managed locations, and suspended ones. Those have to be removed by the site owner at business.google.com.  Errors: - `NOT_FOUND`: the location isn't recorded for this site. Google isn't called. - `LOCATION_NOT_DELETABLE_VIA_API`: Google won't allow the delete, for one of the reasons above. The location is left in place. Note this is checked before t...

actions.name: get_google_location
actions.description: Get google location. Retrieves a GBP location with its current Google data.  The single-location counterpart of Query Google Locations, with the same behavior: if the profile data can't be retrieved from Google, the location is still returned and the reason is in `googleError`.  If the location isn't found, the call fails and Google isn't contacted.

actions.name: delete_media
actions.description: Delete media. Deletes a media item from a location.  Specify the media key from List Media. Deleting an item that's already gone succeeds, so it's safe to retry.  Deletions draw on the same budget of about 10 edits per minute per Business Profile as every other write to it, including Create Media, Update Google Location and Update Location Attributes. A review has at most one reply, so calling this again replaces the existing text rather than adding a second one. The reply shows publicly on Google next to the review, attributed to the business.

actions.description: Start verification. Starts verifying a location with Google.  Call Get Verification Options first to find out which methods Google allows for the location, then specify one here.  For `ADDRESS`, `EMAIL`, `PHONE_CALL` and `SMS`, Google sends a PIN to the site owner. Pass it to Complete Verification to finish.  For `AUTO`, Google verifies the location itself. Mask `primaryPhone` and `additionalPhones` together, and send the complete set you want. Any additional phone you want to keep has to be resent or it's deleted. Unlike categories, no primary is required, so masking both with none set clears every phone number.  Only top-level fields are valid. A nested path such as `serviceArea.places` or `profile.description` is rejected with `INVALID_UPDATE_MASK`. Send the top-level field instead, and Google replaces that whole part of the profile.

storefrontAddress.description: Storefront postal address. Required for a business that serves customers at its premises, and allowed alongside `serviceArea` when that field's `businessType` is `CUSTOMER_AND_BUSINESS_LOCATION`.

addressLines.description: Street address lines. Up to 5 lines.

serviceArea.description: Service-area definition (for businesses that serve customers at the customer's location, exclusively or in addition to their storefront).

regionCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Required by Google for CUSTOMER_LOCATION_ONLY businesses; ignored otherwise.

websiteUri.description: Business website.  Clear it by masking `websiteUri` on Update Google Location and sending `null`. Sending an empty string is rejected.

storeCode.description: Merchant-defined store code (free-form identifier shown only to the merchant).

openDay.description: Day of the week when this open/close window starts.

openTime.description: Wall-clock time the business opens on `openDay`.

hours.description: Hour of day, from 0 to 24. `24` means midnight at the end of the day, and is valid only with `minutes` 0. Google's TimePeriod admits 00:00-24:00, and a close at midnight set in Google's own UI comes back as `24:00`, so a value read from Google must be accepted back unchanged on an update.

minutes.description: Minute of the hour, from 0 to 59.

closeDay.description: Day of the week when this open/close window ends.

closeTime.description: Wall-clock time the business closes on `closeDay`.

latitude.description: Latitude in degrees. Must be in [-90, 90].

longitude.description: Longitude in degrees. Must be in [-180, 180].

status.description: Current listing status.

canReopen.description: Whether the listing can be reopened (only relevant for CLOSED_PERMANENTLY).

actions.name: bulk_create_media_uploads
actions.description: Bulk create media uploads. Queues photo changes for one location and returns without calling Google.  Every item must target the same `locationId`, and one call has to be either all additions or all removals. Send two calls to do both.  To add a photo, set `slotKey`, `sourceUrl`, `category` and `format`. To remove one, set `slotKey` and `mediaKey`. Everything else is assigned by the server.  `sourceUrl` has to stay reachable well after this call returns, not just until it does. Google fetches the image when the queue reaches it, which may be minutes later, and a failure report renders the same URL as a thumbnail possibly weeks later.  Queuing clears the location's previous failures. Every...

mediaUploads.description: Photo changes to queue. All must share one `locationId` and one `operation`.  Per item set `locationId`, `operation`, `slotKey`, and then either `sourceUrl`, `category` and `format` to add, or `mediaKey` to remove. Every other field is assigned by the server and ignored if you send it.  Up to 52 items: 50 gallery photos plus a logo and a cover.

locationId.description: GUID of the location this change applies to. This is Google's location identifier.

slotKey.description: Your own key for this photo: `logo`, `cover`, or `photo:<id>`.  Set it to something stable and meaningful to you. It's how a failure is matched back to the photo that caused it, and it's part of what makes a repeated submission a duplicate rather than a second change.

sourceUrl.description: Publicly reachable URL Google fetches the image from. Additions only.  Keep it reachable well beyond the upload itself. A failure report renders this URL as a thumbnail, possibly weeks later.

category.description: Where the photo appears on the profile. Additions only.

format.description: Media type of the photo. Additions only.

operation.description: Whether this change adds a photo to the profile or removes one.

mediaKey.description: Google's identifier for the photo to remove. Removals only.

returnEntity.description: Whether to return each queued item in `results.item`.

actions.name: dismiss_media_upload_failures
actions.description: Dismiss media upload failures. Clears a location's failed photo changes, leaving queued ones alone.  Failures are otherwise kept until the next submission for that location replaces them, so this is how a site owner dismisses a photo that's never going to succeed.  `dismissedCount` reports how many were cleared.

actions.name: create_dns_zone
actions.description: Create dns zone. Creates a DNS zone in [Google's Cloud DNS](https://cloud.google.com/dns).   If there is an existing DNS zone for the domain, it's deleted before the new zone is created.  The call is synchronous, that means it fails in case of an error on Google's side.  You can only set up a single `record` object per DNS record type. If you want to specify multiple values for the same record type, you must save them in the `values` for the relevant type.  > __Important:__ This call requires an account level API key and cannot be authenticated with the standard authorization header.

dnsZone.description: DNS zones hold information about the records that map a domain's URL to an IP address.

domainName.description: Domain name including the TLD. Both root domains and subdomains are supported.

If you want to specify multiple values for the same record type, you must save them in the `values` for the relevant type.  Min: 2 DNS record - a DNS zone file has to have at least two required DNS records: NS and SOA records Max: 5000 DNS records

hostName.description: Host name. Can be a subdomain. For example, `domain.com` or `mail.domain.com`. Equal to the domain name, except for `CNAME` records.

values.description: DNS record values. Wix limits DNS records to 50 values per type. External providers may support a different maximum number of DNS records for a specific type, Wix doesn't validate that you don't exceed these external limits.  Max: 50 records

This means, you must delete the relevant record and add a new `addition` object for this type to the request, in case you want to add values for an existing DNS record type.  > __Important:__ This call requires an account level API key and cannot be authenticated with the standard authoriza...

To check whether the domain itself can be transferred, call [Validate Domain Transferability](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/account-level/domains/domain-transfer-in/validate-domain-transferability.md).

Checks the domain against every transfer requirement in a single call: TLD support, premium status, whether the domain is already registered with Wix, and whether a transfer is already in progress. Call this method before starting a transfer to confirm eligibility.  Validation problems are returned in `validationResult.violations`, not as errors. actions.name: get_domain_assignment
actions.description: Get domain assignment. Retrieves a domain assignment.   The domain assignment GUID is the domain name. For example, to retrieve the domain assignment of `mystunningsite.com`, specify `mystunningsite.com` as `domainAssignmentId`.  You must specify the Wix account GUID in the `wix-account-id` header.

actions.name: delete_domain_assignment
actions.description: Delete domain assignment. Unassigns a domain from a site and deletes the domain assignment.   If the domain is the site's primary domain, all of the site's domain assignments are deleted, including its redirects. To remove only the primary domain and keep the redirects, first call [Set Domain As Primary](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/account-level/domains/domain-assignments/set-domain-as-primary.md) to make a different domain the site's primary domain. Then delete the previous primary domain's assignment.  You must specify the Wix account GUID in the `wix-account-id` header.

actions.name: set_domain_as_primary
actions.description: Set domain as primary. Sets a domain as the primary domain of the site it's assigned to.   The site's previous primary domain becomes a redirect, and all of the site's redirect domains point to the new primary domain. If the domain is already the site's primary domain, the domain assignment is returned unchanged.  To assign a domain to a site, call [Upsert Domain Assignment](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/account-level/domains/domain-assignments/upsert-domain-assignment.md).  You must specify the Wix account GUID in the `wix-account-id` header.

The questionnaire is generated with AI the first time the form is opened, and the resulting `context` is stored on the intake form. This API stores the generated content but doesn't perform the generation itself.

actions.name: create_feedback_session
actions.description: Create feedback session. Creates a feedback session on a site.  The feedback session is attributed to the calling Wix user, who's notified by email about new comments left through it. Must be called with a Wix user identity: apps, including calls made with an API key, can retrieve and delete feedback sessions, but can't create them.  You can specify only `expirationDate`, which defaults to 14 days after creation. A feedback session can't be updated once created.  To get the URL to share with reviewers, set `fields` to `SHARE_URL`.  Creating a feedback session publishes the site's latest saved version for reviewers, replacing the version published for the site's previous feedback session. ...

feedbackSession.description: A feedback session is a shareable link through which anyone holding the link can review a site and leave comments on it.  A Wix user creates a feedback session on a site, shares its link with reviewers, and reads the comments left through it with the [Comments API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/account-level/studio-workspace/feedback/comment-v1/introduction.md). The user who created the session is notified by email about new comments left on it. A feedback session accepts new comments until its `expirationDate`.

expirationDate.description: Date and time after which the feedback session stops accepting new comments.  Comments already left through the session stay readable, and can still be triaged and replied to. Can be set only when creating the feedback session.  Default: 14 days after creation

The current `revision` must be passed when updating the comment. This ensures you're working with the latest comment and prevents unintended overwrites.  The site owner can delete any reply, not only their own, as part of moderating the comment.  To include the reviewer's name and email in the returned comment, specify `COMMENTER` in `fields`.  The reply is addressed by `replyIndex`, its position in the comment's `replies` list. Because indexes shift when an earlier reply is deleted, a stale `revision` is rejected rather than applied to whichever reply now sits at that index.

The reply is addressed by `replyIndex`, its position in the comment's `replies` list. actions.name: commit_git_code_store_project_upload
actions.description: Commit git code store project upload. Commits and pushes a previously uploaded ZIP's contents to an existing branch.  Replaces the complete tracked file tree. Does not publish or deploy the application. Files omitted from the ZIP are deleted. Creates one child commit and preserves history; never resets the branch history. Defaults to main. An empty ZIP intentionally removes all files. An unchanged tree creates no commit. Unless force is true, a stale expected head fails even for unchanged input. Force replaces the latest checked-out tree and preserves history; concurrent writes can still conflict. Accepts at most 64 MiB compressed, 256 MiB expanded, and 10,000 ZIP entries. Paths are limit...

commit.description: Git commit metadata supplied by the caller when creating a revision.

message.description: Commit message.

expectedHeadRevisionId.description: Full SHA from the download URL response. Required unless force is true; ignored when force is true. Prevents replacing code changed since the download. The handler requires exactly 40 hexadecimal characters when force is false; missing, empty, abbreviated, or non-hexadecimal values are rejected before reading the upload.

force.description: Replace the latest branch tree even if it changed since download. Defaults to false. Preserves history by creating a normal commit; concurrent writes can still cause a conflict.

uploadId.description: Identifier returned by GenerateGitCodeStoreProjectUploadUrl. The ZIP must have been uploaded within the last hour.

actions.name: generate_git_code_store_project_download_url
actions.description: Generate git code store project download url. Generates a temporary URL to download all tracked files at one revision as a ZIP.  Includes tracked hidden directories and binary files; excludes Git history. LFS pointer files are included verbatim; external LFS objects are not downloaded. Defaults to main. Omit `revisionId` to download the current branch head. Supply the returned revision when committing uploaded code unless force is true. Supports at most 10,000 tracked files, 256 MiB expanded, and a 64 MiB ZIP. Paths are limited to 1,024 characters, with at most 255 UTF-8 bytes per file or folder name. Rejects unsafe paths, submodules, special files, and dangling or escaping symlinks. Requ...

revisionId.description: Optional full commit SHA, reachable from the selected branch. Defaults to its head.

actions.name: generate_git_code_store_project_upload_url
actions.description: Generate git code store project upload url. Generates a temporary, project-scoped URL for uploading a ZIP with HTTP PUT.  PUT the ZIP with the returned headers, then call [Commit Git Code Store Project Upload](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/account-level/git-codestore/commit-git-code-store-project-upload.md). The 64 MiB compressed size limit is checked when committing the upload, not by the signed PUT. Uploading alone never changes the repository. ZIP paths must be relative to its root. When committing, paths are limited to 1,024 characters, with at most 255 UTF-8 bytes per file or folder name. Requires an authenticated user with update access to the app or its companion site.

actions.name: get_accessibility_scan
actions.description: Get accessibility scan. Retrieves a scan and its latest status.  Poll this method until the scan reaches a terminal state. REST callers wait for the positive `suggestedPollIntervalSeconds` value returned in the response. SDK callers poll every 5 seconds because the generated get method returns the scan entity directly. If the retained scan record expired, start a new scan.

actions.name: get_latest_accessibility_scan
actions.description: Get latest accessibility scan. Retrieves the latest stored scan for the requested target without starting a new scan. Fails if the target is invalid or has no stored scan.

target.scope.description: Multi-page scope to scan. Currently supports the complete site.

target.page.pageId.description: Wix page GUID when it uniquely identifies the page to scan. Use `pageUrl` for a generated page such as a specific product or blog post.

target.page.pageUrl.description: Absolute page URL belonging to the selected Wix site.

target.pageCollection.collectionId.description: Stable public collection GUID, for example "wix.stores.products".

target.pageCollection.targetType.description: Discriminator for the target variant. It must match the populated target field.

actions.name: list_accessibility_scan_findings
actions.description: List accessibility scan findings. Lists actionable findings for a completed or partially completed scan. Findings are cursor-paged and ordered by severity (critical, serious, moderate, minor, then info), page URL, and finding GUID. They may be filtered by page, rule, severity, or user-intent category. Results are available only for completed and partially completed scans; a failed or expired scan never returns an empty list that could be mistaken for no accessibility issues.

filter.page.pageId.description: Wix page GUID when it uniquely identifies the page to scan. Use `pageUrl` for a generated page such as a specific product or blog post.

filter.page.pageUrl.description: Absolute page URL belonging to the selected Wix site.

filter.ruleId.description: Limit findings to one stable rule GUID.

filter.categories.description: Limit findings to one or more user-intent categories. Categories are combined with OR and then combined with other filters using AND.

paging.limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

paging.cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

actions.name: list_accessibility_scan_page_collections
actions.description: List accessibility scan page collections. Lists the supported page collections currently available on the authenticated site. Use the returned collection GUID unchanged when the user asks to scan a page type such as all products, blog posts, booking services, events, or restaurant menu pages.

paging.limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

paging.cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

actions.name: list_accessibility_scan_page_summaries
actions.description: List accessibility scan page summaries. Lists per-page aggregate results for a completed or partially completed scan. The response includes every discovered page: affected pages, pages with no findings, and pages that failed to scan. A page scan returns at most one page summary. Results are available only for completed and partially completed scans; a failed or expired scan never returns an empty list that could be mistaken for a clean result. Affected pages are returned first, ordered by their highest finding severity (critical first) and then finding count. Failed and clear pages follow in stable page-URL order.

paging.limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in the results.

paging.cursor.description: Pointer to the next or previous page in the list of results.  Pass the relevant cursor token from the `pagingMetadata` object in the previous call's response. Not relevant for the first request.

actions.name: run_accessibility_scan
actions.description: Run accessibility scan. Queues an asynchronous accessibility scan.  Retrying with the same `idempotencyKey` for the same site returns the original scan. Reusing the key with a different target fails.  Fails if the target is invalid or unavailable, another scan for the same target is active, the idempotency key was reused for another target, or the supported scan size is exceeded. Multi-page targets are never silently sampled or truncated. Run requests are limited to 5 per minute per Wix site and can return HTTP 429. Retry the same intended scan with the same idempotency key.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-generated UUGUID used to safely retry this request. Generate a new key for every intended scan and reuse it only when retrying that same request.

target.description: Selects exactly one scan target on the authenticated Wix site: the full site, one page, or every page in a supported Wix page collection.

scope.description: Multi-page scope to scan. Currently supports the complete site.

pageId.description: Wix page GUID when it uniquely identifies the page to scan. Use `pageUrl` for a generated page such as a specific product or blog post.

pageUrl.description: Absolute page URL belonging to the selected Wix site.

pageCollection.description: Every page in one supported Wix page collection.

collectionId.description: Stable public collection GUID, for example "wix.stores.products".

targetType.description: Discriminator for the target variant. It must match the populated target field.
